title: Tua Tagovailoa's return to Pittsburgh puts extra pressure on Mike McCarthy's debut
summary: The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins.
full_text: '' The last time quarterback Tua Tagovailoa started a game in Pittsburgh, it became his last start with the Miami Dolphins. He was benched after the 28-15 loss on a Monday night in December — and he was cut in March. Fast forward to September, and Tua will be returning to Pittsburgh as the Week 1 starter for the Falcons. If it goes poorly, Tua may not be starting for very long. If it goes well, and if the Falcons upset the Steelers (Pittsburgh is currently favored by 3.5 points), there will be a very strong reaction in Western Pennsylvania. Losing to Tua after drubbing him less than nine months earlier will provide the first clear apples-to-apples comparison between new coach Mike McCarthy and his predecessor, Mike Tomlin. Nuances will easily be lost on Steelers Nation. Yes, the Falcons are an overall better team than the 2025 Dolphins. The common denominator is the quarterback; if he plays dramatically better than he did the last time he played in Pittsburgh, Steelers fans will interpret that as an indication that the new boss won't have the same kind of success as the old boss. It would be dubbed an overreaction. But that's what football fans do. With only seventeen games in a season, they all count. They all spark a reaction. And, at some point, the trend of overreacting shows that, actually, it's the normal and usual reaction to a team losing a game it should have won. The Steelers have more than a few winnable games in the eight weeks before the bye, including two against the Browns. Anything less than 5-3 will spark high anxiety on and after Week 10, where the Eagles, Broncos, Texans, Jaguars, a road game at the Bengals, and two games against the Ravens are lurking. The fans who show up in six days will be expecting a 1-0 start. If the end result is 0-1, sphincters will be tightening quickly in the Steel City.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike McCarthy hopeful that Joey Porter will play Week 1
summary: The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts.
full_text: The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts. Thus, time is running out for the team to complete a long-term deal with cornerback Joey Porter. " It’s a business , and there's definitely business conversations going on," head coach McCarthy said Monday, via Jack Markowski of SI.com. McCarthy insinuated that he expects Porter to play regardless how talks turn out before Sunday's season opener against the Falcons. "Yeah, I hope so," McCarthy said. "You know, just keep working him. He's still, I'd put him in a ramp-up mode." When asked what happens if Porter doesn't play, McCarthy said, “We’ll see what happens.” Porter practiced for the first time last Tuesday after spending all of training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list. But last week he was noncommittal about playing Week 1 absent a contract extension. Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, is entering the final year of his rookie contract scheduled to make $3.924 million this year. He is coming off a career year, totaling a career-high 14 passes defensed to go along with 52 tackles, one sack and one interception.
author: Charean Williams

author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Donald mum on plans for season opener
summary: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan expects to see Aaron Donald on Thursday night, but like Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula earlier Monday, the defensive tackle declined to reveal his plans for the game in Australia.
full_text: ' 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan expects to see Aaron Donald on Thursday night, but like Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula earlier Monday , the defensive tackle declined to reveal his plans for the game in Australia. The Rams are scheduled to leave for Melbourne on Tuesday night, and Donald wouldn't even commit to being on the flight. “Taking it day by day. Come up with a game plan to see what's going on," Donald said, via video from Nick Hamilton of NBCLA. " Feeling good , feeling really good. Come up with a game plan and see. "Honestly, man, I really do feel good. Things are clicking faster than I thought it would be. Even my first day out there, with 11-on-11, things would be a little all over the place. Settled in. A couple of plays a little rusty. It ain't where I want it to be, but it's pretty damn good if you ask me. To not play football in two years, to be moving how I'm moving, it's really no dropoff. It's not where I want to be. I can see it. I know there are things I want to clean up, that I'm going to clean up. The more reps I do, the more I play, it'll get there.” Donald has started 11-on-11 drills in practice, but Monday was a planned recovery day. He worked on his cardio and did weight work instead. "I'm 35," Donald said. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year has not played in the NFL since 2023.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots agree to four-year extension
summary: Gonzalez has agreed to a deal that will make him the league's highest-paid corner, ending a contract dispute.
full_text: The two sides cut it close, but in the end, they've gotten it done. According to multiple reports, the Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez have agreed to a four-year contract extension. The deal is reportedly worth $135 million with $102 million guaranteed, which makes Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in league history. Gonzalez, the No. 17 overall pick of the 2023 draft, had been seeking a new deal throughout the offseason. There was some question as to whether or not Gonzalez would play in New England’s season opener against Seattle on Wednesday night. Now that the contract is settled, Gonzalez has every reason to be on the field. Gonzalez, 24, was a second-team AP All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler in 2025. He had 10 passes defensed in 14 regular-season games last year. He also had seven passes defensed, a forced fumble, and an interception in New England’s four 2025 postseason games. New England and Seattle will kick off the 2026 season on Wednesday night at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori remains limited, S Ty Okada DNP again on Monday
summary: Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice.
full_text: Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice. That doesn't bode well for his availability for Wednesday's season opener against the Patriots. Emmanwori did not take participate in any of the team’s open practices during camp, according to Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times . Emmanwori is working his way back from arthroscopic surgery in July to repair his right ankle, which he initially injured in the 2025 season opener and then aggravated in a practice before Super Bowl LX. Starting safety Ty Okada's status for Week 1 also is in question as he missed a second consecutive day. The team's other starting safety, Julian Neal, was a full participant a second consecutive day with a quad injury. D’Anthony Bell, who re-signed to the practice squad on Saturday, started two games in Emmanwori’s third safety role a year ago when Emmanwori was out with an ankle injury. The Seahawks had only one change to their practice report from Sunday, with offensive guard Anthony Bradford (knee) upgraded to full participation. Bradford was limited on Sunday. Wide receiver Tory Horton (hamstring) and offensive tackle Josh Jones (knee) again were limited. Tight end A.J. Barner (oblique) and running back Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) remained full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brian Schottenheimer: We have "great confidence" in T.J. Bass replacing Tyler Smith
summary: The Cowboys showed how much they valued T.J.
full_text: The Cowboys showed how much they valued T.J. Bass as a reserve offensive lineman by using a second-round restricted free agent tender to hold onto him this offseason and Bass will get an immediate chance to show the wisdom of that decision. Bass will step in as the team's left guard while Tyler Smith is out of action due to thumb surgery . Smith is expected to miss 4-6 weeks as a result of the procedure and head coach Brian Schottenheimer said on Monday that the team is not expecting a major drop in play with Bass in the lineup. "Tyler Smith's a great player, but we feel really confident in T.J., and he's put great film on here," Schottenheimer said, via the team's website. "He's played next to Cooper Beebe, he's played next to [Tyler] Guyton, so that's nothing new, the communication and all that stuff. . . . We tendered him the way we tendered him because we trust this guy as a football player. He's a damn good football player that unfortunately is just playing behind a lot of really, really good players. So we have great confidence in T.J." Bass has started 10 games over the last three seasons and he'll have a chance to show he's ready for a full-time role in the starting lineup for Dallas or someone else in the coming weeks.
author: Josh Alper

title: C.J. Stroud: Pressure is a privilege
summary: The Texans have gone to the playoffs in each of quarterback C.J.
full_text: The Texans have gone to the playoffs in each of quarterback C.J. Stroud's three NFL seasons and they've won a game in each of those trips, but that hasn't cemented Stroud as the franchise quarterback in Houston. Stroud has not been able to match his rookie production in either of the last two seasons and he threw five interceptions in last year's postseason. which helped keep a contract extension out of reach this offseason. The team doesn’t plan on talking about one once the season starts and that leaves Stroud in position to make his case for the kind of deal that would remove any doubt about his place in the team's future. That cloud overhead could impact some players in a negative way, but Stroud said he's embracing the position he's in as the 2026 season gets underway. "Pressure is a privilege ," Stroud said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. "I'm excited. I've always been challenged in my career. I've always had to persevere through things, and I think this is something that I'm grateful for. I didn't wake up and forget how to play football." The Texans are expected to have one of the best defenses in the league and that should impact how much the Texans ask Stroud to do on a weekly basis. If he can handle that charge while the Texans make another run to the playoffs, it is hard to imagine a deal won't come together in Houston and Stroud can begin making his case against the Ravens this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: JC Latham gives opponents a warning about what the Titans' offensive line won't allow
summary: Titans offensive tackle JC Latham wants opposing teams to know they're not going to get away with any cheap shots on quarterback Cam Ward.
full_text: Titans offensive tackle JC Latham wants opposing teams to know they're not going to get away with any cheap shots on quarterback Cam Ward. Latham said a big part of the offensive line coming together this offseason has been agreeing that they need to play with more fight, which will include going after any opponent who goes after Ward. "Culture is what you stand for and what you allow," Latham said. "This offseason we all did a moment of self-reflecting of, we want to be the offensive line that we know we can be. We can't be no pushovers, we can't be nobody's bitch, just being completely honest. So all the late hits, all the extra stuff that defenses do, if we want to be what we know we can be, we can't stand for that." Latham said the Titans' new coaching staff has told the offensive linemen that they all have to have their teammates' backs. "If any of us gets into it, we're all getting into it. We're all stepping up," he said. "You just can't go for no bullshit."
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFL fines Cam Taylor-Britt and four other players for preseason Week 3 infractions
summary: The NFL fines players for illegal hits during the preseason, but for the third and final week of the preseason, those fines were fairly limited.
full_text: The NFL fines players for illegal hits during the preseason, but for the third and final week of the preseason, those fines were fairly limited. The biggest fine went to Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt, who was fined $7,791 for unnecessary roughness. Ordinarily that money would be taken out of a player's Week 1 game check, but Taylor-Britt is already suspended without pay for Week 1 for a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, so his fine will come out of his Week 2 check. Four other players were fined for preseason Week 3: Buffalo's Jalon Kilgore $5,560 for illegal use of the helmet, Minnesota's Jermar Jefferson $5,583 for facemasking, New Orleans' Danny Stutsman $7,011 for illegal use of the helmet, and Pittsburgh's Doneiko Slaughter $4,917 for taunting. Only five fines for a week is unusually low in the NFL: In preseason Week 1, nine players were fined, and in preseason Week 2, 16 players were fined. It's likely that the NFL decided not to bother fining some players who were cut after the preseason finale, as those players won't be getting Week 1 game checks anyway. The five players who were fined all remain under contract and have paychecks the NFL can dock. The NFL and NFL Players Association collectively bargained the fine process. The NFL’s officiating department reviews plays and refers potential fines to the football operations staff, which then examines the plays in question to determine whether a fine is in order. Players who get fined are sent a letter informing them of the fine and a video of the play in question. Players who don’t appeal have the money withheld from their next game check. Players who do appeal get a hearing with an appeals officer who is jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association. This season, the appeals officers are Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson and James Thrash. The appeals officer has final say on whether or not the player gets fined. Fine money is donated to the Professional Athletes Foundation, which supports former players in need, and the NFL Foundation, which supports health and safety initiatives in football from youth leagues to the professional level.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Seahawks pick different captains for each game, including Sam Darnold for Week 1
summary: When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains.
full_text: When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains. But that won't be the case every week. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald believes in picking new captains for each game, rather than the season-long captains with a 'C' on their jersey that most teams use. That was Macdonald's approach during his first two seasons as the Seahawks' head coach, and it will continue to be his approach this year. In addition to Darnold, the Seahawks' captains against the Patriots will be linebacker Ernest Jones IV, fullback Brady Russell and defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Macdonald said early in the 2024 season, his first as a head coach, that he believes in making team captain a weekly recognition rather than a season-long responsibility. “It’s a combination of guys who are doing a great job, guys who are trying to build up and give an opportunity to have a voice with the rest of the team, guys you want to recognize that deserve an opportunity to do those things," Macdonald said. "So, that’s really the thought behind it. It’s pretty much that simple. The guys know who the leaders are . You don’t need the title to be the leader of the team. But it’s important to build everybody else up. . . . There’s nothing formal about it. It’s just more of a recognition type thing. Just, ‘Hey, shout out to these guys that are operating the right way, playing the right way, preparing the right way.’" As the starting quarterback, Darnold was an obvious choice for Week 1. He'll be a team leader all year, and doesn't need the captain's 'C' to show it.
author: Michael David Smith

title: George Kittle "in good shape" to play season opener
summary: Tight end George Kittle traveled with the 49ers to Australia, which was a sign he would play in Thursday night's season opener.
full_text: '' Tight end George Kittle traveled with the 49ers to Australia, which was a sign he would play in Thursday night's season opener. It sounds like Kittle will play, but how much remains to be seen. "It's been pretty cool to see Kittle out there looking like himself , looking fresh," offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "How that affects him on game day and what the workload is, that will be determined. But he looks good to me. "He's practicing full speed. He's getting a ton of reps. So I feel like we're in good shape." Kittle tore his right Achilles in a Jan. 11 playoff game against the Eagles. He underwent surgery three days later, with Rams team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache repairing Kittle's Achilles. Kittle made his seventh career Pro Bowl last season despite playing only 11 regular-season games due to hamstring and ankle injuries. He recorded 57 receptions for 628 yards and seven touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Raheem Morris confirms Nick Bosa will play season opener
summary: The 49ers defensive end tore his ACL in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26.
full_text: '' 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa might need some time to get back to 100 percent, but he will play in the season opener. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris confirmed that Bosa's surgically repaired right knee is good enough to get him on the field against the Rams. "Oh, he's going out there. Whatever you want to say, he's going. He'll be there. We're not hiding that," Morris said, via Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle . Bosa, 28, said last week he thought he would be ready to go for Week 1, and he made the trip to Australia. He tore his ACL in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis in his right knee, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice. Bosa has not had a double-digit sack season since 2023, which is the last time he played all 17 games. He has played only 17 games over the past two seasons, totaling 11 sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Three teams have reached out to Darius Slayton
summary: The Giants released wide receiver Darius Slayton on Monday, making him a free agent.
full_text: '' The Giants released wide receiver Darius Slayton on Monday, making him a free agent. Slayton said in a social media post that he is " excited to see what’s next ." Josina Anderson of Exhibit News Network reports that three teams already have reached out to Slayton's representation for preliminary discussions. Anderson also mentioned the Colts as a potential destination, given Slayton's relationship with quarterback Daniel Jones. Slayton spent seven seasons in New York, the longest tenured Giants player before his release. He was a fifth-round pick of the Giants in 2019, four rounds after the team drafted Jones. Slayton and Jones played together six seasons. Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards and one touchdown last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Derrick Henry: I am tired of watching the Super Bowl on TV
summary: Derrick Henry has played in one AFC Championship Game, a 35-24 loss to the Chiefs in the 2019 season.
full_text: Derrick Henry has played in one AFC Championship Game, a 35-24 loss to the Chiefs in the 2019 season. After parting ways with the Titans, Henry signed with the Ravens because he believed he could win a title with Lamar Jackson at quarterback. In Henry's two seasons in Baltimore, though, the Ravens have one playoff berth and one playoff win. He still believes. "It would be crazy for me to say I played with Lamar Jackson, and we didn’t win no championships ," Henry said on "The Lounge" podcast, via Ryan Mink of the team website. "I cannot have that. I do not want that to be a thing. We've got to do it." The Ravens lost to the Bills 27-25 in the divisional round in the 2024 playoffs and failed to make the postseason in 2025. The team fired coach John Harbaugh and hired Jesse Minter, and the Ravens revamped their defense in the offseason. Henry said he "believes that we have all the pieces to get it done." In nine postseason games, Henry has 211 touches for 1,090 yards and seven touchdowns. It hasn't been enough. Jackson is 3-5 in his postseason career, with one trip to the AFC Championship Game. "I want to win a Super Bowl. That's a big motivation," Henry said. "I just want to be able to feel that feeling. I'm tired of watching. Every year, I'm tired of being at home on the couch watching. I want to be a part of it. That's what's motivating me right now. I'm going to keep going until we get to that point. We have the 2026 season to get that accomplished."
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett among Cardinals' team captains
summary: Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season.
full_text: '' Jacoby Brissett who is in his first season as a starter for the Cardinals, was named one of five captains for the team this season. On Monday, the Cardinals announced results of the players' captainship vote from Thursday. Center Hjalte Froholdt was the other offensive captain. Safety Budda Baker and linebacker Mack Wilson Sr. were the defensive captains. Long snapper Casey Kreiter will represent the special teams. "Whether you are a captain or not a captain, you be who you are within your own personality," coach Mike LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website. "When you do get voted a captain, that says your teammates and the locker room looks up to you. "I can't think of five better people to look up to, in terms of guys who will keep it real with each other, hold people to standards, communicate with me. I don't need to know everything that's going on in the locker room. I just need to know what's pertinent." It is the fifth consecutive season for Baker to serve as a captain. Froholdt and Wilson are repeat picks, after becoming captains for the first time in their careers last year. "There were quite a few guys who I won't mention who were right up there in the running for it," LaFleur said. "These guys are still going to have a voice, too. And some of it will be through the silent tape, if that makes sense. That's as important as anything, actually what you're doing [on the field]."
author: Charean Williams

title: Darius Slayton: Grateful for time with Giants, excited to see what's next
summary: Wide receiver Darius Slayton's long run with the Giants came to an end on Monday.
full_text: Wide receiver Darius Slayton's long run with the Giants came to an end on Monday. The Giants released Slayton less than a week before the start of the regular season and just over a week after there were rumors that he could be let go ahead of the cut to 53 players, so the move didn't come out of left field even though he was guaranteed $9.75 million this season. Having that money in the bank likely made it easier for Slayton to hear the news on Monday and his first response to it was filled with gratitude to the only NFL team he's played for. "Grateful for my time in NY. 7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next," Slayton wrote on X.com. The guaranteed money means that Slayton's next stop will likely be for a minimum salary and that should expand the pool of potential suitors for a player who led the Giants in receiving yards in four of his first five seasons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Titans LB Cedric Gray injured in off-road vehicle accident
summary: Titans linebacker Cedric Gray has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after being injured in an off-field accident over the weekend.
full_text: Titans linebacker Cedric Gray has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after being injured in an off-field accident over the weekend. Gray was involved in a utility terrain vehicle accident over the weekend. A UTV, or utility task vehicle, is a rugged, off-road vehicle designed to carry passengers and haul heavy loads over rough terrain. "Over the weekend, Cedric Gray was involved in a UTV accident in Tennessee and sustained a concussion and minor injuries," the Titans said in a statement. "We look forward to Cedric returning to the field soon and in full health when he clears the NFL's concussion protocol." Gray started 16 games in 2026, and he ranked fifth in the NFL with a career-high 160 tackles. A fourth-round pick in 2024, he played seven games with no starts as a rookie.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams DC Chris Shula: Everything's day by day with Aaron Donald
summary: The Rams are moving closer to their trip to Australia for their season opener against the 49ers and it remains unclear if defensive tackle Aaron Donald is going to be on the field.
full_text: '' The Rams are moving closer to their trip to Australia for their season opener against the 49ers and it remains unclear if defensive tackle Aaron Donald is going to be on the field. Donald has been practicing with the team, but, per multiple reporters, defensive coordinator Chris Shula declined to say at a Monday press conference whether he's working in 11-on-11 drills at this point. Shula did say that the team is preparing for all possible scenarios as they put together their game plan for Thursday's game. "Everything’s day by day ," Shula said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times . "We’re ready for him if he does, ready for him if he doesn’t, and we’ll have a plan for however many plays he feels like he can go and we’ll go from there." The 49ers expect to see Donald on the field in Melbourne and we'll find out in the next couple of days if that prediction is correct.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike LaFleur says he feels "good" about Jeremiyah Love's chances for Week 1
summary: Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders.
full_text: '' Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders. It was diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain, and he has not practiced or played since. Love is moving closer to a return, though, and coach Mike LaFleur insinuated that the rookie did something on the practice field Monday. "Progressing," LaFleur said, via Bo Brack of PHNX Cardinals. "He was out there moving around today. We'll see on Wednesday. I'll have a better idea for all those guys [who are injured]." The Cardinals will have their first injury report of the season on Wednesday, which will be the first indication of where Love is in his rehab. LaFleur was asked about his optimism for the third overall pick to play against the Chargers. "Yeah, I feel good ," LaFleur said. Love had 14 touches for 73 yards in the first half of the only preseason game he played.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bill Belichick, to no surprise, has little to say about expanding UNC investigation
summary: Despite the team's 1-0 record, a storm has been blowing through the North Carolina football program, with most of it playing out privately.
full_text: Despite the team's 1-0 record, a storm has been blowing through the North Carolina football program, with most of it playing out privately. The situation became much more public last Thursday, with the abrupt resignation of G.M. Mike Lombardi followed by a report from WRAL indicating that the investigation that started with Lombardi has expanded to include defensive coordinator Steve Belichick and others. Head coach Bill Belichick met with reporters on Monday, for the first time since the situation hit the fan. To no surprise, Belichick didn't have much to say in response to multiple questions about Lombardi, Steve Belichick, and the overall program. The questions were posed despite an opening comment from a team spokesperson before Belichick took the podium, via WRAL: “Coach Belichick, student athletes, and other university employees will not discuss the situation in any manner . That is necessary to protect the integrity of the process and the rights of everyone involved.” In his own introductory remarks, Bill Belichick mentioned “the importance of the work that's being done by the investigative team and, obviously, our high standard here of our code of conduct and doing things the right way and making sure that our student-athletes are given the utmost, the best treatment, the very best care, and the very best coaching that we can possibly give them." He was then peppered with inquiries about the investigation, despite the effort to avoid talking about it. The mere existence of an investigation that is exploring the behavior of multiple football employees shows that there's at least a question about whether the "high standard here of our code of conduct" has been met — including the question of whether the head coach knew about any of the potential irregularities and failed to report them. Bill Belichick's potential failure to report issues of which he was aware becomes a potential recipe for a termination " for cause ," which would cut off his buyout. Frankly, the entire situation feels like an effort to find something that would give UNC an escape hatch from a hiring it already regrets, the upset win over TCU notwithstanding. And it creates an overriding vibe that his departure is inevitable. Possibly with no further financial obligation from the school to its second-year head coach.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants cut Darius Slayton
summary: The veteran wide receiver, who signed a three-year, $36 million contract last season, is out.
full_text: Darius Slayton recently said he didn’t pay attention to rumors that he was at risk of getting cut. Apparently he should have. The Giants announced today that they are releasing Slayton. The move comes as a surprise if only because of Slayton's contract: Just last year, he signed a three-year, $36 million contract, and he is guaranteed $9.75 million this year. Cutting him only saves the Giants $2.5 million, but apparently they're down enough on him that they thought that savings was worth sending him packing. The Giants presumably tried to trade Slayton before cutting him and found that no one wanted to trade for that contract. Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards and one touchdown last season, and he's still good enough that some team will surely pick him up. Just not at anything close to what the Giants were paying him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins return to Bengals practice
summary: The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1.
full_text: The Bengals didn't show concern about wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins missing Week 1 when they missed practice last week and the outlook continues to be good as they move closer to Week 1. Chase and Higgins returned to practice on Monday. Chase hyperextended his knee in a practice and Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion. Defensive end Shemar Stewart also practiced after returning to the field from a knee injury last week and head coach Zac Taylor made it sound like all three are on track to play. "All three looked good today," Taylor said at his press conference. "We'll wait to release injury reports on Wednesday, but I was encouraged by the progress all three of those guys have made." The Bengals would like to get off to a fast start this season and having all three players on the field against the Bucs would be a good step in that direction.
author: Josh Alper

title: Newcomer Zaire Franklin named a Packers captain, along with four repeat captains from 2025
summary: It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader.
full_text: It didn't take long for new Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin to establish himself as a team leader. Franklin, who arrived in Green Bay via a trade in March, has been named one of the Packers' captains. That's not a surprise, as Franklin was a team captain on the Colts in each of the last six seasons. Some players exude leadership, and Franklin is one of them. The Packers named five captains, Franklin and four players who were also Packers captains last year: quarterback Jordan Love, tight end Tucker Kraft, safety Xavier McKinney and special teamer Isaiah McDuffie. Three players who were Packers team captains last year are not captains this year: Rashan Gary and Quay Walker, who are no longer in Green Bay, and Josh Jacobs, who is currently on the commissioner's exempt list amid an investigation into an accusation of violence against a woman.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Christian Barmore returns to Patriots practice, TreVeyon Henderson remains out
summary: The Patriots listed three players as out of practice on Sunday and they got one of them back on the field Monday.
full_text: The Patriots listed three players as out of practice on Sunday and they got one of them back on the field Monday. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore was listed as a full participant. He did not practice on Sunday because of a knee injury and his return to the field bodes well for his chances of playing against the Seahawks on Wednesday night. Running back TreVeyon Henderson's chances of playing don't look as good. Henderson missed another practice with his ankle injury and has not been on the field in a couple of weeks. Offensive lineman Ben Brown was the third player out on Sunday and the Patriots announced he will miss the game with a knee injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions sign LB Joe Bachie to active roster
summary: The Lions have filled one of the openings on their active roster.
full_text: The Lions have filled one of the openings on their active roster. They announced that they have signed linebacker Joe Bachie off of their practice squad. Bachie spent the offseason and preseason with the team and signed to the practice squad after failing to make the initial 53-man roster in Detroit. Bachie opened last season with the Colts and started five games before landing on injured reserve. He moved on to the Titans after being released and played in 10 more games on special teams. He finished the year with 29 tackles and had 48 tackles in 51 games for the Bengals and Eagles earlier in his career. The Lions still have one open spot on the 53-man roster after waiving center Seth McLaughlin and running back Jabari Small last week. They announced that both those players have been signed to the practice squad on Monday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bryce Underwood is Michigan's QB "right now," but his job security isn't "infinite"
summary: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood saved the Wolverines' bacon with a Hail Mary mulligan.
full_text: '' Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood saved the Wolverines' bacon with a Hail Mary mulligan. Underwood eventually may not be able to save his starting job. “ He’s our QB right now ,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham told reporters on Monday, via Nick Kosko of On3.com. “And it’s not something that’s infinite. At some point, we’ve got to turn a corner and we’ve got to see improvement, as we do with a lot of stuff; you’ve got to see improvement out of the coaches, so it’s not just on Bryce. And it’s not just Bryce’s job that is not absolutely set in concrete. You’ve got to perform week in and week out and become somebody that is playing at a level we can win with.” The program has made a significant financial commitment to Underwood, at $3 million per year. It's one of the realities of paying players; you need to pay the right ones. Again, Underwood still has the job. Saturday night's performance against a MAC school was troubling, even with the late-game heroics. Underwood completed 12 of 22 passes for 170 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. He added 47 yards rushing and a touchdown, on nine attempts. He'll need to perform at a higher level against better competition. The next test happens on Saturday, when Oklahoma comes to town.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steelers won't have full-season captains under Mike McCarthy
summary: It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains.
full_text: It's currently team captain season, with plenty of NFL franchises unveiling plenty of season-long captains. In Pittsburgh, however, there won't be a tweet with anywhere from five to 11 players listed as those who will be wearing a "C" in 2026. New coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Monday that he won’t use full-season captains . Instead, he'll name captains for each week’s game . That's how McCarthy handled the captain designations while serving as the head coach of the Packers and the Cowboys. The approach is a clear departure from past practices under Mike Tomlin, and another clear sign that some things will be very different with one Mike yielding to another. Last year, the Steelers had four permanent captains: quarterback Aaron Rodgers, defensive lineman Cameron Heyward, linebacker T.J. Watt, and safety Miles Killebrew. (After Killebrew was lost for the season due to injury, linebacker Payton Wilson replaced Killebrew as the special-teams captain.)
author: Mike Florio

title: Alec Pierce is expected to play for the Colts in Week 1
summary: Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce has been back at practice for a little over a week, but that's been enough time for the team to see what they needed from the wideout.
full_text: Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce has been back at practice for a little over a week, but that's been enough time for the team to see what they needed from the wideout. Pierce had ankle surgery this offseason and set playing in Week 1 as his goal throughout his recovery process. The finish line is days away and it appears Pierce is going to make it. At a Monday press conference, head coach Shane Steichen said, via multiple reporters, that Pierce "should be good to go" against the Ravens. Keenan Allen is also expected to play after being arrested in the hours after the team's final preseason game and tight end Tyler Warren has returned from a groin injury, so the Colts are set to have their full receiving corps available for Daniel Jones's first game since tearing his Achilles last season.

title: 2026 NFL season primer: Rule changes, notable games and more things to know entering Week 1
summary: Familiarize yourself with all the offseason changes ahead of kickoff
full_text:
Congratulations on making it through the NFL offseason! As the league embarks on a new campaign on Wednesday it is time to make sure everyone is up to speed on all the changes that unfolded over the last seven months.
In some ways, it is hard to believe it has been that long since the Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots and hoisted the Vince Lombardi Trophy. The NFL is such a year-round operation that it dominated headlines even in its quietest months.
There are a few new rules to learn before the Seahawks and Patriots return to the field in the first game of the 2026 season. There are also some schedule quirks unique to the upcoming campaign that everyone needs to be familiar with ahead of time. This year also brings a large batch of fresh uniforms and the opening of the doors to a new stadium.
Here are all of the changes to know ahead of the 2026 season.
Of the five playing rules changes the NFL approved at the Annual League Meeting in March, only four will actually apply to the 2026 season. The fifth would have permitted the league office to correct clear officiating mistakes in the event of an NFL Referees Association work stoppage, but a new collective bargaining agreement prevented the need for replacement officials in the first place. The following rule changes will, however, be active.
Additionally, during the final week of the preseason, the NFL and NFL Players Association voted to implement a new suspension rule for certain penalties . Any player who commits three offenses of any of the following penalties will receive a one-game suspension.
All players begin the 2026 season with a clean slate, but violations will carry forward into subsequent seasons. If a player commits just one violation, they will receive 50% of their fine back at the end of the campaign.
Half of the regular season's 18 weeks will feature an international game as the NFL expands its footprint outside the United States. For the first time, there will be nine games on foreign soil, the first of which comes right out of the gate as the second contest of the season. This year marks the inaugural Australia game, the third game in Brazil (and first in Rio de Janeiro) and the debut France game.
Here is the full international schedule:
Teams had better get used to this kind of travel, because the international slate is only going to get larger. The record of nine games abroad in one season will only stand for one year since the NFL is set to stage 10 such contests in 2027 .
Until 2026, only once in modern NFL history has the season started on a Wednesday. The NFL moved its standard Thursday opener up one day in 2012 to avoid a television ratings hit since former President Barack Obama was scheduled to speak at the Democratic National Convention on what would have otherwise been the first game day of the year.
It took 14 years for the league to schedule a second Week 1 Wednesday game. And this one is a doozy. It is a rematch of the 2026 Super Bowl which sends the New England Patriots all the way to the Pacific Northwest for a date with the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks.
Why the midweek kickoff? It all comes back to the Australia game. The league scheduled the Rams vs. 49ers showdown for Thursday, seemingly in an effort to give both teams time to adjust back to the Pacific Time Zone upon their return from a grueling trip Down Under. But the NFL also wanted to preserve its tradition of the defending Super Bowl champion being the first team to take the field. Thus, the Seahawks hit the turf one day prior to the international game.
Every game this year will be available to stream. Viewers will need just about every major streaming service to do so, though. That includes Netflix, which secured three additional games to its inventory as part of a renewed media rights contract it signed in May. The Christmas Day game now becomes a doubleheader, and Netflix will also carry the league's first Thanksgiving Eve game.
These games will be available only on Netflix as part of the streamer's expanded package:
More major broadcast changes come as part of ESPN's acquisition of NFL Network. The biggest development in this regard is the discontinuation of "Monday Night Football" doubleheaders. ESPN returned that inventory to the NFL, which then redistributed games to other partners.
In turn, there are four games on CBS, Fox and NBC that fall in non-traditional windows:
Some of football's best players will suit up for new teams in 2026, including reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett , whose trade to the Rams shocked the NFL and solidified Los Angeles as the Super Bowl front-runner. He is one of the numerous familiar faces in new places this year.
Kirk Cousins ( Raiders ), Kyler Murray (Vikings), Malik Willis ( Dolphins ), Geno Smith ( Jets ) and Tua Tagovailoa (Falcons) are the quarterbacks who will start for new teams.
A bevy of blockbuster trades sent stars to fresh destinations. In addition to the Garrett deal, the Rams also traded for cornerback Trent McDuffie . The Bengals acquired defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence . A quartet of standout receivers have new homes with A.J. Brown heading to the Patriots, DJ Moore being scooped up by the Bills, Jaylen Waddle landing with the Broncos and Michael Pittman finding himself on the Steelers.
In free agency, the Bengals loaded up on defense with Boye Mafe , Jonathan Allen and Bryan Cook bolstering a unit that needs to improve significantly in 2026. Star edge rusher Trey Hendrickson signed with the Ravens after they nixed their trade for Maxx Crosby . And reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III departed Seattle to become the leader of the Chiefs ' run game.
That is in addition to the 10 head coaching changes, which tied the league record for a single offseason:
The new Highmark Stadium opens for regular-season business on Thursday, Sept. 17 when the Bills play host to the Lions. That Week 2 contest opens a new era after Buffalo moved from its old home, where it played from 1973-2025.
EverBank Stadium is in the midst of renovations, which will limit the attendance at Jaguars home games. The reduced capacity of about 43,500 fans will be the league's smallest. The Jaguars will then play their home games in Orlando in 2027 as their Jacksonville venue undergoes the final stages of construction.
This is also the final year for the Titans in Nissan Stadium, which will be replaced by a new Nissan Stadium in 2027.
An expansion of the "Rivalries" uniform series gives new threads to every team in the AFC South and NFC North this year. Half of the league now owns a set of these alternate ensembles.
Additional alternates will make their debuts in Buffalo and Tampa Bay: The Bills' new "Nickel City" outfit and the return of the all-pewter Buccaneers uniform. The Ravens, Bills, Jets and Commanders also have new alternate helmets.
The biggest changes come for the following five teams, who unveiled new sets of primary uniforms.
Authentic, Fast, Timeless pic.twitter.com/mUu516fq1g
look at the details 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/I75lHKh4Hv
Threaded with Greatness. pic.twitter.com/2t1vqqf0lt
Titans of Tennessee pic.twitter.com/f7MEinwKcb
Without further ado... pic.twitter.com/0lOyf0wo20
In 2026, the NFL bids farewell to the Pro Bowl . The week between the conference championship games and Super Bowl will no longer feature any all-star festivities as the league announced in August that the "Pro Bowl Games" will not return for another installment. Although the game (or most recently, the skills competitions) is a thing of the past, 88 players will still receive Pro Bowl honors at the end of each season. Also, since there is no physical game, there will no longer be any alternates selected to the Pro Bowl roster, either.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Predicting the race for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft: Dolphins, Jets among five contenders
summary: Securing the No. 1 pick requires enduring a miserable season, but the reward could be a franchise-changing quarterback from the 2027 draft class
full_text:
Every regular season, there are two battles in the NFL standings . One is the postseason race, and the other is the competition for the No. 1 overall draft pick. The winners of those fights have plenty of reason to feel good about themselves, but the one who secures the top pick in the draft should only take so much pride in it. For as much value as there is in selecting first, you have to be the worst of 32 teams to do so.
Securing the first pick this year should be viewed as even more of a potential franchise-turning point than in other years. The 2027 quarterback class has been ballyhooed for some time now as a loaded crop with perhaps multiple future elite franchise signal-callers. Having the choice of the bunch is a luxury, even if it means the road to get there came with a whole lot of losses.
Here are the five teams that figure to compete the toughest for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft .
Jeff Hafley is a good coach who, like he did at Boston College, finds himself in a rough situation. This is a developmental year for the NFL's youngest roster, and Hafley should be trusted to deliver some promise on the defensive side of the ball. But with such an empty cupboard across the roster's entirety, it would require a masterclass in coaching to even pull the Dolphins out of the AFC East's basement.
Even if Malik Willis hits as a full-time starting quarterback, there just is not enough talent around him to maximize that breakout. De'Von Achane can shoulder a heavy load, but the wide receiver group is quite clearly the league's worst .
The schedule is a grind, which does no favors for an undermanned team. Catching the Jets twice helps, but battling a pair of Super Bowl contenders in the Bills and Patriots should account for four losses. Drawing the entire NFC North and AFC West hurts, too, considering those divisions are deep with likely playoff squads.
There is some real skill position talent in the desert this year between Jeremiyah Love , Trey McBride and perhaps even a breakout-ready Marvin Harrison Jr . The defense has a couple of pieces to like in Josh Sweat and Budda Baker . The roster as a whole simply falls well short of the extremely high NFC West standard, though, which sets the Cardinals up for another long season.
Chalk up six division losses. Add in projected defeats to the myriad of other projected postseason contenders, and that column fills up extremely quickly. There is some runway at the end of the year to potentially build momentum heading into 2027 with the Jets, Saints and Vikings on the slate from Weeks 15-17, but even a win or two in that stretch might not be enough to keep the Cardinals from the bottom of the league standings.
The bottom should not fall out from underneath the Jets, because the front office made enough personnel moves defensively to raise the floor from what was an abysmal 2025 season. That does not guarantee upward mobility, though. This is a team that won a mere three games in Aaron Glenn's first campaign, and another slow start could see New York move on. The franchise has to ask itself whether Glenn is the one they want to oversee a rookie quarterback's development in 2026.
An in-season coaching change would be a forward-facing move that likely comes at the expense of wins in 2026. But even if Glenn holds onto his job, there is no reason to believe the Jets will flourish. Sure, there is young talent on the offense, but it is difficult to trust Geno Smith to utilize it at this stage of his career. And for all Demario Davis and Minkah Fitzpatrick accomplished over their combined 22 years in the league, veterans whose best football is behind them can only do so much in elevating the defense to a new tier.
A ferocious defense won the Browns a couple of games last year. It often kept them competitive in losses, too. But Myles Garrett is gone. Regression is coming; the question is how much. Perhaps Jared Verse limits the impact of Garrett's departure. The secondary is still strong, and linebacker projects as a strength. The problem is that Cleveland cannot afford for its defense to take even a slight step backward, because the offense could be truly miserable.
The young building blocks are enticing. The quarterback situation remains the league's worst. Last year, that equation amounted to five wins and the No. 6 draft pick (before the Browns traded it to the Chiefs ). It could amount to even less in 2026, because Deshaun Watson is simply that bad.
Cleveland is a middle-of-the-road quarterback away from being a respectable team. That has seemingly been the story for decades, but this time, there actually is a lot to be excited about at the other positions. The Browns could have their pick of signal-callers in the next draft, and they had better not mess it up again.
Everything on paper suggests the Titans should be breakout candidates. They hold a second-year, former No. 1 overall pick quarterback and a promising young receiving unit. They boast arguably the best interior defensive lineman in football in Jeffery Simmons . The head coach-offensive coordinator tandem of Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll could be a terrific pairing.
What they showed in training camp and in preseason games, however, was not worthy of optimism. Ward went just 13-for-24 for 126 yards and no touchdowns in two preseason appearances. Saleh's starting defense had a couple of concerning lapses, most notably in the game against the Seahawks wherein Seattle's No. 2 offense logged a 36-yard passing touchdown and practice-squad running back Jacardia Wright broke loose for a 69-yard rushing score.
If the preseason was any indication of what is to come, the Titans will find themselves adding even more early-first-round assets to their young core. There will also be questions about whether Ward is fit to be that unit's ringleader.
author: Carter Bahns

title: 2026 NFL coach hot seat tiers: Zac Taylor, Dan Quinn among those feeling the heat
summary: Ahead of the season, we assess where every coach lands on the hot seat scale
full_text:
The NFL is very much a "what have you done for me lately?" enterprise, and that especially applies to head coaches. A down year can put some of the most highly regarded coaches in some hot water, and two down years in a row might earn them a pink slip. It differs from team to team, owner to owner and front office to front office, but the coaching carousel is busy every offseason. Last year's 10 coaching changes were especially high, but the year before, there were eight, and the year before that, there were seven.
We can expect at least a handful next year, too, whether it's via an in-season firing or an exit after the season. And while some might be expected, others won't be. Entering last year, it would have been impossible to predict Mike Tomlin stepping down as Steelers coach and John Harbaugh getting fired by the Ravens .
With one day until the 2026 season kicks off, we assess the five coaches with the hottest hot seats, as well as a few who could be a potential surprise split come season's end.
From this observer's perspective, Steichen has done a really good job when he had even a playable quarterback. He was 17-17 through two years with Anthony Richardson , Gardner Minshew and Joe Flacco as his quarterbacks and then surged to a 8-2 start last year with a healthy Daniel Jones . Then Jones popped up on the injury report with a fracture in his leg before tearing his Achilles a few weeks later. Last year's Colts finished 8-9.
Steichen's offensive smarts shouldn't be in doubt, but the circumstances around him aren't exactly favorable. Chris Ballard is about as "hot seat" as it gets for a GM considering the Colts have won one playoff game since he took over the role in 2017, and that postseason win was in 2018. Jones is coming off a torn Achilles, and even though he has looked good, time will tell if he's back. The AFC South has gotten much stronger with the Texans and Jaguars surging last year, and the AFC as a whole figures to be a dogfight.
If Ballard is gone, is Steichen gone? If Jones struggles, is Steichen gone? Even if Jones and the offense as a whole are good, is the defense good enough to support playoff aspirations? The Colts could look to start anew, and if they do, Steichen would immediately be an in-demand option next offseason, similar to how Kevin Stefanski got the Falcons job this offseason shortly after being fired by the Browns .
Glenn's 2025 was, predictably, a disaster. The offense was awful as Justin Fields struggled. New York started Fields, Tyrod Taylor and, by the end of the season, undrafted rookie Brady Cook under center. Likely more disappointing for Glenn, a former cornerback and defensive coordinator, though, was his defense. The Jets became the first team ever to finish a season without an interception , allowed the highest passer rating in the NFL and finished 30th in defensive expected points added per play. There were constant breakdowns everywhere.
This offseason, New York focused on getting a ton of steady veterans in the door, not to lift the team to playoff contention, but to simply raise the floor. Still, there are worries. Glenn fired eight different assistant coaches, including both coordinators. However, he took nearly a month after the season ended to fire offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand, meaning the Jets had already missed out on even attempting to lure in some of the more sought-after play callers available. They eventually landed on Frank Reich, whose last two NFL offenses were among the worst in the league. The last time we saw him in the NFL, he didn't even survive one season as Carolina's head coach in 2023. He was out of football in 2024 and Stanford's interim coach in 2025.
The Jets are loaded with draft capital -- three first-rounders in 2027 -- and in need of a quarterback. They will also need to restock a defense currently featuring veterans on short deals. GM Darren Mougey could look to pair his new signal-caller with a new, offensive-minded head coach. At the very least, Glenn's team must look competent. He can get a pass, somewhat, for last year. That won't be the case again in 2026.
In four seasons in Tampa, Todd Bowles has recorded between eight and 10 wins every year. It looked like the Buccaneers were ready to leave that middle ground last year when they started 6-2, but they melted down over the second half of the year.
Bowles hangs his hat on the defensive side of the ball, but Tampa Bay was 20th in scoring defense last year, the worst mark by a Bowles-coached defense since his 2018 Buccaneers. On the offensive side of the ball, he's on his fifth coordinators in five years. He fired Byron Leftwich after his first year, lost Dave Canales to the Panthers ' coaching job in 2024, lost Liam Coen to the Jaguars' coaching job in 2025 and fired Josh Grizzard earlier this year. Now, it's Zac Robinson , who was most recently with the Falcons. That hire is crucial for Bowles' future.
More than anything, though, the Buccaneers feel like a team in transition. Baker Mayfield is playing out the last year of his deal without an extension. Mike Evans is gone. Lavonte David is gone. There's a influx of young defensive talent, including Rueben Bain Jr . and Josiah Trotter in the first and second round, respectively, a strong offensive line and several intriguing players around Mayfield. It's a good -- not great -- roster in a bad division. Anything less than a return to the playoffs and a much-improved defense would have Bowles feeling the heat.
After leading Washington to a 12-5 record and its first NFC Championship game in 30+ years in 2024, Quinn went 5-12 last year. Injuries were a major factor, but Quinn admitted the standard slipped, too.
Quinn inherited a rough situation (really rough, in fact), and the roster still has significant holes in terms of top-end talent and depth. Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps didn't help. The 2026 season features a brutal start of at the Eagles , at the Cowboys and against the Seahawks , and if Washington starts slowly, the heat will really turn up on Quinn.
On one hand, Josh Harris has a history of being patient. As 76ers owner, he oversaw "The Process." On the other hand, the Commanders have failed to put a quality enough product around Jayden Daniels . Quinn is betting big on offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones -- both first-time play callers -- to elevate their respective units. It could be argued that a bounce-back year, even if it doesn't result in a playoff berth, would be enough for him to stay another year. But even that is no certainty.
There are simply no more excuses. After all, as Joe Burrow said in May : "We have everything we need in that locker room. We just gotta go and make it happen."
Cincinnati finally got serious about investing on defense, trading for Dexter Lawrence and signing Boye Mafe , Bryan Cook and Jonathan Allen. Burrow's entire offensive line is back, as are Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins and Chase Brown . Taylor is trying his best to diversify the attack by getting Burrow under center more, an aspect that could, hypothetically, help ... if it goes smoothly. Burrow has never exactly loved the concept, but it should be a boon for the run game.
Taylor is the only AFC North coach not in his first season. The Ravens, Browns and Steelers all moved on from coaches who had previously had major success. Harbaugh and Tomlin were both Super Bowl winners. Stefanski won two Coach of the Year awards. Taylor remains despite having accomplished neither. If this year isn't the year to return to the postseason -- the drought is up to three years now -- Taylor might not return, period.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Prisco's NFL Week 1 Power Rankings: Jaguars, Cowboys deserve attention; Rams' super team too good to be true
summary: Pete Prisco shares his first Power Rankings of the 2026 NFL season, and he's ready for the critics to unleash their fury
full_text:
NFL Week One Power Rankings often become fodder for jokes at the end of the season. That's because we usually have no idea what's about to take place in the wild, crazy NFL. Yet as we head into this season, it's all about the Los Angeles Rams .
Why are the other 31 teams even playing? I mean the Rams are the chic, trendy pick to win it all. They are star-laden, with the reigning MVP at quarterback in Matthew Stafford , along with defensive stars in Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald , who came out of retirement after sitting out two seasons. They can't be stopped or blocked.
Most have the Rams in the Super Bowl . I do not, even though they have so much talent. It's just too obvious. The team that is crowned in August usually doesn't win it all.
Plus, their division is brutal. Let's not forget the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks are in that division. The Seahawks start the season at No. 1 in my Power Rankings because the champs always start at the top. The Rams are second.
Will the Seahawks finish in the top spot and repeat? Not the way I see it, but they will be a deep playoff team.
My picks to play in the Super Bowl are the Dallas Cowboys and the Jacksonville Jaguars . You've already had good laughs about that one when I released it last week. Keep laughing. Talk to me in February.
The Jaguars are third in my rankings to open the season with the Cowboys fifth. When I made the Super pick last week, people said I was either crazy, on drugs or just too damn old -- many in nastier tones than that.
I just think the Jaguars, who won 13 games last year, will be a better team this time around. The Cowboys were already good on offense, but now will be much better on defense with a new coordinator in Christian Parker and a lot of new, talented faces.
The Miami Dolphins start at the bottom and I think they will stay there for a much of the season. This season is about building for the Dolphins, not wins. If Miami wins four games, it will be a successful first season for new coach Jeff Hafley.
So print this out and keep it. I guarantee based on past history that you will get a lot of laughs from these rankings come December. That happens every year.
We think we know. We really don't.

title: Giants release Darius Slayton: Possible landing spots for veteran receiver
summary: The longtime Giant will play somewhere else in 2026
full_text:
In a surprising move, the New York Giants have released veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton less than a week before their season-opener against the Dallas Cowboys .
Slayton, 29, was the Giants' longest-tenured player and was slated to make $13 million this season. A fifth-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft , Slayton caught 296 of 522 targets for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns during his time with Big Blue.
While he never became a star in New York, Slayton was nonetheless a solid and consistent player, especially for a former late-round pick. He's had four seasons with at least 700 receiving yards and averaged an impressive 15 yards per catch during his time in New York.
Slayton is coming off his least productive season to date. In 14 games, he caught 37 of 63 targets for 538 yards and a score. He had just one game with over 50 receiving yards during his final six games of the 2025 season.
Despite last year's numbers, Slayton will probably be picked up by another NFL team sooner rather than later. A former team captain, Slayton has a proven track record and, over the years, has displayed the ability to execute his role as a complementary player without needing more of the spotlight.
Here's a rundown of some of Slayton's possible landing spots.
The Colts were the first team that came to mind following the news of Slayton's release. The Colts still have Alec Pierce , but they lost Michael Pittman when they traded him to the Steelers during the offseason. The Colts recently signed veteran Keenan Allen , who was arrested late last month for suspected DUI.
At the least, signing Slayton would give the Colts some added depth at receiver, which is something they desperately need.
The Big Apple's other team also quickly came to mind upon hearing the news of Slayton's release. Like the Colts, the Jets could also use some added depth at receiver to help complement their top receiver, Garrett Wilson .
Signing Slayton would also potentially take some of the pressure off of Omar Cooper Jr. , the 30th overall pick in April's draft. Slayton's veteran leadership and experience could aid Cooper as he transitions from college to the NFL .
The Saints ' receiving corps recently took a hit when rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson was placed on injured reserve after sustaining a right hamstring injury during a joint practice with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Tyson is expected to be out for about two months.
With Tyson out, rookie fourth-round pick Bryce Lance is slated to start alongside veteran Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele . While Slayton probably wouldn't take his spot (at least right away), he could nonetheless take some of the pressure off of Lance while giving second-year quarterback Tyler Shough another viable option in the passing game.
The 49ers signed Buccaneers legend Mike Evans and re-signed Deebo Samuel after losing Jauan Jennings to the Vikings in free agency and amid the continuous absence of Brandon Aiyuk , who appears to have played his final down with San Francisco, if not in the NFL.
San Francisco could still use some reinforcements at the position after former first-round pick Ricky Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve with a knee injury. Slayton would give the 49ers much-needed depth while complementing the rest of the team's skill players.
The defending AFC champions make sense for multiple reasons, starting with Mike Vrabel's recent acknowledgment that his team isn't very deep. Signing Slayton would help the Patriots make up for the recent departure of Kayshon Boutte , who was traded to the Houston Texans . Slayton could also help take some of the attention off of A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs while giving Drake Maye another proven pass-catcher.
The Cowboys already have CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but another proven receiver would likely be welcome in Dallas' pass-heavy offense. The Cowboys -- who play the Giants in Week 1 -- could also sign Slayton for intel purposes. Slayton could give Dallas some insight into new Giants coach John Harbaugh's offense.
Tennessee makes sense for two reasons. The Titans need some help at receiver, and, in Nashville, Slayton would be reunited with Tennessee offensive coordinator and former Giants coach Brian Daboll. Two of Slayton's best seasons were during Daboll's time as Giants coach.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Cowboys three-time Pro Bowler Tyler Smith to undergo thumb surgery, out 4-6 weeks
summary: Dallas has 'a ton of confidence' in Smith's replacement to hold down the fort in his absence
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys will be without three-time Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith for the next four to six weeks. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced on Monday that Smith will undergo surgery on his left thumb on Tuesday, which will result in his placement on injured reserve, designated to return. That comes with a four- to six-week return period. Dr. Steven Shin will perform Smith's surgery.
"At the end of the day, I felt like he couldn't do the things that he had to do at a high level," Schottenheimer said Monday. "This is a long season, and it's unfortunate. But that's why we coveted T.J. Bass. ... I think he's played a lot of really good football for us, and we expect he'll continue to do so."
Schottenheimer said the left thumb had been bothering Smith all of training camp, but he couldn't pinpoint a specific moment where the injury occurred.
"It's just one of those deals that at the end of the day, we made the decision that we all did, that the best thing is to get in front of this thing. It's a long season, let's go get it fixed," Schottenheimer said. "I think at the end of the day, you always see if you can play through these things. He's done things like that, like a lot of guys out there do. Unfortunately, when you're an offensive lineman, grip strength and things like that are really important. We know he's a quick healer, and we want to get it fixed. He'll be back before too long."
Smith will be replaced by fourth-year, undrafted veteran T.J. Bass, 27 years old, as the starting left guard. Bass has played in 48 games since 2023 with 10 starts, 5 of which came in 2025. Dallas valued him so highly that they placed a second-round tender on him in restricted free agency. He's allowed just two sacks and 15 quarterback pressures on 568 career pass-blocking snaps.
"Ton of confidence. Tyler Smith is a great player, but we feel really confident in T.J.," Schottenheimer said. "He's put great film on here. He's played next to [center] Cooper Beebe, played next to [left tackle Tyler] Guyton. That's nothing new, the communication and all that stuff. We tendered him because we trust this guy as a football player, and he's a damn good football player."
Depending on how quickly Smith heals from his left thumb surgical procedure on Tuesday, he could return for "Thursday Night Football" against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 or at the Green Bay Packers on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6.

title: Falcons name Tua Tagovailoa starting QB: What to expect from former Dolphins Pro Bowler
summary: Tagovailoa will become Atlanta's sixth different Week 1 starting quarterback in as many seasons when the Falcons face the Steelers
full_text:
The Falcons named Tua Tagovailoa their starting quarterback Monday. He beat out Michael Penix Jr . in a stop-and-start, injury-impacted quarterback battle and will make his official Atlanta debut Sunday against the Steelers .
Tagovailoa will be Atlanta's sixth consecutive different Week 1 starting quarterback.
The Dolphins released Tagovailoa, 28, last year, and he subsequently signed a one-year deal with the Falcons. Expected to go head-to-head with Penix for the starting nod, he essentially won the job de facto. Penix, recovering from yet another knee injury, wasn't able to participate in full-team drills until after the team's second preseason game , and he did not play in the third preseason game either.
Penix "did not believe that he was ready" for Week 1, according to ESPN . Shortly after naming Tagovailoa the starter, coach Kevin Stefanski said Penix Jr. won't even be active in Week 1. Cooper Rush will be the backup quarterback.
Tagovailoa, on the other hand, had almost a full training camp and played in two preseason games, though the results were mixed at best. He struggled mightily in Week 1 of the preseason, did not play in Week 2 and then looked better in Week 3 -- though that game was against the Dolphins' backups. He had trouble handling snaps in both appearances, an issue that sometimes plagued him in Miami as well. Overall, he went 10-for-13 for 117 yards across the two cameos.
Tagovailoa reached some impressive highs -- a top-10 MVP finish in 2022 and a Pro Bowl and passing yards crown in 2023 -- in Miami, but he struggled last season, throwing 15 interceptions and eventually getting benched. With the Dolphins undergoing a major rebuild, they moved on from Tagovailoa despite record cap penalties .
He'll now hope to resurrect his career surrounded by superstar running back Bijan Robinson , standout wide receiver Drake London and a solid offensive line. Health will be a key, as he has played all 17 games just once in his career, but for now, he'll get the first shot to prove he can be the answer to Atlanta's quarterback woes.
If the last two seasons and this preseason are any indicators, this will be a bumpy ride. Tagovailoa admitted his first preseason performance "wasn't up to standard" after the Falcons got throttled by the Broncos . He was better in preseason Week 3, but again, that was against several Dolphins backups -- and many of Miami's starters are backup-quality players, so really, it was against guys simply hoping to make a roster or practice squad
Tagovailoa's propensity for getting rid of the ball as soon as possible -- and often accurately -- could technically fit, though his weak arm, limited mobility and turnover issues make the margins for error slim to none. Expect a heavy, heavy dose of Robinson, London and Kyle Pitts on quick-hitting throws. In the preseason, Tagovailoa's average pass went 2.0 yards downfield, a preposterously low number that will obviously rise when his games actually count. Still, throws like these will be commonplace, with YAC doing much of the work.
Tua finds Kyle Pitts Sr. for a 37-yard gain! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/se0K7iEgFs
Last year, Tagovailoa's average release time was 2.59 seconds, the fastest in the NFL . His 6.8 air yards per attempt ranked 28th out of 33 qualifying quarterbacks. Those numbers will rise in part because Stefanski prefers more under-center play action, but still, there's a clear picture with Tagovailoa.
Tagovailoa won this quarterback battle simply by being available (and not being a complete disaster when available). Penix's extended recovery from injury meant he didn't really get a shot.
He will almost certainly get his shot this season, though. Tagovailoa's injury history is well-documented, ranging from several concussions to thumb, rib, finger, back and hip ailments ... and that's just in his NFL career. His dislocated hip while at Alabama also made him a completely different player.
Penix simply needs more time to get into the swing of things, and when he is physically ready, a quarterback change could be quickly in the offing.
The biggest beneficiary of a potential change down the road would be London, who has thrived in his short time sharing the field with Penix.
Michael Penix Jr. on field
