title: Defining success for NFL's seven biggest Super Bowl long shots, including Raiders, Jets and Titans
summary: For the NFL's biggest longshots, success could mean developing a franchise quarterback, evaluating a new coaching staff or positioning the roster for a pivotal 2027 offseason
full_text:
What does a successful season look like for these Super Bowl long shots? Las Vegas has been handicapping the upcoming season since the prior concluded in February and, through Super Bowl odds, expressed how it perceives each team. Seven teams held +10000 odds or worse. Unfortunately, four of those teams were on last year's list, too. The following is in order from shortest to longest odds:
Tennessee enters the second year with quarterback Cam Ward and the first year with coach Robert Saleh. At the bare minimum, the objective should be not to be on this list next year. A success would be feeling good about the Ward-Saleh pairing heading into 2027.
The Titans spent heavily, particularly on the defensive side of the ball ($125 million total guaranteed). It may take some time for that group to come together, but the hope is that they adopt Saleh's hard-nosed demeanor. If all goes as planned, the franchise will be tasked with replacing pieces of the operation next offseason rather than the operation itself, positioning them to take a big leap within the AFC South.
The vibes around the Falcons are not great, but few can boast the collection of elite offensive skill talent -- wide receiver Drake London , running back Bijan Robinson and tight end Kyle Pitts -- assembled in Atlanta.
The best possible outcome would be having clarity on Michael Penix Jr. , one way or another, entering the offseason. If Penix is fully healthy and establishes himself as an investment-caliber quarterback, it would allow them to funnel resources elsewhere. Alternatively, if neither Tua Tagovailoa nor Penix inspires confidence, it would open the door for the team to go in another direction at the position.
In either scenario, the Falcons would be staring down a full season from edge rushers James Pearce Jr . and Jalon Walker , as well as the hope that a new quarterback brings.  Atlanta will have the most salary cap space by a wide margin this offseason, according to Spotrac.
Las Vegas' best possible outlook boils down to the success of No. 1 overall selection Fernando Mendoza and first-year coach Klint Kubiak. Despite Kirk Cousins being named the Week 1 starter, Mendoza must see the field this season and showcase the skill set that enabled him to be drafted so early, which in turn creates optimism as the 2027 campaign begins.
Beyond Mendoza, the Raiders bringing in another supreme talent with an early draft pick as part of the long-term vision would be another step in the right direction.
Las Vegas ranks among the top-10 in projected salary cap space as well.
The Browns had arguably the best rookie class a year ago, and the early returns on the 2026 draft class have been promising as well. The limitations at quarterback have capped the potential of this season, but they have positioned themselves well to bring in that player next offseason through the trade of Myles Garrett .
In an ideal world, Cleveland would be feeling good about the collection of offensive rookie talent -- offensive tackle Spencer Fano and wide receivers Denzel Boston , KC Concepcion -- after the season, while simultaneously being in position to draft its quarterback of choice in 2027. In each of the past two years, the franchise has been in the top six overall of a one-quarterback draft, but failed to secure that player.
It is important to note that the 2027 season would be the first without quarterback Deshaun Watson on the roster since 2021.
New York is the most difficult to project because what is best for the franchise is not what is best for the coaching staff. Aaron Glenn knows his job is on the line and will be desperate for wins. Too many wins, however, could conceivably put a potential franchise quarterback outside of the organization's reach. They have three first-round picks to move up if another team is willing to deal, but what if it is like the 2024 NFL Draft, where every team in the top three overall selected a quarterback, and there was no other option? Could they thread the needle of being bad enough to draft a quarterback without trading all of their assets while also showing enough progress to retain the coaching staff? The proposition seems unlikely, but not impossible.
Additionally, if the organization can identify pieces of the future. Can D'Angelo Ponds hold up at cornerback? Is David Bailey the elite talent he was billed as during the pre-draft process? Will either Omar Cooper Jr . or Kenyon Sadiq emerge as essential outlets in the offense?
If one were to ask two Dolphins fans their ideal outcome for the upcoming season, each would likely give a different answer. The first may desire free agent acquisition Malik Willis to have a good season, and for the franchise to invest in Willis' supporting cast. Miami has a projected $104 million in salary cap space, fifth-most in the NFL . The second may wish for the team to bottom out and be in a position to draft a quarterback No. 1 overall next April.
The team drafted 13 players in the 2026 NFL Draft. If they can identify four or five starters among that group, then that would be a great outcome for the Dolphins. As it stands, running back De'Von Achane and potentially edge rusher Chop Robinson are the only impact performers on the roster.
Arizona has a lot of young talent on defense. If either defensive tackle Walter Nolen II or cornerback Will Johnson Jr. emerges as a blue-chip talent within that defense, then it greatly raises the ceiling of that unit. Cornerbacks Denzel Burke , Max Melton and Garrett Williams have all had positive moments in their respective careers as well. If defensive lineman Darius Robinson gives them anything, it will be icing on the cake.
Offensively, a positive outcome would be having confidence in coach Mike LaFleur's scheme and the way running back Jeremiyah Love , tight end Trey McBride, and wide receivers Michael Wilson Jr. and Marvin Harrison Jr . are deployed.
Having said all of that, next season will be a wash if they do not identify a sustainable quarterback situation. Jacoby Brissett may be fine in the short-term, and Carson Beck is capable of stringing together some decent performances, but the outlook for either becoming a long-term option is bleak.

title: Winners, losers, grades from Week 1 in college football; NFL season predictions produce shocker

full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
For most teams in Week 1, the goal was simple: Beat a team you are supposed to beat. The opening slate was light on marquee matchups and heavy on contests between heavy favorites and massive underdogs. But even in an era where the powerhouses have all the resources in the world at their disposal, college football is college football. Surprises happen.
Look no further than No. 2 Oregon , which only narrowly escaped a very real upset bid from Boise State . The Ducks won in the end, but their defensive line was one of the nation's biggest losers of Week 1 . It was supposed to be an elite, impenetrable unit but instead looked vulnerable against a Group of Six squad. And that wasn't Oregon's only shortcoming in a game it trailed by double digits.
On the flip side, other national championship hopefuls took care of business and left no doubt. No. 7 Miami , for one, might have the best offense in the country. Is that an overreaction ? It sure won't be if Malachi Toney keeps playing like a Heisman Trophy contender .
And how about No. 13 Alabama ? The Crimson Tide was a touch underwhelming in the early years of the Kalen DeBoer era, but it did everything it was supposed to do in a 48-10 thumping of East Carolina . We'll give the team as a whole a "B" grade for turning in a mostly great but still imperfect effort. As for new starting quarterback Keelon Russell , our Brad Crawford graded his debut .
WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement on Friday . The league's first commissioner, who took office in 2019, will step away from the role at the end of the year.
Over more than seven years, Engelbert oversaw the league's most dramatic period of growth. With the introduction of three expansion teams (plus three more on the way by 2030), the signing of a massive $3.1 billion media rights deal, multiple collective bargaining agreements and numerous other achievements on her résumé, she leaves her post as an immensely successful commissioner.
But players and fans alike are not exactly sad to see her go. Our Lindsay Gibbs explains the other side of the equation.
Engelbert said there are already internal and external candidates for her replacement. She will remain on board until early 2027 if the league does not find a successor by Dec. 31. Who is worthy and capable of stepping into what is a more highly scrutinized role than ever? We have a few ideas:

title: 2026 NFL Week 1 early odds: Cowboys road favorites vs. Giants, while Panthers in familiar position vs. Bears
summary: Here's a look at the lines for Week 1 in the NFL as we open up the 2026 season
full_text:
After what feels like a blink of an eye and two decades all jumbled up into one, the NFL is finally back. In just a couple of days, the 2026 regular season will kick off in Seattle, where we'll see a rematch of Super Bowl LX between the Patriots and Seahawks . From there, we're off to the races and heading down to Australia for an early international matchup as the 49ers and Rams will kick off from Melbourne Cricket Ground. It'll be all gas, no brakes, until we get to Los Angeles for Super Bowl LXI.
As we shake off the rust and prepare to wager on the opening slate of the NFL season, let's remember that this is one of the trickiest times to bet on the league calendar. Need a refresher? Let's take a quick look back at the start of the 2025 season, where Week 1 offers a clear-cut example of its obscurity. Last year, the Raiders went into Foxborough and defeated the Patriots, 20-13, in the season opener. After that, New England went on to win the AFC and reach the Super Bowl, while Las Vegas earned the No. 1 overall pick following a league-worst 3-14 record.
With that in mind, it's important to have your head on a swivel in Week 1 because some funky results are bound to occur. Below, we'll take an early look at the Week 1 odds, highlighting the spread, total, and moneyline as we gear up for the new season.
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted)
Patriots at Seahawks (Wednesday)
Patriots +150, Seahawks -180
49ers at Rams (Thursday, in Australia)
Falcons +154, Steelers -185
Buccaneers +170, Bengals -205
Cardinals +410, Chargers -549
Packers +102, Vikings -122
Dolphins +160, Raiders -192
Commanders +180, Eagles -218
Broncos at Chiefs (Monday)
The defending champion Seahawks come into Week 1 after not only hoisting the Lombardi Trophy, but also covering a league-best 75% of their games in 2025 (including playoffs). However, they are a bit of a different club than the one that found itself in the winner's circle a year ago, most notably losing offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak and Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III . They were also 6-4 ATS (60%) at Lumen Field last year. As for New England, they were quite stellar against the spread as well, notching a 13-7-1 ATS record over the course of the regular season and playoffs. That included a 7-2 ATS road record. This offseason, they added the likes of A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs on offense. One X-factor for this game that could certainly swing these odds is the status of All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez , who is in the midst of a contract dispute with the team, raising questions about his availability for the opener.
We're heading Down Under for the second game of the 2026 season, as the Niners and Rams will duke it out from Melbourne. What's fascinating about this matchup (beyond it being a key NFC West head-to-head) is how both clubs are dealing with international travel. San Francisco has already flown down to Australia, giving itself a week to best acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. As for L.A., they'll be in Australia for just over 24 hours, opting to arrive the day before the game . This aligns with how the Rams have handled international travel in the past, and it seems to have worked quite well for them. Under McVay, Los Angeles is a perfect 3-0 (SU and ATS) in international games, while outscoring their opponents 92-17.
Jacksonville was one of the best teams to back in 2025, owning a 12-6 ATS record (regular season and postseason). That included an NFL-best 7-2 ATS record at home, where they boasted a 13.7-point average margin of victory. Meanwhile, the Browns -- who will start Deshaun Watson after the veteran beat out Shedeur Sanders this summer for the Week 1 job -- are looking to improve a dreadful road record in 2025. Last year, they were 2-6 (SU and ATS) on the road and lost by an average of 12.5 points.
The Colts enter 2025 with Daniel Jones back under center as he looks to return to his first-half form from last year before going down with a torn Achilles. Even after their free fall down the stretch, Indy was still 8-7-2 ATS last year. The offense will look a bit different, however, with Michael Pittman Jr. traded to Pittsburgh this offseason, meaning Jones will need to lean on the likes of Alec Pierce , Josh Downs , and Keenan Allen in the passing game at receiver. As for the Ravens, they are beginning the Jessie Minter era after the former Chargers defensive coordinator was hired as head coach this offseason. Minter will look to get Baltimore's defense back into shape. If he does, they'll certainly improve upon the 6-11 ATS record from 2025, which was tied for the second-lowest in the NFL.
Both of these teams made the playoffs a season ago but are looking to take another step towards contention. They were roughly in the same tier in terms of the gambling sphere in 2025, with the Texans going 10-9 ATS (including playoffs) and the Bills going 9-10 ATS. This will be an opportunity for new Buffalo head coach Joe Brady to flex his offensive prowess against a top-flight Texans defense, and for the Josh Allen- D.J. Moore connection to take shape. Meanwhile, all eyes will be on C.J. Stroud as the Texans' QB looks to rebound from a disastrous playoff run. Last year, the Texans were 5-4 ATS at home, while the Bills were 5-5 ATS on the road.
Who doesn't love a little revenge narrative? Robert Saleh will begin his head coaching tenure with the Titans when he hosts his former Jets squad in the opener. Neither Tennessee nor New York is expected to make much of a splash this season, so this is an opportunity for Saleh to start on a strong note, and he will do so as a slim 1.5-point favorite. Under the previous regime, Tennessee was 4-5 ATS at home in 2025. Meanwhile, the Jets still have Aaron Glenn pulling the strings as head coach, but they do have a new quarterback in Geno Smith . With Smith under center, New York will try to improve on the 3-4-1 ATS road record from last season.
Both of these NFC squads are coming off a 2025 season that saw them each reach the playoffs, but it'll be an uphill climb for them to get back there in 2026. Each faces a difficult schedule, but Chicago may be better equipped to handle it and come into this matchup as a 2.5-point road favorite. In their lone game as a road favorite in 2025, the Bears covered. As for the Panthers, this is a position they are quite comfortable being in. Last year, Carolina was an underdog at home eight times. They covered six of those games and won five of them outright.
At long last, the Falcons have named their starting quarterback . In Week 1, it'll be Tua Tagovailoa, who gets the nod from head coach Kevin Stefanski, but it comes after a less-than-inspiring showing this summer. Given that it seemed like Tagovailoa was earmarked for the job over Michael Penix Jr., the line appears to have baked in this result as it continues to sit at Steelers -3.5. In 2025, Atlanta was 4-4 ATS on the road. Looking at the Steelers, they are beginning the Mike McCarthy era after he was hired as the head coach this offseason. Of course, McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers have a long history together from their days in Green Bay, so this should be pretty seamless for the duo. McCarthy will try to get the Steelers playing better ball in Pittsburgh, where they were 5-4 ATS in 2025.
If you're looking for a shootout, this might be your best bet, with this matchup between Tampa Bay and Cincinnati having the highest total on the board in Week 1. Before jumping in on the Over, however, it'd be wise to monitor the status of Bucs wideout Emeka Egbuka . The second-year receiver -- who is expected to take over as the No. 1 option following Mike Evans ' departure in free agency -- has been battling a toe injury that has had him sidelined for portions of the summer. If he can't go, that'd drastically cap Tampa Bay's offense. Last season, the Buccaneers were 4-5 ATS on the road, while Cincinnati was 4-5 ATS at home, so something will need to give…

title: 2026 NFL predictions: Final record for all 32 teams, Super Bowl LXI pick, playoff matchups and MVP winner
summary: We just went through and predicted the entire 2026 NFL season
full_text:
Welcome to football's greatest Labor Day tradition: The release of my annual NFL predictions.
After spending the past three days locked in a windowless room trying to figure out who's going to win the Super Bowl this year, I am ready to share my predictions with the world. Will you hate them? Probably. Will you hate me? Maybe.
If I've noticed one thing over the years, it's that people love to throw the wrong predictions back in my face at the end of the year, but that won't be an issue this year, because I don't plan on getting anything wrong.
That being said, if I do end up getting some (or all) of my predictions wrong, feel free to rub it in my face on social media (You can send hate messages to me on X , and I also started a TikTok because my Gen Z nephews told me that no one uses X anymore, so feel free to make fun of me there).
Anyway, before we get to my predictions, let me explain how things will work here: I'll go through each division and predict each team's final record. After that, I'll be making one bold prediction for each division.
Once you roll through the divisional portion of these predictions, you'll see my playoff picks and eventually the team I'm picking to win the Super Bowl. In two of the past 10 years, my preseason Super Bowl pick has ended up winning it all, so if you want to skip everything and scroll straight down to my Super Bowl pick to see if I'm taking your team, I won't be offended.
Finally, if you're wondering how I did last season , I predicted the exact record for 13 different teams or came within one game of it. According to the guys at Stadium Rant , I had the second-most accurate preseason predictions among the media members they tracked. Does that mean I was good, or does it mean that I was just less worse than everyone else? I'm still trying to figure that out.
Even though my predictions were pretty solid for most teams, there was one team that I absolutely whiffed on last year, and that was the Seahawks . I had them missing the playoffs, and if you watched any football in 2025, then you already know that the Seahawks did NOT miss the playoffs.
The largest and most technologically advanced Super Bowl ring ever created for the SBLX Champions. pic.twitter.com/2M2ANGEBgT
That ring is worth more than my car, and the irony is that I could have bought a new car if I had picked the Seahawks to win the Super Bowl last year and made a big bet on it. I definitely will not be underestimating the Seahawks this year. Does that mean I'll be picking them to pull off a Super Bowl repeat?
Let's get to the 2026 predictions and find out.
1. *Bills: 11-6 2. Patriots : 9-8 3. Jets : 6-11 4. Dolphins : 2-15
AFC East bold prediction: Patriots miss the playoffs
Before I explain myself here, I would like to start by saying that my AFC East bold prediction for 2025 was that the Patriots would win double-digit games and that Mike Vrabel would win Coach of the Year. Well, check and check. I also predicted that the Patriots would win the AFC title game by exactly three points over Denver and that they'd lose by two touchdowns to the Seahawks in the Super Bowl.
OK, now that we've established that I'm never wrong about the Patriots, we can get to this year and why I think they'll miss the playoffs. On defense, I'm worried about New England's pass-rush. Their sack leader from last year, Harold Landry , is going to miss at least the first four games of the season, and they don't really have any proven stars behind him. On the other side of the ball, I'm concerned about the offensive line. On paper, it's certainly better than it was last year -- and Will Campbell will be fully healthy -- but I'll believe they're better when I actually see it. This group is going to get two stiff tests in the first two weeks (The Seahawks defense in Week 1 and T.J. Watt in Week 2), and if they pass those, I'll probably be regretting this bold prediction by Week 3.
And let's not forget about the schedule. Last year, the Patriots took advantage of one of the easiest schedules in NFL history. This year, they have an absolute gauntlet coming out of the gate. Their first four opponents have a combined strength-of-schedule of .721, the highest SOS any team has faced in the first four weeks in 40 years. To make things worse, the Patriots will have to play three of their first four games on the road. They might start 1-3, and if that happens, I could see things getting ugly from there, but not too ugly, because I do have them finishing over .500.
1. *Ravens: 12-5 2. *Bengals: 11-6 3. *Steelers: 9-8 4. Browns : 5-12
AFC North bold prediction: Bengals second-round pick wins Defensive Rookie of the Year
Two years ago, I correctly predicted that Jared Verse would win defensive rookie of the year , and this year, I'm jumping on the Cashius Howell bandwagon. A front-seven player has won this award in eight of the past 10 years, and Howell will keep that trend going.
The easiest way for a defensive player to win this award is to rack up sacks, and Howell is in the perfect position to do it. With Dexter Lawrence now on the team, you can pretty much bet that every offense the Bengals play this year will be worried about slowing down Lawrence. That likely means Lawrence will regularly see double teams, which should open the door for someone on the defensive line to shine, and I think that someone will be Howell, who was taken with the 41st overall pick back in April.
And let's not forget, Howell is in a very sack-friendly division. He gets to face Aaron Rodgers , who has been sacked more times than any other QB in NFL history. He also gets to face a Browns offense that surrendered 51 sacks last season, which was the seventh-most in the NFL. As a matter of fact, there were only eight teams last year that gave up 49 sacks or more, and the Bengals will get to play four games against those eight teams, so Howell will be in a position to put up some impressive numbers.
1. *Texans: 11-6 2. Jaguars : 8-9 3. Colts : 7-10 4. Titans : 3-14
AFC South bold prediction: Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in interceptions
The Jaguars won the AFC South last year, and they did that despite the fact that Lawrence threw 12 interceptions, which was tied for the fifth-most in the NFL. Lawrence's biggest struggles came early in the season with three interceptions in his first four games. The early season could be another struggle for Lawrence this year, and that's because the Jags will be facing two of the best defenses in the NFL in the first two weeks: The Browns (Week 1) and Broncos (Week 2). There were only three teams in the NFL that recorded more than 50 sacks last season, and those were two of them. Basically, Lawrence is likely going to be under a lot of pressure, which could lead to three or four interceptions in the first two weeks. And things won't be getting any easier after that.
Here's what the Jags schedule looks like from Week 2 through their Week 7 bye:
Week 2: at Broncos Week 3: Patriots Week 4: at Bengals Week 5: vs. Eagles (in London) Week 6: vs. Texans (in London)
That's brutal. Lawrence threw at least one interception in nine of Jacksonville's 17 games last season, and he did that even though he had Travis Etienne in his backfield, a player who was so good that he took a lot of pressure off the passing game. The Jags won't have Etienne this year, and although they do have two solid running backs in Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, I don't think they'll be quite as good as Etienne. With the running game taking a step back, I think Lawrence will be asked to do more, which will lead to more interceptions.
1. *Broncos: 12-5 2. *Chiefs: 10-7 3. Chargers : 9-8 4. Raiders : 5-12
AFC West bold prediction: Broncos repeat as AFC West champs and win the division by multiple games
The Broncos won the AFC West last year, but somehow, they still can't get any respect. Going into the 2026 season, the Broncos have the third-best odds to win the division. They are somehow behind both the Chiefs…

title: 3 reasons to be excited, 3 reasons to be concerned about the Cardinals
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are in countdown mode. Think about Mike LaFleur, who has been hired to become the head coach of an NFL team. That has to be exciting, and super anxious at the same time. The preparation, the work, the roster decisions, and all the ideas that came from Moment 1 to the opening […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 12: Trey McBride #85, Michael Wilson #14 and James Conner #6 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrate after a play during the second half in the game against the Atlanta Falcons at State Farm Stadium on November 12, 2023 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are in countdown mode. Think about Mike LaFleur, who has been hired to become the head coach of an NFL team. That has to be exciting, and super anxious at the same time. The preparation, the work, the roster decisions, and all the ideas that came from Moment 1 to the opening kickoff against the Los Angeles Chargers. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSIVE WEAPONS RANKED #6 And now, the excitement of the season. Everything is new. Every team in the NFL has the same record at 0-0-0 with the same goals: division crown, playoff bid, conference championship game appearance, and play in the Super Bowl. For Cardinals fans, there is hope, but also the realization that this team broke a 127-year franchise record for the most losses in a single season with 14. That doesn’t simply cure itself overnight. It is easy to be excited about the new year, the new schedule, new players, and yes, a new coaching staff. But this franchise has been down so many times and kicked off the year with high hopes, only to realize that the new boss is just like the old boss. Here is what we, as Arizona fans, can be excited about and also concerned about. Excited: Offensive weapons are everywhere As training camp approached, ESPN ran an article and rated the best offenses for the upcoming season. The Cardinals were ranked #6. We agree. Every NFL team that has a high-powered offensive group has either a stud at quarterback, a receiver that is uncoverable, or a stallion in the backfield. With Arizona, however, it is their tight end, Trey McBride. What a sensational guy this is, and he is just getting started. He had the most targets on the team last year (169), most receptions (126), most first-down conversions (63), most yards (1,239), and the most touchdowns (11). Those numbers could explode this year with this new offense, which has multiple tight ends on the field for most every offensive play. Backup TE Elijah Higgins will get more targets than you think. Michael Wilson has assumed the WR1 position. The key element of this offense is whether Marv Harrison can rebound and finally become that “generational” player he was advertised to become. And what about RB Jeremiyah Love, the #3 overall pick in the draft? These two are going to be the reasons why Arizona can win games or get bogged down. The receiver depth is very deep this year with Kendrick Bourne, Simi Fehoko, Jalen Brooks, and the rookie Reggie Virgil. With a veteran at quarterback in Jacoby Brissett and capable backups, the weapons that this offense has accumulated are going to surprise a lot of folks. Concerned: The offensive line The Wild Card to this offense? Without a shadow of a doubt: The offensive line. GM Monti Ossenfort did his best to fix this mess with multiple signings for starters and also quality depth. The big question seems to be whether his big splash during free agency, OG Isaac Semualo, can create stability and whether Isaiah Adams is really ready to take on the starting role at the other guard spot. These two men are critical to the offense’s success in running the ball, which is a significant portion of the offense. Not much has been mentioned about Elijah Wilkinson as the new right tackle, so that’s good news. The coaching staff believes he is doing what he is supposed to be doing, although in the past few years he has been known to collect laundry. Hopefully he doesn’t attract many penalties going forward. And center Hjalte Froholdt and LT Paris Johnson. Anyone worried about either one? This group has the potential of being really solid, or could fall apart if they don’t come out as one cohesive unit right out of the gate. The backups are a good group as well, with Jon Gaines and Josh Fryar leading the room. Excited: Up the gut run defense Getting Roy Lopez back with the defense is such a blessing. He has good gap responsibility and is stiff against the run. Now, can Walter Nolen remain healthy? Seemed like each week in training camp he was walking off the turf with some ailment. He is such a force when healthy. Great physical traits with good explosiveness. He is certainly a playmaker, but he has to stay on the field for Arizona. And Andrew Billings has been a big surprise this preseason. Seems like every year his body keeps getting bigger, but since he is a rotational player, his limited snaps shouldn’t be an issue. For some reason, he seems a bit quicker than last year when he was with the Chicago Bears. L.J. Collier has had his moments, but is a good run stopper and gives this defense inside-out flexibility. Concerned: Pass rush opposite Josh Sweat Ossenfort couldn’t fix every hole on this roster. Getting another pass rusher to bookend EDGE rusher Josh Sweat would have been ideal. The GM passed on several young pass-rushing studs early in the draft in order to take Love, which would have made this year’s defense one of the best pass-rushing teams in the division at least. Right now, that responsibility is resting on the shoulders of Darius Robinson and Zaven Collins. Both players were drafted high, and the one thing this defense is not getting from either is another high: production. Collins had just 1.5 sacks last year with 40 tackles and 10 QB hits. That does not scream “elite-level pass rusher.” Robinson has had two sacks total since signing his rookie deal. Most Cardinals fans were expecting him to be released after training camp, and yet, here we are in total mediocrity. And it’s not like Ossenfort can just reach out and sign a free agent for assistance. That list has been picked over to the bone. Excited: Elite defensive backfield One thing Ossenfort loves is cornerbacks and safeties. He is a former college quarterback and knows that competent guys in the back are critical. So, it’s his pet project. He didn’t draft S Budda Baker, but he realizes just how special this dude is. NFL All-Rookie Team, eight Pro Bowls, Art Rooney Award winner, two-time Second Team All-Pro, and two-time First Team All-Pro. All of that in just nine seasons. Six seasons with 100+ tackles, including 164 in 2024. In 2019, he made the most solo tackles in the league with 104. So, what does Ossenfort do? He takes care of Baker. He continues to nurture him and make him feel needed and happy. As Cardinals fans, thank you for doing this Mr. O. Then there is the cornerback room. Will Johnson is a league star waiting to explode. And his creative cast is doing a great job with Garrett Williams, Max Melton, and Denzel Burke, who showed last year he can ball out. Now, all of this is with an asterisk. Can each of these young men remain healthy? The collapse of the pass coverage last year due to multiple players getting hurt killed this defense. The lone backup is Kei’Trel Crawford. Ossenfort was able to nab a veteran safety that hardly anyone is talking about, and that is Andrew Wingard. He is as solid as he can be, and will hit his grandma if she catches a ball in his zone. The backups all show promise, with Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (who could actually start right now) and the new guy, Wydett Williams. This entire group will decide the season. The NFC West has exceptional receivers, pass-catching tight ends, and veteran quarterbacks who know how to find tight windows. Concerned: The friggin’ schedule Aren’t the fourth-place division teams from last year supposed to play each other and have the easiest schedules the next year? What happened to that plan? Because the Cardinals currently own the league’s fourth-most difficult schedule. Isn’t there somebody we can sue for misrepresentation? And about playing all the worst teams from the season before? From that list of last-place division finishers, Arizona…

title: How the Falcons can start reviving a dejected fanbase with low expectations
summary: Whenever a team finds itself alone in a category except for the New York Jets, it most likely has fallen on hard times. That’s where the Falcons are when it comes to playoff appearances since 2020. After the Panthers won the NFC South last season, only the Falcons and Jets remain as teams that haven’t […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 20: Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) runs through a drill during the Indianapolis Colts and Atlanta Falcons joint training camp practice on August 20, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Whenever a team finds itself alone in a category except for the New York Jets, it most likely has fallen on hard times. That’s where the Falcons are when it comes to playoff appearances since 2020. After the Panthers won the NFC South last season, only the Falcons and Jets remain as teams that haven’t made the playoffs in the 2020s. Considering the state of the NFC South since Tom Brady retired after the 2022 season, it’s unfathomable that the Falcons haven’t won the division. They made significant free agency investments in 2023 and 2024 to put themselves in a position to bring playoff football back to Atlanta. They swept the team that finished in first place in Tampa Bay in 2024. The front office went all in on drafting two highly regarded edge rushers in the first round to address the most significant flaw on the roster last year. None of it has resulted in making a playoff appearance. Three consecutive disappointing years have led to multiple coaching changes, four starting quarterbacks, and exceptional players on both sides of the ball deserving so much better. It has left a fanbase largely jaded. From the Arthur Smith-Desmond Ridder debacle in 2023 to Kirk Cousins collapsing in 2024 to Raheem Morris losing control last year, the consistent failure has been heavy for a franchise that can’t figure things out. Matt Ryan becoming the Falcons’ President of Football provided a much-needed spark. It will take much more than the return of a franchise legend to inject optimism into a franchise that hasn’t made the playoffs since Nick Foles’ peak. New coach Kevin Stefanski needs to build a true identity. Ian Cunningham must prove his promising start as general manager leads to lasting success. That starts with young players emerging on one of the league’s oldest rosters. Whether the Falcons make the playoffs or not won’t determine their success in 2026. Several personnel concerns exist across the roster, none bigger than at the sport’s most important position. Putting playoff expectations on a team that doesn’t know which quarterback will start the most games for them isn’t practical. That shouldn’t prevent them from making strides as a franchise. The revamped coaching staff and promising talent are there for genuine growth in Atlanta. Overcoming quarterback uncertainty through coaching Other than Kevin O’Connell, it’s hard to find a current head coach who has endured more quarterback instability yet still found ways to succeed than Stefanski. You lose count trying to remember all the different signal callers he had to work with for six seasons in Cleveland. That’s a challenge the two-time Coach of the Year will have to take on again in 2026. The difference is he has a more solidified offensive infrastructure with legitimate firepower. A trio of Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts creates exciting possibilities no matter who is under center. An offensive line returning four starters, with Bill Callahan coaching them, provides stability that was lost in his final years in Cleveland. The pieces are there to construct an efficient offense that can outscore teams, even with the glaring quarterback limitations. Diversifying the run game will be crucial in controlling tempo and wearing down opposing fronts. After relying too heavily on outside zone for multiple seasons, adding more gap-scheme concepts should bring more consistency on the ground. Increasing play-action usage and more varied formations are other potential schematic assets that Stefanski brings to the table. The overall offense needed a total reset after it became so predictable under Zac Robinson. Questions linger about the game plan, whether it’s for Tua Tagovailoa early in the year and perhaps Michael Penix Jr. later on. There’s also skepticism about Tommy Rees as offensive coordinator, as Cleveland ranked 30th in EPA per play when he took over play-calling duties in Week 10 last season. While the Falcons’ offense is significantly more talented, can Rees work with Stefanski to help maximize the quarterback’s capabilities? Whether it’s a quick-pass, heavy RPO system with Tagovailoa or a more aggressive shotgun-based plan with Penix Jr., the Falcons invested too much into their offense to be below average. Stefanski worked wonders with Cleveland in 2020 and 2023 when expectations weren’t exactly high. Some of it came from utilizing heavier personnel packages, running 12 and 13 looks, creating more high-percentage looks in the passing game, and putting the offense in better down-and-distances. Attacking defenses with a wide variety of screens was another key component to his success. These are ideal strategies the Falcons can use, given where they stand at quarterback and wide receiver. That said, Stefanski must be decisive, alongside Rees, to execute his vision with the right quarterback on the current roster. Based on how much Tagovailoa has struggled this summer, Penix Jr. appears to be his best option, but Penix is not ready to start just yet. Staying afloat defensively while a stellar secondary establishes itself Jeff Ulbrich deserves enormous praise for the defense’s elevation last season. After his return to Atlanta initially underwhelmed many people, he silenced critics with his pressure plans and coverage variation. The franchise record for most sacks in a season was broken without a game-changing edge rusher on the roster, with defensive line coach Nate Ollie also deserving major credit. While James Pearce Jr. broke the franchise record for most sacks by a rookie in a season, he didn’t take over games. It took a cohesive effort for them to overwhelm some of the league’s best offenses in dramatic upset victories. Many of the players who were at the forefront of their success aren’t with the team going into the season. According to The Atlanta Journal-Constitution’s Daniel Flick, only 28.1% of the sack production will be on the opening-day roster. That total will increase when Pearce Jr. returns from suspension in Week 9. That won’t change the fact that this is a major obstacle for Ulbrich to overcome. Losing Jalon Walker for the season was a devastating blow after his promising rookie season. While it’s encouraging that the new regime was proactive in signing ZaDarius Smith and trading for Gervon Dexter Sr. to add talent up front, it’s difficult to envision the front imposing their will on many offensive lines. That not only increases the pressure on Ulbrich to call more twists and blitzes. It raises expectations for an ultra-talented secondary to lead the overall unit. Expectations must be high when a group features an All-Pro safety, Pro Bowl-caliber cornerback, an emerging ball-hawking safety, and two promising cornerbacks, as well as a well-regarded secondary coach in Justin Hood. It likely won’t happen on opening day, but Jessie Bates, A.J. Terrell, Xavier Watts, Avieon Terrell, and Billy Bowman Jr. should be on the field together at some point. Assembling those five players should fluster quarterbacks and produce turnovers. I wrote about how special the secondary can be a month ago. While Mike Hughes will start the season, things could change as Avieon Terrell proves he can handle playing significant snaps and Bowman Jr. is healthy. Bates and Watts are consistently around the ball, attempting to make game-changing plays. A.J. Terrell is quietly coming off one of his better years. This group has all the pieces to take a significant leap to become one of the league’s best. Along with Divine Deablo, it’s the best hope to keep the defense stabilized after enduring significant losses. Brandon Dorlus’ rapid ascendance, with Maason Smith and…

title: Michael Penix Jr. injury update: Falcons QB is ‘very close,’ but not 100%
summary: Whether you like it or not — and I know a great many of you do NOT like it — Tua Tagovailoa is the Falcons’ starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Steelers. But that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s Tua’s job to lose. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to take over the starting job at […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up prior to a pre season game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Whether you like it or not — and I know a great many of you do NOT like it — Tua Tagovailoa is the Falcons’ starting quarterback for Week 1 against the Steelers . But that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s Tua’s job to lose. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to take over the starting job at some point, but as of right now, he isn’t ready. “I want to be stronger,” Penix told the media after Monday’s practice. “I want to be able to be out there and give my team 100%. And if I don’t feel I can do that, that’s not fair for this team. It’s not fair for the organization. I want to make sure whenever I am out there, I’m 100%.” Head coach Kevin Stefanski told the media Monday that he is on the “same page” with Penix and the medical team, and they feel good about Penix’s progress. “I think it’s important for us as coaches and organizations to understand that’s a case-by-case basis on how guys would be ready to play based on where they are in their own head, if you will,” Stefanski said. “When it comes to players, you can get cleared for 11 on 11, or you’re cleared for a game, but then you have to be able to do your job.” And that seems to be the issue for Michael Penix Jr., who repeated a couple of times that his teammates deserve the best version of him as a starting quarterback. Penix has plenty of experience returning from injury, and that experience has informed his approach to returning to the field this time around. “I’ve been in the position where I did rush back and I didn’t feel confident, and I didn’t play good and it didn’t look good. So it’s like, I know whenever I do step on that football field, I want to be 100% for this team,” Penix said. I mentioned this in my reporting from Monday’s practice , but I believe we could see Penix take over as the starter as early as Week 4 against the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football . The previous week, the Falcons will take on the Packers at Lambeau on Thursday Night Football , and that little mini-bye after the Thursday Night game might be a perfect opportunity to make a change. Of course, the NFL season is full of surprises, so who knows. Maybe Tua comes out and plays like a future Hall of Famer against the Steelers. The Falcons may have a tough time making a move if Tua’s playing lights out. But barring any extraordinary play from Tua or any setbacks for Penix, in my opinion, that’s the earliest we could see Penix take over as the Falcons’ starter. Is that possible for Penix physically? He said a few times on Monday he’s “very close” to being ready, but he doesn’t want to put a timetable on it. If he’s feeling any pressure to solidify his spot as the team’s franchise quarterback this season, he’s keeping that to himself. “It’s not about having a big year for me,” he said. “You know, it’s mainly about, I want to be able to give this organization, this team 100%. And if I feel like I can’t do that, that’s not fair for them. And I love this organization, and I want to make sure that whenever I do step out on the field, I’m ready.” Penix will be inactive for this week’s matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, per Stefanski. Tua Tagovailoa will start, and Cooper Rush will be the team’s backup.

title: Tua Tagovailoa named Falcons’ starting QB for Week 1 vs. Steelers
summary: The biggest question facing the 2026 Atlanta Falcons has been answered. On Monday, the Falcons announced that Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with the Falcons this offseason after being released by the Miami Dolphins, has been named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Falcons’ quarterback situation has been a roller-coaster ride […]
full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) reacts as he exits the field after the game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The biggest question facing the 2026 Atlanta Falcons has been answered. On Monday, the Falcons announced that Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with the Falcons this offseason after being released by the Miami Dolphins, has been named the starter for Week 1 against the Steelers in Pittsburgh . The Falcons’ quarterback situation has been a roller-coaster ride since the first day of training camp — and not a particularly fun one. On Day 1 of camp, the team announced that Trevor Siemian had been released with an injury settlement; Tua Tagovailoa would not be participating in practice due to some lower back stiffness; and the team was signing QB Cooper Rush. Michael Penix Jr. wasn’t medically cleared until the final week of training camp, so that left Rush and rookie undrafted free agent Jack Strand to participate in that first practice. Stefanski declined to name a starter throughout the preseason, even though Penix’s medical clearance came so late in the process that he was unable to take any preseason game snaps. And Tua’s preseason performance didn’t necessarily enthuse fans. He completed 3 of 5 attempts for 22 yards, zero touchdowns, and zero picks in Week 1 of the preseason against the Broncos, sat out Week 2 (this was always Stefanski’s plan, to let the starters take most of the joint practice reps with the Colts and sit out that preseason game), and went 7 of 8 for 95 yards, no touchdowns, no picks, and one absurd botched snap that turned into a fumble and kind of overshadowed the rest of his performance. But I have concerns about whether or not Michael Penix is ready, after basically three days of full practice, to play an entire NFL game. I do believe, based on what Penix has said about it, he’s past the mental aspect of his recovery, and I trust that he’s physically healthy. I worry that his lack of contact leading up to Week 1 could lead to a different injury altogether, or that the lack of contact and full-speed practice or preseason action has him unprepared for the speed of the regular-game. And that’s not to suggest there aren’t injury concerns with Tua. His concussion history worries me — not because of football, but for the sake of his long-term health and well being. But he has gotten most of the meaningful work this preseason with the starters, he has participated fully in padded practices, joint practices, and the preseason, and it stands to reason that he is more prepared — through no fault of Penix’s, just because of the timing of his medical clearance — to be the Week 1 starter. Tua spent the first six seasons of his career with the Miami Dolphins, who drafted him with the fifth overall pick out of Alabama in the 2020 NFL Draft. He has a 68% completion percentage over his NFL career, throwing 120 touchdowns against 59 interceptions. He was released by the Dolphins in March 2026 after a 2025 season he finished with 2,660 yards, 20 touchdowns, 15 picks, and took 30 sacks. He was benched for the final three games of the season, and the Falcons took advantage of him being cut to sign him for an extremely affordable one-year deal. New head coach Kevin Stefanski and general manager Ian Cunningham saw him as competition and insurance for Penix, and now he is the starter. I don’t think this decision says anything about either Tua’s or Penix’s long-term future with the Falcons or as the starter. There’s a lot of football to be played before I’ll have an opinion about that. But I do think it’s Tua’s job to lose. If he goes out there and balls out, it would be silly to sit him. If he doesn’t, though, it likely won’t be long before Penix is ready to step in. Can the 2026 version of Tua Tagovailoa do that, and stay healthy? That’s now one of the biggest questions facing the 2026 Falcons now.

title: Dark horse Jovaughn Gwyn wins Ravens’ Week 1 starting center job
summary: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jovaughn Gwyn would start at center for the 2026 regular-season opener against the Indianapolis Colts. “ I would say that’s a Week 1 decision — not necessarily a permanent decision,” Minter added, noting that former Browns starter Ethan Pocic was “still coming back” from a torn Achilles […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens guard Jovaughn Gwyn (54) warms up before the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jovaughn Gwyn would start at center for the 2026 regular-season opener against the Indianapolis Colts. “ I would say that’s a Week 1 decision — not necessarily a permanent decision,” Minter added, noting that former Browns starter Ethan Pocic was “still coming back” from a torn Achilles suffered last December. Gwyn, 27, will now make his first career start against the Colts’ ferocious defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart. This will be an early test for offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s new scheme and quarterback Lamar Jackson’s command of it at the line of scrimmage. The Ravens’ starting center competition was one of the team’s biggest offseason storylines following Tyler Linderbaum’s departure in free agency. Gwyn was seen as a dark horse after spending three years in Atlanta with offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford, who had a loud voice in The Castle this offseason. Former Colts backup Danny Pinter seemed to take an early lead in spring practices, and Pocic’s arrival in July threatened to push Gwyn to the third string once he was healthy. But Gwyn’s standout performance in the Ravens’ first preseason game against the Eagles and Pinter’s season-ending knee injury during joint practices in Minnesota propelled him into the first team. Pocic still got plenty of playing time across the last two preseason games, but he never did enough to displace Gwyn. Minter’s comments also indicate that Pocic is not back at 100% and could factor into the picture later in the season. Gwyn could preempt that with a strong start to the year, especially against such stiff competition. Beyond blocking Buckner and Stewart, he will have to cover all of the mental aspects of the center position. His ability to read the defense and communicate the calls in partnership with Jackson at the line of scrimmage will be crucial. The Ravens’ decision is another sign of Ledford’s influence within the organization. The team declined to trade up for a center on Day 2 or select one of the several Power Four starters who were available on Day 3, instead trusting their new offensive line coach to coach up one of their other options. Among them was Gwyn, a 2023 seventh-round pick out of South Carolina who Ledford developed in Atlanta and brought with him to Baltimore this offseason. Gwyn stayed on the Falcons’ practice squad for two years before earning the backup center job in 2025. Early struggles from Gwyn would be a significant problem for the Ravens offense. They would also offer a glimpse at Minter’s in-season management style. Would he be quick to replace Gwyn with Pocic, or would he fall into the past regime’s frustrating pattern of leaving subpar blockers on the field for far too long? The new head coach has preached standards and accountability since he arrived in Baltimore; that would be a chance to practice them. The Ravens, of course, will be hoping that situation never comes up. It is worth noting that Gwyn is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason – as is Pocic – so Minter’s mention of a non-permanent decision also (perhaps inadvertently) references the team’s lack of a long-term at the center position. But for at least one week, it will be Gwyn snapping the ball to Jackson when the Ravens offense takes the field.

title: Ravens discussion: who is flying under the radar heading into Week 1?
summary: This offseason, the Baltimore Ravens rebuilt the interior of their offensive line and retooled their pass rush – and turned over virtually their entire coaching staff. Over the past few months, those coaches have installed an entirely new offensive scheme while drilling down on the details on defense. Young playmakers like Ja’Kobi Lane and Mike Green […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 23: Travis Jones #98 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field prior to an NFL football game against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images This offseason, the Baltimore Ravens rebuilt the interior of their offensive line and retooled their pass rush – and turned over virtually their entire coaching staff. Over the past few months, those coaches have installed an entirely new offensive scheme while drilling down on the details on defense. Young playmakers like Ja’Kobi Lane and Mike Green turned heads in training camp, while undrafted gems Joe Fagnano and Ethan Burke impressed enough in the preseason to enter the roster spot. But with Week 1 right around the corner, it’s time to look away from the headlines and the highlights and talk about some Ravens who are flying under the radar heading into the regular season. Nikhil’s take: Over the course of the preseason, every player gets talked about at some point. But discussions regarding Baltimore’s backfield focused on future Hall of Famer Derrick Henry, owner Steve Bisciotti’s personal draft pick Adam Randall, and on-the-bubble youngster Rasheen Ali. Lost in the conversation was veteran Justice Hill, who has been an afterthought this year after missing the second half of the 2025 season with a neck injury. But Hill has quietly averaged 4.8 yards per carry and 8.3 yards per reception since 2023 and is poised to continue serving as the Ravens’ third-down back this year. Henry will no doubt get the lion’s share of the work on the ground, but offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will likely give Hill opportunities on screens and isolation routes against linebackers. If the 28-year-old can remain efficient with his touches, protect Jackson in the pocket, and make plays when his number is called, he will be a key cog in the 2026 offense. On the other side of the ball, defensive tackle Travis Jones is simply not getting enough love. He was the Ravens’ second-best defender last year behind Kyle Hamilton and singlehandedly held the defensive line together whenever he was on the field. But with the arrival of Trey Hendrickson and the return of Nnamdi Madubuike, Baltimore’s more athletic, stat-stuffing edge rushers have been the main talking points. But Jones stands to benefit from the focus on his new teammates. If opposing offenses are more worried about the bigger names, they might leave Jones in 1-on-1 situations more often and hope their blocker can lose slowly before being overwhelmed. But the 26-year-old refined his pass rush repertoire after a few years in the league and should be able to collapse pockets consistently. Having Calais Campbell and Broderick Washington back in the fold will also ease Jones’ workload, which skyrocketed to a 70% defensive snap share and 889 total snaps last year. Now, it’s your turn! title: Ravens news: DT Nnamdi Madubuike could be ready for Week 1
summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In this week’s edition, we cover Nnamdi Madubuike’s return to full-team work in practice, landing spots for recent ex-Ravens, and media projections for the 2026 season. Let’s dive in! Nnamdi Madubuike nears return The Ravens were […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 7: Nnamdi Madubuike #92 of the Baltimore Ravens runs around the edge during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 07, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of all the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In this week’s edition, we cover Nnamdi Madubuike’s return to full-team work in practice, landing spots for recent ex-Ravens, and media projections for the 2026 season. Let’s dive in! Nnamdi Madubuike nears return The Ravens were extremely cautious with Nnamdi Madubuike’s ramp-up in training camp, holding him out of 11-on-11 work for the entire preseason. He did not even make contact with a sled until the week before the team’s last preseason game. But last week, the two-time Pro Bowler returned to full-team drills, a huge leap of progress that brings him one step closer to playing in a game. Ian Rapoport (Good Morning Football, NFL Network) I think it’s fair to say there was some doubt, especially heading into the offseason, on if he would play football again. Needed a procedure, needed it to go well, needed a lot of things to happen for him to be back on the field. And there he is, not only back on the field but doing individual drills and other such things for most of training camp. Now is in 11-on-11, a significant step, making you believe that Madubuike will be on the field when the season starts in Week 1 or shortly thereafter. It is impossible to overstate Madubuike’s potential impact on Baltimore’s defense. The defensive line virtually collapsed after he went down in 2025. His return, along with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, could vault the Ravens pass rush from the bottom of the league last year to the top this season. But his ability to stuff the run could be just as important in Jesse Minter’s new defense. 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – Ben Solak (ESPN) In 2023, Madubuike had 13 sacks at defensive tackle. Preposterous stuff. A comprehensive list of defensive tackles who had at least 13 sacks in a season over the past decade: Aaron Donald (twice) and Chris Jones (twice). That’s it… …Defensive tackle comes into even greater focus when you consider how often new head coach Jesse Minter runs light boxes (fifth-highest light-box rate in football last season). Strong defensive tackle play is a must for teams trying to fit the run from two-high shells, and next to Travis Jones, Madubuike can stuff early-down runs and get the defense to passing downs. There, a deeper bench of rushers can take some of the pressure off him. Former Ravens make career moves Linebacker Kyle Van Noy signs with Vikings on practice squad (ESPN) Van Noy, 35, played the past three seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. He followed up a career year in 2024 with one of his most disappointing seasons last year, struggling to generate consistent pressure. He finished his last campaign with just two sacks, ending a run of six straight seasons with at least five. But with the Vikings, he should provide some needed depth and experience at the edge rusher position, where Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner give Minnesota a dynamic set of starters, but the rest of the depth chart is largely unproven. Giants To Sign LB Malik Harrison – Adam La Rose (Pro Football Rumors) This deal will allow for a reunion between Harrison and head coach John Harbaugh after the two worked together in Baltimore from 2020-24. During that time, Harrison primarily contributed on special teams but he also logged 372 defensive snaps on defense during his final Ravens campaign. Upon arrival in Pittsburgh, the former third-rounder saw a career-high 40% defensive snap share while playing 11 games. Additionally, former Ravens tight end Qadir Ismail signed with the Bears’ practice squad. Evan Beerntsen, the team’s final draft pick this year (Round 7, No. 253 overall) worked out for the Raiders and the Seahawks, and kicker Justin Tucker had a tryout with the Jets. Media projections for the Ravens’ 2026 season AFC North Preview: Should You Believe in the Bengals? – Sheil Kapadia (The Ringer) The Super Bowl case here is straightforward: Jackson is healthy and thrives in the new offensive system. The offensive line overachieves. A young pass catcher like rookie Ja’Kobi Lane emerges as a quality second option. And Minter coaches the defense to a top-five level. I see a very good team, but the issues above give me pause. I see a team that can win in different ways. But I’m not sure I see an elite unit. I could get there with the offense if I trusted the offensive line or the pass catchers more. I could get there with the defense if I were confident in the pass rush. I like the Ravens as a wild-card team with a Super Bowl ceiling. But ultimately, I think that they probably need one more offseason to build up the roster. Projected record: 11-6 NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts – ESPN Best-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 13-4 Worst-case scenario for 2026, per FPI: 8-9 This season is a success if … the Ravens advance to at least the AFC Championship Game. Baltimore fired coach John Harbaugh because of a lack of deep playoff runs. The Ravens need to avoid quick exits under Jesse Minter. — [Jamison] Hensley One key fantasy nugget: With Jackson’s electric dual-threat ability and a play-action-heavy system under new coordinator Declan Doyle, the Ravens quarterback is primed to produce big numbers. Jackson completed a league-best 80% of his play-action throws last season. — [Matt] Bowen Bold prediction for 2026: The Ravens’ defense will rank in the top four in EPA per play. That’s a pretty big jump from last season, when it finished 16th. But in Minter’s first season with the Chargers, he took a defense that ranked 29th and brought it to seventh best. And Minter probably has more talent to work with in Baltimore. — [Seth] Walder Who Will Have the NFL’s Best Offense in 2026? – Anthony Dabbundo (The Ringer) 7. Baltimore Ravens You used to be able to ink Baltimore into the top five of any preseason offensive rankings, but the Ravens are entering this season with more questions than usual. They scored 40 points in a thrilling Week 1 loss to Buffalo last year, but for the rest of the season, Baltimore ranked only 13th in EPA per drive. Quarterback Lamar Jackson missed four games with a hamstring injury and never looked as explosive as a runner after returning. His 2025 pressure-to-sack rate was the highest of his career and one of the highest in the entire league. Will a healthier Jackson resemble his pre-2025 self? Or was last season’s decline in his rushing efficiency the beginning of an age-related trend? That question will become increasingly prevalent this season and beyond. Jackson’s mobility has always helped Baltimore’s line perform better than the sum of its parts, but having a less explosive version of him would place more pressure on the offensive line in protection and on Jackson to operate the traditional passing game. The uncertainty does not end there. The Ravens have to replace longtime center Tyler Linderbaum, who departed for Las Vegas, while Declan Doyle takes over for Todd Monken as offensive coordinator. This will be Doyle’s first time calling plays after spending last year working as OC under Ben Johnson in Chicago—so this will also be the first test of Johnson’s coaching tentacles. The Ravens still have a solid rushing infrastructure with Derrick Henry and one of the league’s most uniquely talented quarterbacks. But for the first time in years, ranking Baltimore among the NFL’s elite offenses requires projecting a rebound rather than relying on recent evidence. Join the conversation! title: Buffalo Bills must be prepared for this unique characteristic of Texans defense
summary: The Houston Texans aren’t an exotic defense. They don’t utilize creativity get to the quarterback on a regular basis. It’s probably the NFL’s most straight-forward, pin-your-ears-back defensive scheme. That is not to say the Bills can scrap the gameplanning portion of this week for what their offense will see across the line of scrimmage on […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball and scores a touchdown during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans aren’t an exotic defense. They don’t utilize creativity get to the quarterback on a regular basis. It’s probably the NFL’s most straight-forward, pin-your-ears-back defensive scheme. That is not to say the Bills can scrap the gameplanning portion of this week for what their offense will see across the line of scrimmage on a play-to-play basis in Week 1. It’s to suggest their strategy for attacking Houston’s vaunted defense needs to be anchored in not expecting extra rushers being sent toward Josh Allen. Last season, the Texans had the lowest blitz rate in all of football, at just 16.7%, yet finished seventh with a pressure rate of 40.3%, per Fantasy Points Data — a dream scenario for any defensive coordinator. That combination was integral to that unit’s excellence. And Houston was able to essentially duplicate those magical percentages in the game against the Bills in Week 12 last year. In that victory, the Texans blitzed Allen on just 15.2% of his 39 drop backs and still managed to pressure him 43.5% of the time. Seven of his eight sacks came without a blitz! That has to be exceptionally rare in the NFL. And check the difference for Allen in that game, split by when he was blitzed and not blitzed. Josh Allen vs. Texans in 2025 Completions / Attempts Yards (YPA) TD / INT Rating Not Blitzed 19 / 28 186 (6.6) 0 / 2 56.5 Blitzed 5 / 6 67 (11.2) 0 / 0 113.2 Of course, Spencer Brown and Dion Dawkins were dinged in that contest. The former toughed it out but clearly was not himself, and Dawkins left the game for a long stretch, which led to 17 relief-appearance snaps for Ryan Van Demark. Dalton Kincaid didn’t play due to that knee injury. There was no Keon Coleman. Also, Allen dropped back to pass on 28 of 39 plays in the second half, an aerial-centric attack I’d normally advocate for, but such telegraphing in that particular game felt far from ideal. Heck, Joe Brady even admitted to a less-than-stellar play-calling job after the defeat. But it’s not as though Allen — and Brady — regularly struggled against teams that played coverage against the Bills offense and held back on blitzing. Even with this Week 12 performance included, Allen’s 105.4 quarterback rating against no-blitz plays from opposing defenses ranked third-best in the entire NFL among qualifying passers. If that game is removed, that rating jumped to 110.4, quite naturally. As a longtime Bills pass-game pusher, particularly due to Allen’s presence, it’s somewhat unorthodox for me to advocate for the run game. Then again, it’s not lost on me that James Cook is the league’s reigning rushing champion, and in the first half of that Week 12 outing a season ago, he had 71 yards on seven carries including a 45-yard touchdown run. More Cook in this game — probably a smart idea for the Bills, because he’s clearly one of the league’s most explosive offensive weapons, and his continued usage keeps Houston’s pass rush honest. Limiting the Texans duo of Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter is, of course, vital to beating this AFC South team. Buffalo has preached the “they have to play us” mentality all offseason, and playing the Bills is dealing with Allen, his assembly of pass catchers… and Cook. We’ll see if Brady learned his lesson schematically from last year’s contest. How do you think the Bills should handle the Texans minimal-blitzing defense?

title: Football-tangential things to look forward to during the 2026 NFL regular season
summary: Football is awesome. You’re likely not reading this if you don’t think football is awesome. The most casual of observers don’t come to SB Nation sites and click on stories to read on a random weekday. Thus, I’m not telling you anything you don’t already know. But it’s not just the actual sport of football, […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 22: Buffalo Bills fans tailgate in the parking lot prior to the AFC Divisional Playoff game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on January 22, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is awesome. You’re likely not reading this if you don’t think football is awesome. The most casual of observers don’t come to SB Nation sites and click on stories to read on a random weekday. Thus, I’m not telling you anything you don’t already know. But it’s not just the actual sport of football, played between whistles, that makes us love football so much. It’s all the phenomena that are football-related that add to our enjoyment of the season that always seemed too short. First, I would encourage you to share the non-football events, moments, or traditions that make the sport’s 18+ weeks so much fun for you in the comments below (maybe someone can pick up an enjoyable idea). Secondly, I’ll share some of mine here: Food I strongly ascribe to the belief that traditional food calendars should not influence your culinary choices. If you want stew on a hot summer day, you should have it. If it’s the dead of winter and you want some ice cream, get some ice cream. Whether it’s a usually-prepared “summer food” or not should not stop you from enjoying it. When it’s considered seasonally appropriate, who knows if it’ll hit the spot then? I will not be oppressed by the tyranny of the fictitious food calendar! That being said, certain people and restaurants do not ascribe to my progressive culinary thinking. Because of that, my food options are sometimes slightly limited by what the person or establishment deems appropriate for the season, and that exclusion stops now. If I was a pumpkin spice person like my wife (to complete the ensemble with the Ugg boots and leggings), I’d be blocked off from getting it until the Starbucks overlords deemed appropriate to bless the peasants with that overly-nutmegged (that’s totally a word) liquid concoction. So I’m excited for the new wing flavors. I’m excited for all the caramel apple desserts. I’m excited for my local shop to start offering their pumpkin rolls again. As long as I’m forced to live in a society that doesn’t let me have the easiest access to apple fritters in June, I’ll be grateful for the return of some elite-tier foods. Hoodies Much like my above take on food, I’m a “wear what you want, when you want”-kind of guy… …but you know, the weather and stuff. As long as you live in the Northern Hemisphere, fall and winter are cooler than summer. How much cooler depends on your location, but for a lot of people, American football season (and the immediate aftermath) is the only time they can wear a hooded sweatshirt outside their house without it quickly serving as an inadvertent sauna suit. The joy of this article of clothing is also related to the first point identified above, as the magic of the hoodie allows for a few extra fall pounds to be packed onto a human body secretly, well hidden by the sweatshirt until which time as the spring comes and we begin to slightly regret our football-related consumption choices. Insane Radio Callers Maybe the Bills should play Josh Allen at linebacker. Maybe Aaron Kromer should have been made the head coach. Win or lose, the people who call into stations like WGR 550 or 97 Rock (the new Buffalo Bills flagship station) immediately post-game can provide some of the most unhinged and galaxy-brained ideas and takes that anyone sober could ever truly appreciate. No matter what you believe to be the most relevant issues surrounding the team after a regular season or playoff game, the hard left and right turns provided to you by some of the individuals who call into the post-game radio shows make the programs must-listen simply for the entertainment value of their takes alone, completely apart from the competence of the radio hosts themselves. Tailgating stories I don’t typically go to Bills games. I went to the first football game ever played in the new Highmark Stadium when Buffalo took on the Carolina Panthers in the preseason, but I hadn’t been in years prior to that and likely won’t go again for a while. But even I love the adventures that can only come from Bills tailgating. Throwing the football with strangers who become friends over some grilled food, irresponsibly jumping into tables, spraying ketchup and mustard all over yourself (for some reason I still haven’t quite figured out)…it all makes for adventures and stories that people can tell each other for years to come. It’s part of the quintessential Buffalo football experience. Other sports try it, other teams try it, but there’s something special about it specifically for members of Bills Mafia. I smile every time the TV feed shows people who have obviously been tailgating for hours or ever days prior to the game, and I root for all y’all to have an excellent, yet safe, time. Social media gameday traditions Brother Bill (@TheeBrotherBill on Twitter) announced recently that his famous gameday morning opponent-specific videos (set to the tune of “Seven Nation Army” by the White Stripes) would be discontinued after seven years of providing laughs and coffee-beers to the member of Bills Mafia on social media, but other traditions remain. Greg Tompsett of Cover 1 (@GregTompsett) will still attempt to make the perfect steak the night before the game to “earn the right to win”. His teammate Aaron Quinn (@AaronQuinn716) will still post his breakfast sandwiches. I will still type out the word “I hope the Bills win today” and post it every game day (I’ll chuckle when I do it). Traditions, even the tiniest ones, help create a shared community. And for Bills fans all over the globe who can’t be physically in each other’s presence like the tailgaters mentioned above, social media and websites like Buffalo Rumblings can help provide a venue for that community. I love that football is back. But I love all the other little things that come alongside our beloved sport. Let’s do all of it together once again. …and that’s the way the cookie crumbles. I’m Bruce Nolan with Buffalo Rumblings. You can find me on Twitter and Instagram @BruceExclusive and look for new episodes of “The Bruce Exclusive” every Thursday on the Rumblings Cast Network — see more in my LinkTree!

title: Bills news: Thoughts on Buffalo’s chances of succeeding in Joe Brady’s first year
summary: The Buffalo Bills could have cleaned house entirely following last year’s disappointing AFC Divisional Round playoff loss to the Denver Broncos, but instead of bringing in an outside voice to lead Josh Allen and the Bills, Terry Pegula decided to promote Brandon Beane and elevate Joe Brady from offensive coordinator to head coach. So far […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 15: Dee Alford #23 of the Buffalo Bills makes his way to the field before a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers at Highmark Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills could have cleaned house entirely following last year’s disappointing AFC Divisional Round playoff loss to the Denver Broncos, but instead of bringing in an outside voice to lead Josh Allen and the Bills, Terry Pegula decided to promote Brandon Beane and elevate Joe Brady from offensive coordinator to head coach. So far through his first offseason, Brady seems to have earned high marks for how he has coached the Bills, but the real test of his mettle as head coach comes when the Bills kick off the 2026 NFL season on the road against the Houston Texans on Sunday, Sept. 13. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by exploring whether Brady can be successful and whether Beane has surrounded Brady with enough player and coaching talent to lead the Bills to that elusive Super Bowl title. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts in the comments section.
