title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 6
summary: It is Day 6 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: WASHINGTON, D.C. - CIRCA 1980's: Wide Receiver Drew Pearson #88 of the Dallas Cowboys catching pass in pre game warm-up before an NFL football game circa 1980's against the Washington Redskins at RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C.. Pearson played for the Cowboys from 1973-83. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 6 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Things really heat up now as we reach Day 6 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a play so significant that its nickname became permanent football language. With Dallas trailing Minnesota and its season only seconds from ending, Roger Staubach launched a desperate pass toward Drew Pearson. The “Hail Mary” was officially born. Sunday, December 28, 1975 — 2:00 p.m. ET Metropolitan Stadium, Bloomington, Minnesota Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, Minnesota Vikings 14 Dallas, a 10-4 wild-card team, faced one of the league’s strongest opponents, Minnesota. Minnesota had gone 12-2, boasting the NFC’s best record and featuring league MVP Fran Tarkenton. Their defense, which allowed the fewest yards in football, made life extremely difficult for Staubach and the Cowboys throughout the afternoon. The first half was dominated by defense. Minnesota eventually received a huge break when a punt bounced near Cliff Harris. Dallas lineman Pat Donovan attempted to recover it, but the loose ball escaped him, allowing Minnesota to recover at the Cowboys’ four-yard line. Chuck Foreman scored from one yard out shortly after, giving the Vikings a 7-0 lead that held through halftime. Dallas finally produced a sustained drive after the break. A late-hit penalty following a Preston Pearson reception helped move the Cowboys downfield before Doug Dennison scored on a four-yard run to tie the game. Toni Fritsch then kicked a 24-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter, putting Dallas ahead 10-7. Minnesota responded with its best offensive possession of the game. Tarkenton directed an 11-play, 70-yard drive before Brent McClanahan powered across from one yard with 5:24 remaining. The Vikings had regained a 14-10 lead, and after Dallas went three-and-out on its next possession, Minnesota appeared capable of simply running out the clock. With the Cowboys defense providing a final chance, Minnesota faced third-and-two before the two-minute warning. They attempted to keep the ball in Tarkenton’s hands, but Charlie Waters broke through Foreman’s block and dropped the quarterback for a three-yard loss. This forced the Vikings to punt, and Dallas took possession at their own 15 with 1:51 remaining and no timeouts. The final drive nearly ended before the famous play ever happened. After moving the ball to the Dallas 31, Staubach mishandled a low shotgun snap and lost eight yards. The Cowboys eventually faced fourth-and-16, when Staubach found Pearson near the sideline for 25 yards. After an incompletion, Dallas had time for one desperate shot. Staubach dropped back, pump-faked and launched deep down the right sideline toward Pearson. The pass came down around the Minnesota five as Pearson and Wright made contact. Wright fell, Pearson secured the underthrown football against his body and ran untouched into the end zone for a 50-yard touchdown with 24 seconds remaining. No offensive pass interference was called, despite furious protests from the Vikings. Afterward, Staubach explained that he had closed his eyes and said a “Hail Mary” after releasing the football. Staubach’s description of the play helped transform Hail Mary into the universally understood football term for a last-chance desperation pass. This game belongs near the very top of the countdown because its influence extends beyond Cowboys history. Dallas did not simply win an extraordinary playoff game, Staubach and Pearson created a moment whose name became shorthand throughout the sport. Every time a quarterback launches one final desperation pass toward the end zone, the connection between number 12 and number 88 lives on. #Cowboys vs #Vikings 1975 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 17, Minnesota Vikings 14 The Hail Mary #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/ILdF9sgDos — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 7, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Pearson entered Dallas’ final possession without a reception and then caught four passes for 91 yards on the winning drive. title: 3 reasons the Cowboys offseason feels different
summary: [Ed Note]: Greetings BTB! We have a new writer joining us today – Dyllan Rivers. It’s possible you’ve already encountered him on twitter as @Lord_Dylly with his recent of coverage training camp. He also runs a YouTube Cowboys channel which we recommend. Help us welcome him aboard at BTB. —- Dave Halprin We’ve had this […]
full_text: [Ed Note]: Greetings BTB! We have a new writer joining us today – Dyllan Rivers. It’s possible you’ve already encountered him on twitter as @Lord_Dylly with his recent of coverage training camp. He also runs a YouTube Cowboys channel which we recommend. Help us welcome him aboard at BTB. —- Dave Halprin We’ve had this feeling before as fans: pure excitement over the potential of the Dallas Cowboys heading into a season. However, through the excitement, we’ve grown callous to the idea that the team really could win it all. Regardless of outcome, though, this year has already been different. Here are three reasons why. Front office evolution Since August 28th, 2025, this front office has been obsessed with proving they were right to trade away Micah Parsons. The moves since that day are the things Cowboys fans across the world have dreamed of for years. They traded away picks to finally address the defensive interior. They actually signed a big-ticket player (a safety nonetheless) in free agency. These are not moves that fans are accustomed to seeing from the Jones family. Moving on from the All-Pro edge has created a sense of urgency that’s been foreign to the organization for far too long. Organizational harmony All of the changes that this organization has made over the last year are puzzle pieces designed to fit into the larger board. Nobody is throwing spaghetti on the walls in this house. Every move has been intentional. Can’t stop the run? Get rid of lackluster run defenders while acquiring Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Otito Ogbonnia to plug the holes. Need to fix the secondary? How about filling the defensive coordinator position with Christian Parker: the man who played a massive role in flipping the Eagles pass defense from 30th to 1st in just a single season (2024). And while they were at it, they went and traded up a spot to select arguably the best player in the draft to run his new defense. Every single move fits together in perfect harmony. The results should be immediate and tangible. Schottenheimer holds the reins When this team needed a new head coach in the post-Mike McCarthy era, the front office looked no further than a few doors down to quickly hire Brian Schottenheimer. When this team needed to hire a new defensive coordinator, the front office looked to an old friend in Matt Eberflus. Seemingly very little work was involved in these decisions. But when the Cowboys needed a new defensive coordinator in 2026, Schottenheimer and the front office took 16 days and interviewed nine candidates, then narrowed that down into a second round before finally landing on Christian Parker. That is a stark contrast in how this team has operated in years prior. This is a serious culture shift that has permeated through the entire organization, top-down. We have Brian Schottenheimer to thank for that. Adding it up Taken together, the decisions this organization has made have built a team that should, with just one year of rebuilding, compete with the best in the NFC. The NFL is a week-to-week league. Many things can change in just a short period of time. But the Cowboys have put themselves in a terrific position with top-shelf starters on offense, a completely revamped defense, and the best depth we’ve seen in years. Pair that with a coaching staff that understands what it takes to win in the modern NFL, and they’ve got something cooking Where this season ends is yet to be written in the history books. Could this actually be the season that finally ends differently from the rest? The Cowboys seem to have as good a shot as anyone. After all, “different” has been their theme all along.

title: One fantasy football nugget for each NFL team
summary: It’s a new season. A clean slate. A time to wipe away all those fantasy mistakes you made a year ago… and make all new ones this year! Well, hopefully not. Fantasy football is a great way to showcase your football expertise and GM your own team, but to do that, you have to be […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 13: Jeremiyah Love #4 of the Arizona Cardinals runs against Hezekiah Masses #35 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a preseason game at Allegiant Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Cardinals defeated the Raiders 27-14. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a new season. A clean slate. A time to wipe away all those fantasy mistakes you made a year ago… and make all new ones this year! Well, hopefully not. Fantasy football is a great way to showcase your football expertise and GM your own team, but to do that, you have to be equipped with the right information. That’s exactly what we have for you today, as we’ll provide one fantasy nugget for every NFL team. ARIZONA CARDINALS – Players selected third overall aren’t thrown into committee roles. Volume and dynamic ability are fantasy gold, and rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has both. ATLANTA FALCONS – Tua Tagovailoa’s short passes created the volume to help Devin Achane go from good to great. TE Kyle Pitts will be the receiving beneficiary of those dump-offs. BALTIMORE RAVENS – WR Zay Flowers quietly finished as the WR7 despite only catching five touchdown passes. There is no reason to not expect another top-10 finish. BUFFALO BILLS – Nothing is finer than being the workhorse back on a run-heavy team that scores often, and that is what RB James Cook III is. CAROLINA PANTHERS – The Panthers used a second-round draft pick on RB Jonathan Brooks. He’s finally healthy, and Carolina has a strong rushing attack. CINCINNATI BENGALS – WR Tee Higgins continues to be the best-bargain receiver who possesses both a safe floor and high upside should JaMarr Chase miss time. CLEVELAND BROWNS – Rookie TE Harold Fannin Jr. had the fifth-highest targets of his position, and there is no reason not to expect continued volume. DALLAS COWBOYS – Over the last six years, Dak Prescott has alternated between a top fantasy quarterback and an injured quarterback. Last year, he finished as QB5. Grab’em if you love him, but make sure you have a Dak-up plan. DENVER BRONCOS – WR Courtland Sutton is coming off of two-straight top-13 finishes and already has chemistry with Bo Nix. He’s the value pick while everyone else is chasing Jaylen Waddle. DETROIT LIONS – QB Jared Goff is the best-kept fantasy secret. He’s efficient, plays most of his games in a dome, has weapons galore, and a defense just bad enough to sustain scoring-friendly game scripts. He has three straight top-10 finishes. GREEN BAY PACKERS – WR Christian Watson has never finished inside the top 25 for WRs, and his target competition is Jayden Reed, Mathew Golden, and Tyler Kraft. Avoid the hype. HOUSTON TEXAS – Only three WRs have finished in the top 10 in points per game in each of the last three seasons – Puka Nacua, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Nico Collins. INDIANAPOLIS COLTS – K Spencer Shrader is the new Brandon Aubrey. Use your last pick on him. JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS – QB Trevor Lawrence has a plethora of weapons and a great offensive coordinator. Expect another strong fantasy season from him. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS – Expectations are big for Kenneth Walker as he walks into an ideal situation, but Andy Reid spreads the ball around. Only once over the last decade (2017, Kareem Hunt) have the Chiefs had a RB finish in the top 10. LOS ANGELES CHARGERS – WR Ladd McConkey finished as WR12 his rookie year, but then what happened? Keenan Allen happened, but he’s really gone this time. Expect a return to stardom for this young Ladd. LOS ANGELES RAMS – Even with a 65/35 timeshare, Kyren Williams is a fantasy gem. He has three-straight top-10 finishes despite Blake Corum already being there to “steal” his volume. He’s the cheapest RB2 you’ll find in the draft. LAS VEGAS RAIDERS – QB Fernando Mendoza will be all the craze in Vegas at some point this year. If your roster space allows, stash this playmaking quarterback. MIAMI DOLPHINS – The Dolphins offense has been abysmal the last two seasons, and it is astounding that De’Vone Achane has finished as a top-6 RB in each of them. But he has. His volume and elusiveness won’t change. Pounce if he slides. MINNESOTA VIKINGS – Remember when Justin Jefferson was a consensus top-3 WR? Well, that time is now as long as J.J. McCarthy is not in charge of throwing him the ball. NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS – WR A.J. Brown has never had a quarterback this good. Huge season loading… NEW ORLEANS SAINTS – There are so many good eats on Kellen Moore’s offense, but TE Juwan Johnson finished third in receiving yards for tight ends. He only had three touchdowns, but still finished in the top 10 for TEs. Had he caught three more touchdowns, he would have finished as TE3 for the year. Sleeper potential. NEW YORK GIANTS – QB Jaxson Dart has top-5 upside, but also could come with weekly high variance. If you roll the dice on him, package him with a stable QB you can find at a low cost (see Detroit Lions). NEW YORK JETS – WR Garrett Wilson is the most blah fantasy receiver out there. His upside is capped by a bad Jets offense, but his volume is continuous. The Geno upgrade should help him retain a WR2 finish. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES – Regression to the mean bodes well for RB Saquon Barkley, but wear and tear is a real thing. If you must venture down that aisle, handcuff him to Tank Bigsby, who enters RB1 territory should Barkley go down. PITTSBURGH STEELERS – QB Aaron Rodgers’ arm is spaghetti, so expect a lot of dump-off passes to running backs. This is good news for sneaky receiving RB Jaylen Warren. SEATTLE SEAHAWKS – Rookie RB Jadarian Price walks into a great opportunity after the departure of Walker and the often-injured Zach Charbonett SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS – RB Christian McCaffrey has finished as the best fantasy running back twice over the last three years. If you can stomach the risk, he delivers big rewards. TAMPA BAY BUCANNEERS – Don’t let recency bias make you sleep on RB Bucky Irving. He’s healthy now, and his volume, shiftiness, and usage as a receiver make him a valuable commodity. TENNESSEE TITANS – I love rookie first-round receivers from Ohio State, and you should too, but the WanDale Robinson fella might be one of fantasy’s best-kept secrets. He’s not a league winner, but an effective depth guy that you can snag at the end of your draft. WASHINGTON COMMANDERS – QB Jayden Daniels was a fantasy gem when he could run and he could stay healthy. Now, it feels like you can only have one or the other. Buyer beware.

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The countdown to the start of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys season is in the home stretch, and we have just one NFC opponent left to preview in this ongoing series that will lead right up to that first Sunday Night Football test at the New York Giants. That team would be the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - DECEMBER 22: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers scrambles out of the pocket during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on December 22, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The countdown to the start of the 2026 Dallas Cowboys season is in the home stretch, and we have just one NFC opponent left to preview in this ongoing series that will lead right up to that first Sunday Night Football test at the New York Giants. That team would be the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who like the Cowboys were on the outside of the playoff picture looking in last season. Last season was the first time the Bucs did not make the playoffs under Todd Bowles, and the first time in five straight seasons. Continuity on offense, including Baker Mayfield, with young receivers expected to take a leap and a retooled defense will give Tampa Bay hope of reclaiming this division yet again, though it’s a division where all three other teams should and will feel confident about their own chances as well. Let’s take a closer look at what the Buccaneers have done this offseason. Buccaneers Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY LB Alex Anzalone RB Kenneth Gainwell QB Jake Browning SAF Miles Killebrew G Dan Feeney (Re-signed) TE Cade Otton (Re-signed) DL A’Shawn Robinson LB Al-Quadin Muhammad * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY QB Teddy Bridgewater CB Jamel Dean WR Mike Evans RB Rachaad White The Buccaneers lost a future Hall of Fame wide receiver and face of the franchise player in Mike Evans this offseason when he chose the San Francisco 49ers in free agency. Evans was third on the team in targets in 2025, behind rookie Emeka Egbuka and tight end Cade Otton, who was brought back this offseason. This is an offense that will also be looking for more contributions from Jalen McMillan, Chris Godwin Jr., Tez Johnson, and a rookie “pet cat” of many draft observers, Ted Hurst. In the backfield, the team’s new complementary back to Bucky Irving is Kenneth Gainwell, coming over from the Steelers to replace Rachaad White. Gainwell and Irving both have big play potential as runners or pass catchers, and if the Bucs have a more consistent downfield pass game in 2026, watch out for what these backs can bring between the tackles to make this a more imposing offense as well. With a more balanced offensive approach and work done in the offseason to be quicker in the front seven with more pass rush juice, the Bucs will be looking for better close game outcomes to potentially take a massive leap in the win column. Alex Anzalone and A’Shawn Robinson are key additions to this front seven, along with first round pick Rueben Bain out of nearby Miami, which brings us to the rest of what the Bucs did in April’s draft. Buccaneers 2026 Draft Class Round 1, Pick 15: EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. Round 2, Pick 14 (46 Overall): LB Josiah Trotter Round 3, Pick 20 (84 Overall): WR Ted Hurst III Round 4, Pick 16 (116 Overall): CB Keionte Scott Round 5, Pick 15 (155 Overall): DT Demonte Capehart Round 5, Pick 20 (160 Overall): G Billy Schrauth Round 6, Pick 4 (185 Overall): TE Bauer Sharp The Bucs landed not one, but two Miami Hurricane defenders that were a part of a team that went to the national championship game in their home stadium, Bain and cornerback Keionte Scott. With a defensive tackle group that just added Robinson to pair with Calijah Kancey and Vita Vea, Bain is stepping into an ideal situation to win one-on-ones off the edge. How his consistent ability to do this in college would translate to the next level was hotly debated all spring, but Bain can certainly be an impact player very early on to watch as the Bucs try to get back to a higher standard on defense. Keionte Scott is a true nickel cornerback that feels like a natural fit in Bowles’ coverage scheme, while linebacker Josiah Trotter can slot in next to the freshly-signed Anzalone to develop as a rookie. The Bucs did a great job adding draft picks at positions they already have established talent and experience, giving them healthy depth and a chance to be more of a threat deeper into the season. Buccaneers 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson Passing Game Coordinator T.J. Yates Special Teams Coordinator Danny Smith Defensive Line Marcus West Quarterbacks Chandler Whitmer A concept that Cowboys fans are familiar with when it comes to the upside of hiring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker strongly applies to the Bucs coaching changes this offseason as well, and that is the added benefit of pulling a coach away from a division rival. Tampa Bay took this to an almost extreme level, nabbing offensive coordinator Zac Robinson away from the Atlanta Falcons, T.J. Yates from the Falcons, and adding QB coach Chandler Whitmer, who’s last NFL job was in 2024 – also with the Falcons. The Bucs and Falcons have played six straight one score games against one another, with the Bucs winning four of them, and these teams splitting last season. Atlanta is not expected to be very prolific on offense this season, and stealing assistants away on this side of the ball to create another situation for new Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski to navigate is well done if you’re a fan of the swashbucklers. Robinson’s best trait as an OC is his ability to scheme receivers open on the perimeter, something the Bucs need more consistency in as they evaluate this season if Mayfield will be the guy beyond 2025. Working alongside former longtime QB T.J. Yates as passing game coordinator and Whitmer as Mayfield’s latest QB coach gives the Bucs, on paper, a very strong brain trust around this offense that carries big expectations at the moment. Whitmer’s most recent stop is arguably the best résumé builder any coach coming from college to the NFL has ever had, being the QB coach and co-offensive coordinator for Fernando Mendoza and Indiana, who became the first number one overall pick out of Indiana after winning the school’s first national championship which capped an undefeated season – of course also a first for that program. NFL fans at large are familiar with the edge Mayfield plays with when feeling doubted or disrespected in any way, and although that angle comes from his own front office this time around, it very may still work to unlock the best of Baker in 2026, with coaching being a huge part of this equation too. Depending on how malleable the Bucs defense is under Bowles who will need to show adjustments as his time in the league passes the quarter century mark this season, this is a team with strong coaching continuity elsewhere and many reasons to believe in their ability to contend yet again. One of the best thing the defense appears built to do is limit big plays through the air, something they can exploit further with their own vertical pass offense, but how they match up physically against the run is a question mark. The Cowboys will take on this Bucs defense at home in primetime on a short week, immediately following a road test against the tough Houston Texans defense in week four. The last time these teams met in primetime was also in Arlington, with a 6-8 Cowboys team out of the playoff picture giving an inspired December performance in what proved to be the third to last game of the Mike McCarthy tenure. Dallas won 26-24, their last win of that season. It hardly feels like a rivalry, but all of the recent Buccaneers and Cowboys meetings have had some interesting raised stakes, and although the 2026 meeting comes early, it should feel no different on Thursday Night Football . This game is the start of a stretch for HC Brian Schottenheimer in year two where he will go up against very experienced head coaches, starting with Bowles and then Matt LaFleur in week six at the Packers, followed by Nick Sirianni at the Eagles in week seven. This comes after already playing John Harbaugh in the season opener and Dan Quinn in week…

summary: For the 2026 season the Dallas Cowboys largely ignored the offensive line, instead relying on names like Tyler Guyton to take a big step forward in 2026. full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Caleb Downs #13 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the first quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the 2026 season the Dallas Cowboys largely ignored the offensive line, instead relying on names like Tyler Guyton to take a big step forward in 2026. Also, we look into whether the possibility of depth and coaching could do enough to vault the Cowboys over the presumed NFC defensive powerhouse in the Rams. Dallas cleared up cap space in restructuring Daron Bland and Jake Ferguson, but if they don’t do anything with the cap space, it will only hurt them heading into 2027. Malik Davis was handed a fine for a week two lowering the helmet incident. And we put a bow on the offseason by asking fans how they view the last eight months. Everything Dallas Cowboys fans need to know before the 2026 season – Staff, DMN Given how poorly last season went, there is a lot of shakeup that happened this offseason. And with the opener less than a week away, it’s probably best to catch up on all things 2026 Cowboys. Caleb Downs has a big brain. His ability to process the game allows the Cowboys to trust the rookie defensive back to play the slot, line up near the line of scrimmage or deep in the backfield. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create communi ty posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Is the Cowboys Offensive Line Rebuild a Failure? – Mark Heaney, Inside The Star Dallas has done a lot of good things this offseason to add depth and rebuild critical positions. However, questions still remain along the offensive line. Starting from left to right, let’s make no mistake about it: this season is absolutely make or break for Guyton at left tackle. Dallas drafted him as a raw prospect, but that title can only last you so long. Despite star power, can Cowboys defense outperform Rams in long run? – Terence Watson, Cowboys Wire There is no debate that, up and down, the Rams have a more talented defense. However, with coaching, depth, and youth development, could the Cowboys outperform them in 2026? Parker’s roster building approach was two-pronged: rather than targeting the biggest names in free agency or on the trade market, he focused on adding quality starters who fit specific roles within his defensive scheme. More importantly, Parker prioritized rebuilding their depth at all three levels. Cowboys are making a dangerous bet on DaRon Bland and Jake Ferguson – Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat While having more cap room is great, in restructuring these two contracts, Dallas is now on the hook likely through next season. Which is a pointless gamble if Dallas isn’t going to use the cap room to make a signficant move. Ferguson should have been playing for his future this season. Restructuring his contract increased his 2027 dead cap hit, making it highly unlikely that Dallas will move on. The same goes for Bland, who underwent a second surgery on his left foot in January. Cowboys’ Malik Davis Receives Punishment For Preseason Infraction vs. Cardinals – Mike Moraitis, Sports Illustrated Fines like this always pop up following games, so this should come as no surprise. However, it does seem a bit aggressive given Davis is the only Cowboys player fined during the preseason According to the NFL’s official website , where all fines are listed, the league handed down a $6,735 fine to Davis for unnecessary roughness as a result of an illegal use of the helmet. The infraction occurred in the first quarter of the preseason Week 2 game against the Arizona Cardinals at the 12:07 mark. See the Cowboys offseason grade according to fans – David Halprin, Blogging The Boys Drafting Caleb Downs and signing a younger DC in Christian Parker did a lot to advance the goodwill of fans. But in less than a week, all of that goes out the window, and fans find out if it actually made a difference. All those moves and more have pleased the fanbase. We asked you to grade their performance, and 54% said ‘B’ and 37% said ‘A’. Only 9% voted for a combined ‘C’ through “F” grade. Daily discussion question: What will be our biggest takeaway this time next week?

title: Horse Tracks: Payton expects Mahomes, Chiefs to be full strength on MNF
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! We are FINALLY kicking off Week 1 of the 2026 season and Broncos against Chiefs on Monday Night Football could not be a better way to do it. And whatever hope you have that the Chiefs will trot out a hobbled Patrick Mahomes in Week 1 after spending the offseason recovering […]
full_text: Good morning, Broncos Country! We are FINALLY kicking off Week 1 of the 2026 season and Broncos against Chiefs on Monday Night Football could not be a better way to do it. And whatever hope you have that the Chiefs will trot out a hobbled Patrick Mahomes in Week 1 after spending the offseason recovering from a season-ending ACL tear last year, Sean Payton has some advice for you. Just stop (because he “answered this last week”). “I think we’re looking at it and expecting someone who’s 100 percent, someone who’s moving well based on what limited footage you get,” Payton admitted. “He’s going to be one of those guys that threatens you not only in the pocket, but out of the pocket.” “We’re expecting someone who’s 100 percent. …You have to be ready and prepare for what you know is his best, and that’s in the pocket, that’s the extended plays, that’s him running.” Sean Payton on facing Patrick Mahomes Basically, the head coach said, prepare for vintage Mahomes. “Our approach has been pay close attention to what we’ve seen historically film-wise, how we defend not only him, but their team,” the head coach added. “I think you have to be ready and prepare for what you know is his best, and that’s in the pocket, that’s the extended plays, that’s him running.” And often finding an open target, much to the dismay of the defensive backs. But Patrick Surtain II and his fellow DBs have been focusing on takeaways this offseason, so they are looking forward to showcasing the hard work. “I think it’s all about intention. It’s one thing to think about turnovers, but it’s being intentional at the same time,” Surtain II said. “When you’re going to the ball, you’re intentional about stripping the ball out, about intercepting the ball. I think that’s what matters because we all have the ability. We all could get a takeaway, we all could pick the ball, but it’s all about a mindset going in towards a play and actually capitalizing on those opportunities.” Workin' towards Week 1️⃣ pic.twitter.com/9dCODNBvpe — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 2, 2026 And with the addition of Kenneth Walker III to the running back room, the Broncos’ run defense may have to be as strong as its pass defense when facing the Chiefs. “I think [Walker III] has really good contact balance, vision with home-run speed,” Payton said. “He’s a heck of a football player.” But perhaps one of the toughest matchups for Payton when facing the Chiefs is squaring off against defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. “Steve [Spagnuolo] has always done a great job disguising looks, giving you zone-pressure looks,” Payton said. “He’s not afraid to play zero. You’re going to have to have a real good protection plan and be disciplined in your approach, especially when you’re facing that defense on the road with the noise.” “Every game is tough. …You have to forget about what happened last season, because every season’s completely different. …The division’s open for whoever to take at this point.” QuinN Meinerz Since the Broncos have won the last three matchups against the Chiefs, it would be easy to be lulled into thinking this rivalry — and this division — is the Broncos’ to lose. But no one in the building is thinking that. Every year is a new season with new challenges — and new challengers. “This is a very tough division,” said offensive guard Quinn Meinerz. “Every game is tough. … You kind of have to have short-term memory. You have to forget about what happened last season, because every season’s completely different. We have a new team. They have a new team. The division’s open for whoever to take at this point.” Meinerz added that each season the team has prove itself all over again. “That’s something we have to do again this year. That’s just kind of the nature of the beast of the NFL is everyone kind of resets and gets ready for the next season,” Meinerz added. “I think we’ve done a good job resetting. We know they’ve done a great job as well. They’re a really well-coached team. It’s going to be AFC West football.” This time, next week. ⏳ pic.twitter.com/M67lAofEdW — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 8, 2026

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Devon Witherspoon #21 of the Seattle Seahawks forces a fumble against Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. I ran out of things to talk about over the summer and decided to put this post on hiatus until the season. Well the season is finally here and MHR Roundup is back! Hopefully everyone had a safe and enjoyable Labor Day weekend. The NFL is wasting no time getting things rolling with a Wednesday Night Football game. From there, it will be 18+ weeks of NFL wrecking ball. Are you ready? Broncos daily recap Broncos sign veteran safety Taylor Rapp to their practice squad Taylor Rapp was widely believed to be their third safety this coming season before getting released over a personal issue requiring time at home. Coach Payton later cleared up the confusion and told reporters that Rapp had a personal issue come up and that he needed some time at home; To make room for him, they released rookie long snapper Luke Basso from their practice squad, leaving veteran Mitchell Fraboni as the only option now. Denver Broncos 53-Man Roster: Stock Up, Stock Down Nate Adkins is a Sean Payton favorite and will see playing time in tight end sets; Dallen Bentley made the team over Justin Joly as a surprise stock-up pick for another in-line blocking option. Garett Bolles continues to serve as the Broncos’ blindside protector for QB Bo Nix; Ben Powers is healthy after an offseason of questions. Kicker Wil Lutz remains unchanged despite pressure on game days, whereas Luke Wattenberg stays steady at offensive guard. Punter Jeremy Crawshaw had some growing pains but improved as the season went on so he looks to put his early-season rookie struggles behind him in year two. Potent quotables It’s been a quiet Labor Day weekend for the Broncos, but head coach Sean Payton did meet with the media this morning. We have his relevant quotes below. On what Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III brings to Kansas City’s offense and their evaluation of him during free agency “You always get a chance obviously to see a top free agent like that, especially when he plays in the Super Bowl. I think he has really good contact balance, vision with home-run speed. He’s a heck of a football player.” On if it is more difficult to prepare for a Chiefs Defensive Coordinator Steve Spagnuolo defense with multiple new starters “[Chiefs Defensive Coordinator] Steve [Spagnuolo] has always done a great job disguising looks, giving you zone-pressure looks. He’s not afraid to play zero. You’re going to have to have a real good protection plan and be disciplined in your approach, especially when you’re facing that defense on the road with the noise.” On the keys to how they have been able to turn things around in the AFC West “The first thing is focusing as a team on improving. There’s a sense of urgency when you get somewhere new. We have a ton of respect obviously for [Chiefs Head Coach] Andy [Reid], his staff and what they’ve accomplished, that team. So our task or our goal was really get to work and find the right 53 guys each season and work on the details of the game. So it’ll be a big challenge, especially with the crowd noise in Kansas City this year.” On how they structured practice over the past two weeks “I think the difference, and to your point, it’s not the bonus Monday, but it’s kind of today, but then also not playing until Monday night. Our work week is planned out accordingly because it’s not the first game of the season mechanics that all of us have somewhat grown accustomed to, it’s the first game being a Monday night game.” On preparing to face Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes coming off of injury “I think I answered this last week. I think we’re looking at it and expecting someone who’s 100 percent, someone who’s moving well based on what limited footage you get. He’s going to be one of those guys that threatens you not only in the pocket, but out of the pocket. So our approach has been pay close attention to what we’ve seen historically film-wise, how we defend not only him, but their team. So that’s kind of been the approach.” The Feed Post your own thoughts on MHR’s Feed . The NFL is kicking off the season on Wednesday too, so be ready for that. I wouldn’t be surprised if we end up with a game on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday AND Monday down the road at some point. The NFL is going full tilt on saturating the market. Hopefully the product improves, though. The officiating especially has been a point of major annoyance for fanbases across the country. Keep the product elite and the saturation works out nicely for all. Right now, I still think they have a problem with officiating and the changes made over the offseason likely hasn’t fixed the issue. I’m probably just getting my officiating angst out now, lol. I’ll actually enjoy watching some NFL football on Wednesday night. It’s been a long wait for Week 1.

title: Denver Broncos 53-Man Roster: Stock Up, Stock Down
summary: We have finally made it. Training camp and the preseason are behind us; the 53-man rosters are set, and now we’re officially in the week leading up to Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season. The Broncos will head to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday Night to take on the returning Patrick Mahomes and the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) sets to pass in the first half during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We have finally made it. Training camp and the preseason are behind us; the 53-man rosters are set, and now we’re officially in the week leading up to Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season. The Broncos will head to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday Night to take on the returning Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Before we get to all that, let us take a look at the Broncos’ 53-man roster, player by player, and evaluate whether their stock is going up, down, or staying the same heading into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up: We only saw Bo Nix for a handful of plays vs. the Packers in Week 2 of the preseason, but he looked good. He led the Broncos offense to 10 points, including an absolute dime to running back RJ Harvey for a touchdown. He looks ready for Week 1 and will head to Arrowhead, a place where he has played well, and will look to lead the Broncos to a 1-0 record. Jarrett Stidham – Stock up: He’s a stock-up because he won the backup quarterback job. Head Coach Sean Payton confirmed it last week, which was expected, and now he’ll be the QB2 for the Broncos once again this season. Sam Ehlinger – Stock up: All three quarterbacks are getting stock-up. After a strong camp and preseason, Ehlinger made the 53-man roster and now will serve as the Broncos’ QB3 once again this season. Running Back JK Dobbins – Unchanged: The veteran running back hasn’t played a snap since he suffered an injury vs. the Raiders on Thursday Night Football last season. However, he is healthy and has been practicing fully all summer and will be unleashed vs. the Chiefs on Monday Night. The Broncos did not have Dobbins in their matchups with them last season, so he will be a bit of an x-factor for them this time around. RJ Harvey – Stock up: Harvey could play a big part in the Broncos’ passing offense this season. He is an explosive player in space and can get open down the field for big plays. We’ll see how much he offers in the run game, but I think he is going to be a playmaker in the passing game. Jonah Coleman – Stock up: Is he the Broncos’ RB2? We have to wait and see how everything shakes out after Week 1, but I would not be surprised if Coleman splits time with veteran JK Dobbins as the early down back while Harvey comes in on passing downs. Either way, I think we will see Coleman involved early and often come Week 1. Tyler Badie – Unchanged: Badie made the Broncos’ 53-man roster, but his role will basically be the same as it was last season. He could be among the inactives, but if he is active, he will serve as the Broncos third down pass blocker while contributing in the kicking game. Adam Prentice – Stock up: He is on the Broncos’ practice squad, but he will be elevated and active for them moving forward and could be a big part of their short-yardage game. We saw Prentice used a lot in short-yardage and at the goal line during the preseason, and I would not be surprised if that continues at times during the season. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock up: Waddle is going to have a big Week 1. The Chiefs’ secondary saw a lot of changes and will be starting a rookie. Look for Waddle to start his Broncos career in a big way. He has been as advertised since he joined the Broncos, and I cannot wait to see what he does moving forward. Courtland Sutton – Unchanged: I am saying unchanged because we know what we’re getting in Sutton at this point. He will give you about 1,000 yards, 8 to 10 touchdown receptions, and some insane catches mixed in throughout the year. The addition of Waddle should open him up to some more favorable matchups, and we could see a big year from the Broncos’ longtime veteran pass catcher. Pat Bryant – Stock up: Bryant won the WR3 job and was the Broncos’ breakout/standout player of training camp. He had Sean Payton saying they’re not taking him off the field, and other Broncos coaches/players hyping him up all summer. Now, it’s time to carry that play and hype into the regular season. With all the attention on Waddle and Sutton, Bryant has a chance to make some plays in this Broncos offense. Marvin Mims – Unchanged: I think Mims is who he is right now. He will be an All-Pro-caliber returner while also giving the Broncos a dangerous deep threat who can make the big plays in key moments. While he may not be a starter or see a lot of targets, Mims has a chance to make a big play whenever he is on the field. Troy Franklin – Unchanged: I am not sure where Franklin fits in the Broncos’ game-day roster plans right now. We should have more clarity on that after Week 1, but I would not be surprised if he was among the inactives, especially with Lil’Jordan Humphrey making the team. We’ll see! Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Stock up: Lil’Jordan Humphrey made the Broncos’ 53-man roster, and we all know he is going to play. He is a Sean Payton guy and has played a lot in recent years, and I would not be surprised to see him active in Week 1. With the Broncos likely wanting to establish the run vs. the Chiefs, look for LJH to be out there in some capacity. Tight End Adam Trautman – Unchanged: The veteran tight end is your “starter” once again and will be the Broncos’ top in-line tight end. Sean Payton and the Broncos trust him in this role, and it will be the same one he has had since he joined the team. Evan Engram – Unchanged: Engram is the Broncos’ top pass-catching threat and could see a larger role in the offense with OC Davis Webb now calling plays. The two are close friends due to their time with the Giants, so I would not be surprised if Webb drew up some plays for his good friend. With that said, we have to wait and see. There was a lot of hype for Engram last season, and it never really panned out, but hopefully, things are different this time around. Nate Adkins – Stock up: I am going with stock up because Adkins made the team and showed some pass-catching ability in the preseason finale. He is another Sean Payton favorite and will see playing time in two or three tight end sets as a run blocker. Dallen Bentley – Stock up: The 7th-round rookie tight end made the team over 5th-round rookie Justin Joly, which was a surprise, and now will give the Broncos another in-line blocking tight end. He will probably be among the Broncos’ inactives, but the fact that he made the team is why I have him as a stock-up guy. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: The veteran left tackle will serve as the Broncos’ blindside protector for QB Bo Nix and continue to be one of the best left tackles in the NFL right now Ben Powers – Stock up: He is healthy, and after an offseason of questions about him potentially being cut or traded, he is back as the Broncos’ starting left guard. Luke Wattenberg – Unchanged: Wattenberg is a steady presence in the center of the Broncos’ offensive line and is known as one of the more intelligent centers in the NFL. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: He gets a stock up because he’s Quinn Meinerz. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: McGlinchey stabilized the Broncos’ right tackle position and gives them a reliable veteran presence with leadership qualities at that position. Matt Peart – Stock up: I had him on the roster bubble, but the veteran reserve tackle made the team and will serve as the Broncos’ swing tackle once again this season. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Palcho is likely the Broncos’ 6th offensive lineman who will come in on certain heavy packages while also being a reliable and versatile backup. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: He has been sidelined with an injury, but he appears to be healthy and will once again be the Broncos’ backup center. Kage Casey – Unchanged: The rookie lineman…

title: Broncos sign veteran safety Taylor Rapp to their practice squad
summary: According to multiple reports, including 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are signing, or re-signing, veteran safety Taylor Rapp to their practice squad. To make room for Rapp on the practice squad, Klis is also reporting the Broncos released rookie long snapper Luke Basso from their practice squad. The team initially kept two long […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 23: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills runs onto the field prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to multiple reports, including 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are signing, or re-signing, veteran safety Taylor Rapp to their practice squad. To make room for Rapp on the practice squad, Klis is also reporting the Broncos released rookie long snapper Luke Basso from their practice squad . The team initially kept two long snappers on the practice squad, but now, they are down to just veteran Mitchell Fraboni. #Broncos have signed veteran safety Taylor Rapp to their practice squad per source. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) September 7, 2026 Rapp originally signed with the Broncos late in training camp and was widely believed to be their third safety this coming season. However, he was surprisingly released by the team a few days later, which was a surprise to fans and media, especially after the way Sean Payton and Vance Joseph spoke of him days before. Head Coach Sean Payton later cleared up the confusion and told reporters that Rapp had a personal issue come up and that he needed some time at home. He also added that there was a “better-than-good chance” that Rapp would return to the team when ready. Well, Rapp worked out for the Broncos last week, and now he is signing, or re-signing, to the Broncos’ practice squad. I would imagine he will need a few weeks to get into shape before being ready to play, but he figures to be in the Broncos’ plans at safety at some point this season. Taylor Rapp is only 28 years old and is a former 2nd-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft by the Los Angeles Rams. He is an experienced safety with plenty of starting experience who has spent time with the Rams and previously with the Buffalo Bills. During his seven seasons in the NFL, Rapp has appeared in 93 games and started 72 of them. Last season, he appeared in six games for the Buffalo Bills before a knee injury ended his season, and he was placed on the injured reserve. Throughout his career, Rapp has totaled 488 tackles, 11 tackles for a loss, 2 sacks, 12 interceptions, 31 pass deflections, and 2 forced fumbles. For now, the Broncos will head into the season with JL Skinner, Devon Key, and Tycen Anderson as their depth players behind starters Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones. When Rapp is ready, I would look for him to instantly become their top reserve off the bench and likely become their third safety.

title: While others play, Broncos wait
summary: Can you feel it, Broncos Country? It’s officially week 1 in the NFL! Okay, maybe it’s a little premature to get amped for Broncos football when Denver doesn’t play for another whole week, but that doesn’t make the football season any less ‘here’. This season kicks off with a Super Bowl rematch in Seattle, featuring […]
full_text: Nov 28, 2021; Denver, Colorado, USA; A general view of the Bronco on the top of Empower Field at Mile High as the sunsets in the fourth quarter between the Denver Broncos and the Los Angeles Chargers. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-USA TODAY Sports Can you feel it, Broncos Country? It’s officially week 1 in the NFL! Okay, maybe it’s a little premature to get amped for Broncos football when Denver doesn’t play for another whole week, but that doesn’t make the football season any less ‘here’. This season kicks off with a Super Bowl rematch in Seattle, featuring the Patriots of New England and the champion Seahawks. Expect a lot of deserved seabird chest beating and exuberance in their 12th man identity, licensed from Texas A&M . On Thursday night, the NFL’s first international game takes place between the 49ers and the Rams in Australia. One wonders how our friends in the UK feel about a marquee divisional matchup being exported to Australia while Londoners are plagued for eternity with Jaguar home games. It just doesn’t seem fair. Sunday begins the bulk of the week 1 games, with 13 being played throughout the day. The first football Sunday in the 2026 season culminates in the obligatory Giants and Cowboys showdown that’s forced on innocent football fans every year, no matter how inept or awful both teams may be. It’s probably best to get this one out of the way early. Then… Finally… On Monday, a whole week from the time of this writing, the Broncos will travel to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs in a rare September tilt. Fans will finally get to see just how lethal Nix-to-Waddle connection can be this season. Questions will be answered, like how long will Sean Payton be able to keep his hands off Davis Webb’s play sheet? Will the defense absorb the loss of free agent John Franklin Myers? Will Jonathon Cooper’s offseason stupidity affect this team? Folks, you’ve waited for the 2026 season ever since a snowy white out and Jarett Stidham’s limitations surprised the Broncos in the AFC Championship game. Sure, Denver’s game is still a week away, but there is plenty of football to tide us over. Get ready Broncos Country, week 1 of the NFL season is officially here!

title: 2026 NFL predictions: Detroit Lions defensive MVP
summary: While the Detroit Lions’ offense is filled with proven talent, the defensive side of the ball has a few more questions than answers. That said, there is still some top end talent. In total, five Lions defenders have earned All Pro or Pro Bowl honors: Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Devin White, Brian Branch, and Kerby […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - DECEMBER 24: Aidan Hutchinson #97 and Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions look on against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium on December 24, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Lions defeated the Vikings 30-24. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Detroit Lions’ offense is filled with proven talent, the defensive side of the ball has a few more questions than answers. That said, there is still some top end talent. In total, five Lions defenders have earned All Pro or Pro Bowl honors: Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Devin White, Brian Branch, and Kerby Joseph. That’s actually the exact same number as the defense (Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Penei Sewell). So, maybe there are more candidates for the 2026 Detroit Lions defensive MVP than you think. As we continue our 2026 NFL predictions, here are our picks for Lions 2026 defensive MVP. Don’t forget to cast your vote at the bottom of the page! Previously: Offensive MVP predictions Who will be the Lions’ defensive MVP in 2026? Morgan Cannon: Jack Campbel Obviously, there is an argument to be made for the monster on the edge that wears #97, but I am going with Campbell because I think by end of season, he will be the unquestioned heartbeat of the defense. From racking up tackles, forcing fumbles, and being a general game-wrecker against opposing team’s running games, he is also a seasoned veteran in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard’s defense. Being able to ensure everyone is where they need to be, while also being in control of pre-snap checks and shifts is going to pay huge dividends for the Lions in 2026. Al Karsten: Alim McNeill It hasn’t exactly been a fairytale 20-plus months for Alim McNeill since tearing his ACL in Week 15 of 2024, just two months after signing his blockbuster contract extension. But for the hip-hop artist who goes by “Dream,” the nightmare appears to be over—and his dreams are very much at the forefront of reality after a remarkably strong bounceback during Lions training camp. While the expectation is for Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell to continue their All-Pro-level play, McNeill has an opportunity to completely shapeshift this defense if he can consistently maximize his talents. If the version of McNeill who flashed from 2022-24 returns for a career year, Detroit suddenly has the makings of a lethal defensive front capable of helping propel this unit into the top 10. Like his draft classmate Milton Williams did for the Patriots after joining them last offseason, McNeill could provide the type of uplifting impact that helps spearhead a defense on a run to the Super Bowl. A season with 7+ sacks, 20+ quarterback hits, and 10+ tackles for loss would make Detroit a force to be reckoned with come January and February. Erik Schlitt: Aidan Hutchinson The Lions’ defensive line looked great in training camp and could be a huge catalyst in their defensive success. Hutchinson is already one of the best defensive players in the NFL, but with a healthy Alim McNeill, improved Tyleik Williams, along with DJ Wonnum and Derrick Moore splitting time on the opposite edge, Hutchinson should see his opportunities increase and could be in for a monster season. Jeremy Reisman: Aidan Hutchinson I believe Hutchinson is in for a career year. While I think his supporting cast is better, I don’t think that will draw any attention away from Hutch. But with some of the things we’ve seen in training camp, I don’t believe defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is just going to let teams add an extra tight end or running back to Hutchinson’s side and make him fight off double and triple teams every play. No, the Lions are committed to keeping their pass rush creative this year, and Hutchinson is going to EAT. John Whiticar: Jack Campbell In the past, Aidan Hutchinson was the clear-cut MVP on defense, but Campbell has now become 1B to his 1A. However, I think the Lions have added a lot of good defenders to pair with Hutchinson (Wonnum, Moore, Gill-Howard) and with Alim McNeill back and healthy, Hutchinson will no longer be leaned on as the only reliable lineman on the roster. Campbell, meanwhile, is far and away the Lions’ best linebacker, a position that is vital to every part of the defense. Ryan Mathews: Aidan Hutchinson Aidan Hutchinson will be the Lions’ defensive MVP in 2026. This is as talented and deep the defensive line has been in Detroit since Hutchinson arrived in 2022. And while Hutchinson will be a key part of gameplanning for any opposing offensive coordinator, there’s going to be plenty of chances for Hutchinson to make impact plays. Anthony Balaj: Brian Branch While Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson will likely be tapped with the All-Pro accolades, Branch will be the player that unlocks Kelvin Sheppard’s ability to dynamically disguise the defensive scheme (and likely land Sheppard a head coaching job in 2027). Brandon Knapp: Aidan Hutchinson While he was looking to be on a career season in 2024, that injury didn’t appear to slow him down as much in 2025. Now that he’s had a full year under his belt post-injury, and more help added to the opposite EDGE position and the interior defensive line, I think Hutchinson makes a true case for DPOY in 2026. The help fans have pleaded for has arrived, and I think Hutchinson will benefit the most out of it.

summary: The Detroit Lions will open their 2026 regular season against the New Orleans Saints, hoping to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season. The Lions will get the advantage of hosting this game in Detroit, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -6.5 points. The Saints finished 2025 with a 6-11 […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 03: Jameson Williams #9 of the Detroit Lions dives to score a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the New Orleans Saints at the Caesars Superdome on December 03, 2023 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions will open their 2026 regular season against the New Orleans Saints, hoping to rebound from a disappointing 2025 season. The Lions will get the advantage of hosting this game in Detroit, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -6.5 points . The Saints finished 2025 with a 6-11 record under first-time head coach (and former Lions backup quarterback) Kellen Moore. While they certainly underwhelmed, they finished the season strong, with four of those wins coming in the final five games of the regular season. “This is a hungry opponent,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Monday. “It’s a lot of young, hungry players, talented players. You could see their progression as the season went on last year; they started playing pretty good football—minus Atlanta, in that last game.” This offseason, the Saints prioritized upgrading their offense and plugging holes on defense. One of the Saints’ biggest offseason moves was upgrading their guard positions. They signed starting left guard David Edwards in free agency, then added rookie Jeremiah Wright (a fourth-round pick) to the mix to challenge Cesar Ruiz, who is entering his seventh year as a starter (mainly at right guard) for the Saints. They invested in youth at their skill positions, signing running back Travis Etienne to complement Alvin Kamara, but Kamara is dealing with an MCL injury and is expected to miss the opener. The Saints also drafted three wide receivers—Jordyn Tyson (first round), Bryce Lance (fourth), and Barion Brown (sixth)—and a tight end—Oscar Delp (third)—and all four are expected to contribute as rookies. Unfortunately, the Saints will have to wait to see the eighth overall pick take the field as Tyson landed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and will miss the first four games of the season; Lance is expected to start in his place. Delp will open the season as TE3 and will challenge free-agent acquisition Noah Fant for TE2 reps. On defense, the Saints lost one of their best players in starting linebacker Demario Davis, but re-signed Kaden Ellis to fill his role. Along the defensive line, 2023 first-round pick Bryan Bresee is out for the season with a torn ACL and is expected to be replaced by 2025 third-round pick Vernon Broughton. The Saints are banking on 2025 picks corner Quincy Riley (second) and nickelback Jonas Sanker (third) to step into vacated roles in their secondary. The Lions and Saints will square off on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field in Detroit.

title: Discussion: Who will be the first Detroit Lion to record a sack in 2026?
summary: Nothing gets the home crowd hyped up quite like a quarterback sack. With the Detroit Lions hosting the New Orleans Saints in Week 1 of the 2026 season, Ford Field will be eager to see Tyler Shough hit the turf—preferably multiple times. Despite the Lions lacking pass rush last season, they still finished tied for […]
full_text: Nothing gets the home crowd hyped up quite like a quarterback sack. With the Detroit Lions hosting the New Orleans Saints in Week 1 of the 2026 season, Ford Field will be eager to see Tyler Shough hit the turf—preferably multiple times. Despite the Lions lacking pass rush last season, they still finished tied for fourth in the league with 49 sacks. Part of this came from consistency. The Lions had five games with four or more sacks, yet they also recorded seven games with one or fewer sacks. Too often it was feast or famine for Detroit. Aidan Hutchinson led the way for the team, recording 14.5 sacks on the season. Perhaps surprisingly, it was Al-Quadin Muhammad coming in second with 11.0 sacks. However, his season was another example of that inconsistent pass rush. Despite playing in all 17 games, 7.5 of his sacks came in just three games—across the remaining 14 games, he had just 3.5 sacks. With Muhammad departing for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in free agency, the Lions were looking for running mates for Hutchinson. They signed DJ Wonnum and added Derrick Moore and Skyler Gill-Howard via the draft. Coupled with Alim McNeill, Levi Onwuzurike, and Ahmed Hassanein returning from injury, the Lions are hoping their front seven can provide a much-needed upgrade in the pass rush department. Which member of the Lions defense will be the first one to bring down an opposing quarterback? Who will be the first Detroit Lion to record a sack in 2026? Today’s Question of the Day is: My answer: Jack Campbell. There is no question that Hutchinson should lead the team in sacks by the end of the season, but early on, I expect opponents to focus on stopping him. I am optimistic about how McNeill, Wonnum, Moore, and Tyleik Williams can perform in this defense, but none of them command the attention that Hutchinson does. I am expecting double teams and chip blocks early and often for Hutchinson. Of the linemen expected to play a majority of snaps, the two names that stand out the most are McNeill and Wonnum. McNeill has looked like his old self in training camp, while Wonnum should be a reliable contributor on early downs. However, given that this could be a run-happy Saints offense, pass rush opportunities could be somewhat limited—I would not be surprised if the Saints drop back fewer than 20 times in Week 1. If the Lions are focused on stopping the run, the primary role of McNeill and Wonnum could be to plug gaps and hold contain, not rush the passer. I also want to tip my hat to the Saints offensive line, a unit that I think is better than advertised—I really liked their signing of David Edwards to shore up their weakest position, left guard. That is why I think Campbell could record the first Lions sack of the season. We know how potent he can be as a blitzer, and I expect Kelvin Sheppard’s defense to get creative with timely blitzes. Because of how versatile Campbell is as a linebacker, predicting where he will be on each snap is a nightmare for offensive coordinators. Whether he is stopping the run, dropping into coverage, rushing up the middle, or spying the quarterback, he demonstrated in 2025 that he can do it all. I think there is a good chance that a Campbell blitz could go unnoticed and result in a big-time play. Which Lions defender will notch the first sack of 2026? Let us know in the comments below.
author: John Whiticar

title: Detroit Lions announce 7 captains for 2026 season, including 3 first-timers
summary: On Monday afternoon, the Detroit Lions announced the seven players who will act as captains for the entirety of the 2026 season. They are: quarterback Jared Goff, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, offensive tackle Penei Sewell, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, defensive tackle Alim McNeill, linebacker Jack Campbell, and punter Jack Fox. Goff is now entering […]
full_text: Nov 27, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (46) runs onto the field prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Monday afternoon, the Detroit Lions announced the seven players who will act as captains for the entirety of the 2026 season. They are: quarterback Jared Goff, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, offensive tackle Penei Sewell, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, defensive tackle Alim McNeill, linebacker Jack Campbell, and punter Jack Fox. Goff is now entering his sixth year as a Detroit Lion, and he’s been a captain for all six seasons. Not only has he been around for the team’s entire turnaround, but he’s been a critical part of it—even if some believed he was just a bridge quarterback when he was first acquired in the trading of Matthew Stafford. St. Brown and Sewell—both acquired in Detroit’s first draft under general manager Brad Holmes—are now in their fourth year of being Lions captains. Their only seasons without being named a captain were each of their first two years in the league. It’s been a similar path for Hutchinson, who was drafted in 2022 and has been a captain for three straight years now (2024, 2025, 2026). Jack Campbell, despite being the heart of the Lions’ defense for a couple of years running, will be captain for his first-ever season in Detroit. It was only a matter of time, as Campbell was a captain at Iowa for two years. The only thing holding him back from duties in Detroit was that veteran Alex Anzalone had become a strong leader in the locker room. With Anzalone gone in free agency, it was time for Campbell to take his proper place. “Jack is a big, physical human being for the middle linebacker position, which means he can take a beat and then he can deliver a beating. And that’s hard in today’s game,” Dan Campbell said of Jack during training camp. “So, to have a guy like him, I mean, he can take on a lot of reps. Not everybody can do that, but he’s too valuable. I mean, he does everything for us.” Alim McNeill is also another first-time captain. Coming off a torn ACL in 2024, McNeill is facing high expectations to bring back disruption to the middle of the defensive line. In 2023, he tallied 10 QB hits, 5.0 sacks, and six tackles for loss, resulting in a contract extension in 2024, just a couple of months before he suffered his injury. Finally, Jack Fox has been named the special teams captain for the first time in his seven-year career. Detroit has typically gone with a four-phase specialist like Jalen Reeves-Maybin or Grant Stuard, but Fox has been one of the most reliable players on the entire team. He’s a two-time Pro Bowler, a one-time All-Pro, and his currently 10th in the NFL in all-time net punting average (43.1).

title: Detroit Lions make several roster moves ahead of Week 1 vs. Saints
summary: The Detroit Lions have made a few more roster maneuvers to get the roster ready for their Week 1 matchup with the New Orleans Saints. Detroit started the week with two vacancies on their 53-man roster. Now they’ll still have one. Detroit announced that: Starting with Bachie, he takes up a spot on the 53-man […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions linebacker Joe Bachie (35) takes part in a linebacker drill during Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions have made a few more roster maneuvers to get the roster ready for their Week 1 matchup with the New Orleans Saints. Detroit started the week with two vacancies on their 53-man roster. Now they’ll still have one. Detroit announced that: Linebacker Joe Bachie has signed from the practice squad to the 53-man roster C Seth McLaughlin has signed to the practice squad RB Jabari Small has signed to the practice squad G Mason Miller has been placed on the practice squad injured reserve list Starting with Bachie, he takes up a spot on the 53-man roster now, giving Detroit an extra body amongst a crowded linebacker room. But with rookie Jimmy Rolder missing most of training camp and not officially back yet, Detroit likely needed someone who can provide depth on gameday and play special teams. Bachie is a six-year veteran with seven career starts and over 1,100 special teams snaps. McLaughlin and Small’s return to the practice squad was expected. Both players made the team’s initial 53-man roster, but were waived later in the week in order to do some roster maneuvering. It would not be surprising to see McLaughlin get a Week 1 practice squad elevation considering Detroit currently doesn’t have a healthy backup center behind Juice Scruggs. Small could also provide some gameday depth, but it sounds like the Lions already have other RB2 plans with Isiah Pacheco starting the season on injured reserve . Speaking of IR, it’s a disappointment to see Miller land on the practice squad IR. He was a great story on the final week of training camp, because he had to be the team’s emergency center during the final preseason game and played quite well despite no experience at the position. Unfortunately, he’ll be sidelined for at least four games. Like on the active roster IR, Miller will not count against the team’s practice squad 16-player maximum capacity. Detroit still has an empty spot on the 53-man roster. Smart money is on wide receiver Tom Kennedy to assume that spot, but the Lions may be waiting until next week to do so, because his contract would become fully guaranteed if he were on the Week 1 roster. Regardless, Kennedy is likely to be a part of Sunday’s roster, as he’s the leading candidate to be the team’s starting punt returner and fourth or fifth wide receiver.

title: Detroit Lions believe DJ Wonnum is great complement to Aidan Hutchinson
summary: If you read every single one of our daily Detroit Lions training camp observations, you may only see a passing mention or two of defensive end DJ Wonnum. Despite being in line for a potential starting role on a revamped Lions defensive line, Wonnum’s spring was quiet. But coach Dan Campbell said on Monday that […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum (98) practices during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co If you read every single one of our daily Detroit Lions training camp observations, you may only see a passing mention or two of defensive end DJ Wonnum. Despite being in line for a potential starting role on a revamped Lions defensive line, Wonnum’s spring was quiet. But coach Dan Campbell said on Monday that it’s been a good kind of quiet for the six-year veteran. “I mean this is a very good way: it’s been kind of a quiet, just steady training camp for him,” Campbell said. “I think he’s come in and just done his job. I think he’s been very consistent with what we’ve asked him to do. There’s nothing flashy about it, but he’s a crafty, sneaky, smart veteran football player that understands how to play the run, understands—he’s got some slipperiness as a rusher.” Wonnum first caught the team’s attention when he was playing as a rotational player for the Vikings. Again, there wasn’t anything particularly flashy about what he did in Minnesota, but he went about his business, produced 20 sacks between 2021-23, contributed on special teams, and grew to become a reliable run defender. As soon as Wonnum joined Detroit this offseason, Campbell knew he fit the team’s culture of hard, steady workers. “I just remember when he came in, he was one of those guys,” Campbell said. “He’s a lunch-pail guy that’s going to give everything that he’s got, and he plays a smart brand of football, and I love that about him.” For years, the Lions have been looking for a bookend to Aidan Hutchinson. They needed someone who can not only hold the edge in the run game, but provide a legitimate pass-rushing threat to pull attention away from Hutchinson—or at least be able to win their one-on-ones if teams opt to spend additional resources on only Hutchinson. “I think he’s going to complement Hutch very well on the other side,” Campbell said of Wonnum. “So, I think he’s exactly what I expected to get here to this point.” But Wonnum won’t be alone. Detroit invested a second-round pick this year in Michigan defensive end Derrick Moore, who had flashes between injuries at training camp. They’ll also have a healthy Alim McNeill back to cause some disruption in the middle of the defense. And don’t count out the depth along the defensive line, including Tyleik Williams, Levi Onwuzurike, Ahmed Hassanein, and Skyler Gill-Howard, among others. Last year, the Lions finished t-fourth in sacks with 49, but that didn’t tell the whole story. Per NFL Pro, Detroit’s time to pressure—the average amount of time to move the quarterback off his spot—was 2.86 seconds, which ranked 30th in the NFL. And that was despite having the ninth-highest blitz rate. Detroit doesn’t want to stray too far from its “stop the run first” mentality, but with a player like Wonnum, they won’t have to. He brings a steady presence to the run game, and Detroit is banking on him thriving as a pass rusher opposite Hutchinson.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Dan Campbell provides some clarity on Detroit Lions’ RB2 situation
summary: The Detroit Lions will have a different backup running back than expected to start the 2026 season. Last week, the Lions placed Isiah Pacheco—their primary offseason signing at running back—on injured reserve with a back injury. That means he’ll miss at least the first four games of the season, and Detroit will have to rely […]
full_text: Aug 3, 2026; Allen Park, MI, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jacob Saylors (25), running back Sione Vaki (33), and running back Jabari Small (26) stretch during Detroit Lions training camp. Mandatory Credit: Paul Barnick-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions will have a different backup running back than expected to start the 2026 season. Last week, the Lions placed Isiah Pacheco—their primary offseason signing at running back—on injured reserve with a back injury. That means he’ll miss at least the first four games of the season, and Detroit will have to rely on someone new at the running back position behind Jahmyr Gibbs. As of now, the Lions roster only has two options behind Gibbs: 2024 fourth-round pick Sione Vaki and last year’s pickup from the UFL Jacob Saylors. Vaki has battled through injuries for much of his career, which has stunted his development a bit since moving from his college position of safety. Saylors only carried the ball for the Lions twice last year, but he took the majority of carries for the team in the preseason and was excellent. He finished the preseason with 187 rushing yards (second most in NFL) on just 31 carries, an average of 6.0 yards per carry. On Monday, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked about Saylors and his rise from the UFL’s St. Louis Battlehawks. Interestingly—and tellingly—most of Campbell’s answer surrounded about how excited he is to see Vaki play. “It’s about committee, too,” Campbell said. “I see Vaki getting some reps, too, now. I don’t see, ‘Okay, Saylors is like running back two.’ Saylors brings special teams value and there’s things that he’s been able to do. We’ve seen more of him than Vaki in games, preseason games. “But Vaki’s banked some pretty good reps in practice, and we know Vaki’s a very valuable special teams player, too. But we feel like Vaki’s ready to take some of this on, too, as a runner and as a pass protector and a receiver. So we feel good about either one of those guys in there when Jah [Gibbs] needs a breather.” While you could certainly read that as the job will be split between Vaki and Saylors, that certainly seems to be more of an endorsement of Vaki in the primary backup role—especially considering the question asked was focused on Saylors. Vaki as the potential backup is a calculated risk. Early this offseason, Campbell admitted that he was still in the infancy of learning the position. “The running back position is a little raw,” Campbell said during minicamp. “Yes, he has been in there, he did a little bit in college, this is year three, but he hasn’t played running back, not that much, and a lot of it is injury.” Unfortunately, injuries got in the way again this training camp. Vaki missed well over a week with a broken nose and eye injury, and he didn’t get any play in the preseason, either. However, Vaki has gotten a lot of recent work in training camp, regularly repping immediately behind Gibbs while Pacheco has been out. He’s flashed his ability to catch the football, and his best early trait may be as a pass protector, which leans into the physicality that made him a good safety and special teamer. Still, Vaki is entering Year 3 of his career with just seven career carries, three catches, and 27 total offensive snaps. Sunday against the New Orleans Saints could be his first significant action since Week 10 of 2024, when he logged 10 snaps against the Jaguars in a blowout win. The Lions are confident he’ll be able to handle the role. Are you?
