title: Random ESPN simulation predicts dream 2026 Detroit Lions season
summary: ESPN has a prediction system called Football Power Index, which uses a bunch of metrics and projections to simulate and predict outcomes. They use this system to create probabilities for the season, sometimes based on thousands and thousands of simulations. For example, their FPI system project the Detroit Lions to make the playoffs 71.4% of […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 14: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions celebrates a touchdown against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on September 14, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN has a prediction system called Football Power Index , which uses a bunch of metrics and projections to simulate and predict outcomes. They use this system to create probabilities for the season, sometimes based on thousands and thousands of simulations. For example, their FPI system project the Detroit Lions to make the playoffs 71.4% of the time and produce an average of 10.5 wins this season—good for fourth-most. Every year, ESPN takes one of those thousands of simulations and zeroes in on it. How they select which of those simulations to dissect is not clear, but it’s presumed to be random. And this year’s simulation is one Detroit Lions fans would dream of. The simulation—labeled simulation No. 9,187 by author Seth Walder—not only has the Lions producing an NFL-best 13-4 record (tied with the 49ers), but it has Detroit winning the Super Bowl over the Los Angeles Chargers . Despite producing the best record, Detroit earned the NFC’s No. 2 seed, while the 49ers got the first-round bye. From there, the Lions won three straight games to get to the Super Bowl. Defeated the Packers 27-24 in the Wild Card round Defeated the Cowboys 27-20 in the Divisional round Defeated the Rams 20-17 in the NFC Championship Game Talk about an absolute dream route to the Super Bowl. First, Detroit gets to take out their biggest rival in the opening round. Then they take out a Dallas team that has been an annoying thorn in their side for decades. Then, Jared Goff gets one more slice of revenge against the franchise that jettisoned him, while Detroit also potentially ends Matthew Stafford’s career. A fun side-note from that game, Walder notes that Aidan Hutchinson wins Defensive Player of the Year over Myles Garrett. Then, in the Super Bowl, the Lions take down a Chargers team in a thriller. Here’s Walder explaining what happened in the simulation. Back and forth the game swung, with Cameron Dicker hitting a 55-yard field goal to put Los Angeles up 31-30 with 90 seconds left. But that was too much time for Goff. After a chunk passing play to Jameson Williams, the Lions found themselves in field goal range with plenty of time remaining. They handed the ball to Gibbs several times to inch closer and burn Los Angeles’ timeouts. Jake Bates connected on a 42-yard field goal as time expired to win the title. And as a sweet cherry on top, all the hype that the Chicago Bears are getting? It resulted in a 6-11 record for Ben Johnson and company. Alas, the simulation is meaningless in the grand scheme of things. But here’s hoping the reality we live in isn’t too far from from Simulation No. 9,187.

title: Discussion: What is the Detroit Lions’ ceiling for the 2026 season?
summary: “Next year is our year.” It’s become the battle cry of Detroit Lions fans annually after the previous season has come to its disappointing conclusion. There haven’t been many more recent seasons more disappointing for Lions fans than the 2025 campaign. For the prior four seasons, it had been all about growth. 2022 ended with […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 23: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts after beating the New York Giants 34-27 in overtime at Ford Field on November 23, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images “Next year is our year.” It’s become the battle cry of Detroit Lions fans annually after the previous season has come to its disappointing conclusion. There haven’t been many more recent seasons more disappointing for Lions fans than the 2025 campaign. For the prior four seasons, it had been all about growth. 2022 ended with Detroit’s thrilling Week 18 win to kick the Packers out of the playoffs and make a statement that the Lions are coming. 2023 was the closest this team has ever come to making a Super Bowl, with an unbelievably run deep into the playoffs. In 2024, Detroit posted a franchise high in regular season wins (15), only to see it come crashing down with a second-round exit in the playoffs. After each of those seasons, it felt like it was inevitable Detroit would eventually break free of the postseason torment and finally reach the elusive Super Bowl. We said, “Next year is our year” with actual confidence, not an ironic twinge. Then 2025 happened. Detroit took their first clear step back as a franchise under coach Dan Campbell, and it certainly has some wondering if the Lions can right the ship and get back to championship contention. So today’s Question of the Day is: What is the Detroit Lions’ ceiling for the 2026 season? My answer: Well, if you believe ESPN’s prediction model and their full 2026 NFL season preview , Detroit’s ceiling for wins is a 13-4 record, and they’ve got a 71.4 percent chance of making the playoffs. So, certainly, making the playoffs should be considered the expectation, not the ceiling. But how far can this team make it? Can they really orchestrate a Super Bowl run? Does their roster compete with the consensus contenders like the Los Angeles Rams, Buffalo Bills, and Seattle Seahawks—the three teams with the best Super Bowl odds? I would contend that they do. Their offense is filled with superstardom, from Jared Goff to Jahmyr Gibbs to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell. And as I pointed out last week, the team’s depth on the offensive and defensive lines are deeper than they’ve been in quite some time . Sure, there are questions about how quickly the newly formed offensive line can gel together. And there is certainly warranted concern about both the starting-level talent and depth at cornerback. Every team has questions, and every roster has some talent gaps. We here in Detroit tend to obsess over those things, as they are typically the things that sink this franchise. And they could very well again this year. But at the same time, the Lions’ schedule looks easier to start the season, which should give the offensive line some grace to continue to build chemistry. And while the cornerback room certainly looks like the team’s biggest weakness, Detroit’s investment in pass rush and assignment-sound safeties could be enough to mask that weakness as much as possible. So do I think the Super Bowl is on the table for the Lions this year? Absolutely. Will it require several things to go Detroit’s way in 2026? Yes, and that is the case with every single Super Bowl winner in NFL history. So pour a little Kool-Aid in your coffee this morning. title: 2026 NFL predictions: Who will be the Detroit Lions’ Offensive MVP?
summary: It’s finally, officially Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Our patience will finally be paid off with a full week of NFL games starting on Wednesday… then Thursday… then Sunday… then Monday. But before the games kick off, the Pride of Detroit staff will be providing their predictions for the 2026 Detroit Lions’ season […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Jared Goff #16 and Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions in action against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally, officially Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Our patience will finally be paid off with a full week of NFL games starting on Wednesday… then Thursday… then Sunday… then Monday. But before the games kick off, the Pride of Detroit staff will be providing their predictions for the 2026 Detroit Lions’ season all week. And we kick things off Monday with our projections for the Lions’ Offensive MVP. You can make your predictions with the poll at the bottom of this story. Who will be the Lions’ offensive MVP in 2026? Brandon Knapp: Jahmyr Gibbs He’s arguably the top running back in the NFL, and now he is behind a reinforced offensive line with more chances to get the ball with David Montgomery gone. I think he will see an expanded role in the passing game, which pushes him toward of front of being the main weapon the Lions offense will prioritize in 2026. Anthony Balaj: Jared Goff Not because he’s the quarterback, but because he’s grown into one of the NFL’s best at his position. It’s the reliability and maturity in his play that now separates Goff from many of his peers, which will ultimately raise the floor of this young offensive line while maximizing the ceiling of the all-pro skill group. Ryan Mathews: Jameson Williams Jameson Williams will be the Lions’ offensive MVP in 2026. Most will point to Jahmyr Gibbs needing to be the MVP on this side of the ball, but if Williams is able to be the explosive threat he’s been the last two seasons on a little more volume, he’s going to be the most valuable part of the Lions’ offense. John Whiticar: Jahmyr Gibbs Sure, quarterbacks are more valuable and Jared Goff is critical to the offense’s success, but the expectations for Gibbs are sky-high. With no David Montgomery, he is now the focal point of an offense that loves to run the ball. The Lions lost a lot of games last season because their run game could not dominate early on and their passing attack was left to play catch-up. If the Lions are to be successful in 2026, they need Gibbs to be a contender for Offensive Player of the Year—and he has the talent to do so. Al Karsten: Jahmyr Gibbs Jahmyr Gibbs is primed to not only be the Detroit Lions’ offensive MVP this season, but contend for NFL Offensive Player of the Year while setting career highs in touches and total yards. Once the calendar flipped to November last season, Gibbs saw a significant dip in production outside of feasting on poor Commanders and Giants defenses. This season, however, he should benefit from both a rejuvenated offensive line and high-level play calling with the addition of Drew Petzing. That combination should put Gibbs in position to restore his consistent down-to-down production and explosiveness as he looks to return to a 50%+ success rate and 15%+ explosive play rate. With the Lions prepared to put even more on his plate in both the running and passing games, a 2,500+ total-yard, 20+ touchdown season is very much on the table. Erik Schlitt: Jahmyr Gibbs The Lions have made a major commitment to Gibbs this offseason and appear all-in on him as a key cog in this offense. With no David Montgomery to split carries with, it’s all-athlete, all the time. That’s the makings of an MVP-like season. Jeremy Reisman: Jahmyr Gibbs Outside of the quarterback, Gibbs is going to get the most touches of any Lions player—and that’s not just a function of him being the running back. He is the Lions’ offense. He’ll be their go-to guy for explosive plays. He’ll be their go-to guy in the red zone. He’ll be their early-down option to get into manageable downs and distances. And with no Isiah Pacheco early in the season, he’s likely to get an even bigger workload to start the year. Vote on your prediction for Lions’ Offensive MVP below!

title: Green Bay Roster: Breaking down the new Packers for 2026 and their roles
summary: As of now, the Green Bay Packers have 15 new players on their 53-man roster who weren’t a part of the team in 2025. Today, we’re going to break down every single one of these new players and what their expected roles on the team are, in case you missed any of the new from […]
full_text: Javon Hargrave #98 of the Green Bay Packers signs an autograph for a young fan during the Green Bay Packers training camp at Ray Nitschke Field in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin, on August 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As of now, the Green Bay Packers have 15 new players on their 53-man roster who weren’t a part of the team in 2025. Today, we’re going to break down every single one of these new players and what their expected roles on the team are, in case you missed any of the new from Green Bay this offseason. There are also a couple of players I want to make a note of as honorable mentions, as they were technically members of the 2025 roster, but they didn’t play in a single regular season game. Let’s dive into who the new contributors will be for this year’s team, starting off with the offensive skill players. QB Tyrod Taylor While he didn’t have a good preseason, Tyrod Taylor threw 16 passes for 8 completions (50 percent) and just 38 yards (2.4 yards per attempt). The Packers never let anyone else take significant snaps with the second-team offense during training camp. After trading away Kyle McCord to the Miami Dolphins at the cutdown deadline, Green Bay’s brass admitted that there was never really a competition for the job to back up Jordan Love, as Taylor was brought in to bring a veteran presence to the quarterback room. With proven veteran backup quarterbacks generally going in the $5 million to $8 million range, the Packers got Taylor on the cheap, as he signed a one-year, $2.5 million deal with the team shortly after the 2026 NFL Draft. Taylor has previously played for Green Bay passing game coordinator Jason Vrable, who was the assistant quarterbacks coach with the Buffalo Bills in 2016, when Taylor was the starter there. Taylor is going into his 16th season in the NFL and has played in 100 games (62 starts, with a 29-31-1 record). RB Kaleb Johnson At the cutdown deadline, just before the news that starting running back Josh Jacobs was going to be put on the commissioner exempt list , the Packers traded for former Iowa and Pittsburgh Steeler running back Kaleb Johnson . Notably, Johnson played under Hawkeyes offensive coordinator Tim Lester, who served as a senior analyst for the Packers in 2023. In 2025, Johnson was considered the 55th overall player in his draft class, according to the consensus draft board , but had some early struggles in Pittsburgh and fell down the depth chart. He’s hoping to rebound with the Packers and their return to the outside zone scheme, which he ran frequently at the college level. He should back up MarShawn Lloyd as Green Bay’s number two ball-carrying option (Chris Brooks is more of a blocking back) while Jacobs is out. WR Skyy Moore One of the few “compensatory free agents” that the Packers signed this spring was receiver Skyy Moore, who recently played for the San Francisco 49ers and Kyle Shanahan, a close friend of Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur. At the moment, it looks like Moore will be the backup slot receiver (behind Jayden Reed) offensively and also contribute as both a kick returner (at least until Savion Williams returns from his ankle injury) and as a punt returner. WR J. Michael Sturdivant The undrafted rookie streak lives on in Green Bay, and this year the man who kept it alive was former Florida (and Cal/UCLA) receiver J. Michael Sturdivant. Sturdivant should slide in behind Christian Watson as the backup Z receiver in the Packers offense while Savion Williams is sidelined, as they played similar roles (on both offense and special teams) during the summer. Sturdivant also received reps on special teams as a gunner on the punt team, a lead blocker on the punt return team and as the “off returner” (a lead blocker role, unless he’s kicked to) on the kickoff return unit. He was a lead blocker on kickoff return at the college level, too, so the 6’2.5”, 207-pound receiver with 4.40-second speed is familiar with contributing on special teams. To end the preseason, Sturdivant had his best performance of the summer, bringing in six receptions for 112 yards and a touchdown. That was the most yards a Packers receiver recorded in a single preseason game since 2011. TE Jonnu Smith Head coach Matt LaFleur has a prior connection with Jonnu Smith, as he coached Smith when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator with the Tennessee Titans. Smith is famously an off-ball tight end who at times even carries the ball. Don’t go assuming Smith is an all-around tight end who is a threat when his hand is in the dirt. He’s here to play a hybrid tight end-fullback role where he contributes to the offense by getting the ball in his hands. Look for him to help out in obvious passing situations as a yards-after-catch threat. Eventually, whenever Luke Musgrave returns from the PUP list after his neck injury, Smith should push Josh Whyle out of his role on the team. At some point, the team will probably release Whyle, hoping to land him back on their practice squad, because they’ll simply need roster numbers at another position. We didn’t get a look at Smith during the preseason, because he only officially signed with the Packers on the day of the cutdown deadline. When I’ve asked about why Green Bay didn’t wait an extra day to sign Smith, I was told that the Packers had a practice that day and they wanted Smith to participate in it, the same reasoning for why long snapper Matt Orzech spent all of training camp on the PUP list but was activated on the day of cutdowns. TE Mark Redman After the draft, general manager Brian Gutekunst stated that the team was disappointed that there wasn’t value on the board for the Packers to take a true Y tight end, as there was a crazy run at the position starting in the second round of the draft. This void was eventually filled by Mark Redman, who was traded from the Los Angeles Rams at the cutdown deadline. Worth noting: Redman was coached by Matt LaFleur’s brother, Mike, when he was the offensive coordinator with the Rams in Redman’s rookie season of 2025. we have hoss potential with Rams TE #83 Mark Redman. pic.twitter.com/2XMOJjZUA7 — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) August 28, 2026 By all accounts, Redman looks the part of a blocking tight end based on his preseason film (he didn’t play a regular-season game last year). He’s got a little more wiggle than John FitzPatrick, who played this role for the team post-Marcedes Lewis. OL Jager Burton There’s a little uncertainty on the offensive line right now, because the team has been managing the recovery of left guard Aaron Banks (tendinitis) and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (partially torn patellar tendon) throughout the summer. With that being said, Banks’ injury has given Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick, a lot of opportunities to play with the first-team offense in both training camp and in the preseason. If Banks can’t go to start the year, assume that Burton will take over at left guard (because it seems like the starting right guard job has gone to Jacob Monk). Even if Banks is “starting,” I’m not sure he won’t be rotating with Burton, which has been a common occurrence for the 5th and 6th offensive linemen under Matt LaFleur’s tenure as head coach. Burton has really good traits and does some things well for a Day 3 rookie, but he also drops his head often when making blocks, which causes him some issues on stunts — particularly. He’s green, but the faster he’s onboarded, the better the Packers will be off long-term, in my opinion. DL Javon Hargrave Because we didn’t get an extended look at Javon Hargrave in the rotation during the preseason, the veteran defensive tackle’s standing in the lineup is a bit of a question mark. There are signs that Karl Brooks is going to be the starting 3-4 defensive end opposite Devonte Wyatt, as Brooks has been pulled with the first-team defense around the same time as other established starters on defense, which leaves Hargrave’s role on the team up…
author: Justis Mosqueda

title: Green Bay Packers name team captains for 2026
summary: The Green Bay Packers have named captains in several different ways under head coach Matt LaFleur, but it appears that they’ll be rolling with a season-long set of five captains in 2026, based on the team’s announcement on Monday. In the past, the team has also rotated captains on a game-by-game basis, as we all […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Zaire Franklin #44 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have named captains in several different ways under head coach Matt LaFleur, but it appears that they’ll be rolling with a season-long set of five captains in 2026, based on the team’s announcement on Monday. In the past, the team has also rotated captains on a game-by-game basis, as we all remember the Jaire Alexander suspension back in 2023 . The Packers seem to have two offensive captains, two defensive captains and a special teams captain. On offense, the leaders are quarterback Jordan Love and tight end Tucker Kraft, who has yet to sign an extension going into the regular season . Defensively, the captains are safety Xavier McKinney and new Mike linebacker Zaire Franklin, who was traded for this offseason from the Indianapolis Colts. On special teams, the captain is linebacker Isaiah McDuffie, who has been a contributor on the unit going into Year 6 now. Notably, only 2 of the Packers’ top 11 highest-paid players made the cut for the team’s five-man set of captains. Love and McKinney made the list, but Micah Parsons, Christian Watson, Zach Bako-Bewele, Aaron Banks, Devonte Wyatt, Jayden Reed, Josh Jacobs, Javon Hargrave and Sean Rhyan all make significantly more on an average salary basis than Kraft, Franklin and McDuffie.

summary: If you can believe it, there are already people looking toward the 2027 NFL free-agent cycle. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you can believe it, there are already people looking toward the 2027 NFL free-agent cycle. Greg Rosenthal of NFL.com posted an article this week laying out the top 25 possible free agents for next year’s free-agent class heading into the 2026 regular season. Coming third on the list is the Green Bay Packers’ Tucker Kraft. Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst has stated several times this offseason that he hopes to get Kraft, who has now returned to practice as a full participant, signed to a long-term extension before the Packers’ 2026 regular season begins. So far, though, there has been no news about a new deal for the tight end. According to Rosenthal, the only players who rank ahead of Kraft are Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua and Dallas Cowboys receiver George Pickens, who was hit with the franchise tag at a $27.3 million figure in March. Here’s what Rosenthal had to say about Kraft: Both the Packers and Kraft have expressed confidence that a deal will get done soon, despite last November’s ACL tear. The 6-foot-5, 259-pounder has rare value as a complete tight end. The only other tight end on the list is Detroit Lion Sam LaPorta. It will be interesting to see which NFC North tight end ends up signing first, as whoever is second will almost certainly sign for a higher figure. They are the only two significant tight ends “due” for a new contract, following Kyle Pitts’ three-year, $54 million extension . Right now, here are the leaders at the position, in terms of average per year: George Kittle: $19.1 million per Trey McBride: $19 million per Kyle Pitts: $18 million per Isaiah Likely: $13.3 million per It seems likely that both Kraft and LaPorta will get more than Pitts, but the question is whether or not they will reset the tight end market entirely. So far, we’ve heard no details on how negotiations are going between the two parties on the Kraft deal. The Packers probably won’t be very active in free agency next year, as 2027 is when the belt will really start getting tight on the team from a cap perspective, but the top cornerbacks going into the 2027 class are the Steelers’ Joey Porter Jr., the Bengals’ DJ Turner II and the Broncos’ Riley Moss. The only running back to crack Rosenthal’s top-25 is Bengals ball-carrier Chase Brown.

title: Groupthink: Texans 2026 Season Outlook
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, you’ve arrived at Week One of the NFL Season. Soak it up, the wait is over. The Texans have Greater Expectations than Pip. Three straight AFC Divisional Round finishes has set the benchmark for this franchise. Fans and pundits expect the team to make a run, but another tough schedule and a […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Quarterback C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans leads his team onto the field ahead of the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ladies and gentlemen, you’ve arrived at Week One of the NFL Season. Soak it up, the wait is over. The Texans have Greater Expectations than Pip. Three straight AFC Divisional Round finishes has set the benchmark for this franchise. Fans and pundits expect the team to make a run, but another tough schedule and a questionable offensive line will set the terms for this team. With the season right around the corner, I checked in with the Battle Red Blog crew to gauge their hopes, expectations, and reality checks for the 2026 season. What is your outlook for the 2026 season? What record do you think the Texans will have, and if they make the playoffs how far will they go? VBallRetired: I will go 11-6 and AFC South champions. I see them losing in the divisional round again. The team will look very similar to last season with great defense and spotty offense. We will be a better running team but the passing game takes a step back without Higgins. That glass ceiling just can’t quite be broken this year. Mike Bullock: I’ll echo the 11-6, but I think this year H-Town gets another AFC Championship appearance only to lose in some gut wrenching, “this is why we can’t have nice things” sort of way. Lights-out defense, improved offense, but a few “tragic” ball bounces sets another team up to get destroyed by the LA Rams in the Super Bowl. Then the “waiting for next season since 2002” kicks back in. L4Blitzer : I’ll go with the ol’ standby of 10-7 with a +3/-2 on the record. Houston plays a difficult schedule (7th toughest) and they hopes that the offense can actually be better vs last year. If they can improve the offense and can avoid any major defensive injuries, they have a better chance to get that coveted 2 or 1 seed. However, if the offensive line can’t gel and/or Stroud is more broken from last January than we thought, then a losing record could be in play. Playoffs are likely but I won’t put them higher than the divisional round until I actually see them do it. Patrick H.: I’m gonna be optimistic and say they go 12-5, get the first round bye and get to the conference championship game. Beyond that I don’t know that I feel confident saying I like our chances against the field. So much of this hinges on four things. A) The bad/inexperienced playcalling at offensive coordinator has been resolved (only time will tell). B) The offensive line has been sufficiently addressed by the talent and depth on the roster. (11 offensive linemen made up of high draft picks, free agents, and trades on the opening roster). C) The offensive line lives up to the expectations of being at least average (a significant improvement over the last several years). D) The struggles C.J. Stroud previously experienced were caused by the problems mentioned in A, B, and C and have all been resolved. E) A crap ton of good injury luck. If all of these hold true, nothing stops this team. Kenneth L.: To quote Mike’s Why this is Houston’s Year post, Nick Caserio and Demeco Ryans have “assembled arguably the best team the Texans have ever had” in three years. Top to bottom, the Texans have the weapons, defense, and top-end talent to secure a Super Bowl. Going all the way takes more than talent. There’s health, luck, a couple good calls, and continuous roster management needed. My big prediction is that by Week 7, if the Texans are 6-1 or 5-2, the will trade their first round pick for an offensive lineman. A top-end guard on a failing team could be the difference maker for this Texans team. The weakness, it doesn’t take nine years of writing for this site to tell you that the offensive line is confounding. Neither Braden Smith (IR) or Wyatt Teller will start on this re-made (x4 seasons in a row) offensive line. There’s concern over LT Aireontae Ersery’s development and regression by Ed Ingram. I think Houston will go 12-5. Losses to Buffalo, Dallas, Jacksonville, Baltimore, and Philadelphia. These are teams that can score at will, because otherwise this defense will SWARM. I’m hoping this defense is must-watch TV for fans. I the playoffs, Houston will be without a doubt the team no one wants to face regardless of their rank. Unfortunately, I do predict another divisional round exit. Whether it’s to the emerging teams such as New England or Denver, or the stalwarts Buffalo, Kansas City, or Baltimore, someone will have our number.

title: Colts d-line could be poised for interior dominance with latest Ravens lineup update

Originally a 2023 7th round pick of the Atlanta Falcons, Gwyn was signed earlier this offseason by the Ravens. He was […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 15: Jovaughn Gwyn #54 and Andrew Vorhees #72 of the Baltimore Ravens line up against the Philadelphia Eagles during the second half of a preseason game at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to first-year head coach Jessie Minter, the Baltimore Ravens will start Jovaughn Gwyn at center over Ethan Pocic, which is a less than ideal situation for starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and their offense. Ravens HC Jesse Minter announced Jovaughn Gwyn will start at center Sunday vs. the Colts. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 7, 2026 Originally a 2023 7th round pick of the Atlanta Falcons, Gwyn was signed earlier this offseason by the Ravens. He was competing for Baltimore’s starting center job against Pocic, as well as former Colts backup center Danny Pinter, who was lost to a season-ending torn patellar tendon suffered during a late August training camp practice. During his 3-year career, the 27-year-old Gwyn has appeared in 19 career games, formerly with the Atlanta Falcons, but never started in the NFL yet—meaning he’s rather inexperienced during his first year starting with the Ravens. At right guard, Baltimore is already expected to start talented rookie 2026 first round pick Vega Ioane, so Gwyn’s additional greenness only adds to the inexperience of the Ravens interior offensive line collectively. The Colts defensive line could be poised to take advantage, particularly with a veteran savvy interior tandem of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart. Not to mention, subpackage interior pass rusher Ade Adebawore can be a handful situationally as an interior pass rusher, with his first-step twitch, quickness, and explosiveness. If the Colts interior can help shut down Derrick Henry and the Ravens ground game, while getting to Jackson early and often within the passing pocket, it would be a big boost to the Colts ultimately starting the season 1-0.

title: Colts WR Alec Pierce expected to be ready for regular season opener against Ravens

(Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to head coach Shane Steichen, Indianapolis Colts lead wideout Alec Pierce is expected to be ready for the team’s regular season opener against the Baltimore Ravens this weekend ( via ESPN’s Stephen Holder ): There wasn't really any doubt about this, but Colts coach Shane Steichen reiterates that WR Alec Pierce is right on track and will play in Sunday's opener against the Baltimore Ravens. — Stephen Holder (@HolderStephen) September 7, 2026 Having been activated off PUP, Pierce has recently been participating with his teammates in practice since last week, and the recovery timeline expectation all along is that he would be ready for Week 1—having undergone ankle/heel surgery in March. Haulcy “hasn’t been ruled in or out” by Steichen yet, as his injury status still remains fluid ( via The Athletic’s James Boyd ). If Haulcy cannot ultimately go, it would be 2nd-year safety Hunter Wohler as ‘the next man up.’

title: Ravens Colts Preview: How Shane Steichen Dominated Jesse Minter’s Defense in 2025
summary: We made it! Week 1 is finally here. With new players and coaching staffs all across the league, especially with continuity being a scarcity, it’s tough to predict what every team could look like early on. So although we have very little information of how Jessie Minter will deploy the Ravens defense in 2026, we […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Alec Pierce #14 and head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts celebrate after their team's touchdown in the third quarter of a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images We made it! Week 1 is finally here. With new players and coaching staffs all across the league, especially with continuity being a scarcity, it’s tough to predict what every team could look like early on. So although we have very little information of how Jessie Minter will deploy the Ravens defense in 2026, we do know what happened the last time the Colts played a Minter led defense. The Colts embarrassed the Chargers with 38 points, 5 TDs, and over 400 yards. At halftime it was 23-3, and while the defense got gassed and let the Chargers offense start to come alive, the offense dominated from start to finish. Watching back Shane Steichen vs. Jessie Minter from last year. Steichen absolutely had his way with this defense. They played so much quarters and he just attacked the flats all day long. pic.twitter.com/BM9JTj7uh8 — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 1, 2026 I mean this respectfully, because there is zero doubt Minter is a good coach, but I was shocked at how “vanilla” his defense looked vs. the Colts. There was a lot of quarters, and not much pre-snap disguise. One of the weaknesses to a quarters defense is the flats. Corners are mostly going to be 7 yards off and the quarter flat defender is not leveraged to cover that type of ground underneath the corner. Every coverage has its weaknesses, and all in all, defensive coaches do not care if the best answer to beating quarters is attacking the flats. That being said, Minter never trapped the flat or made any sort of notable adjustment to stop the Colts from chipping away and Steichen just stayed patient and attacked the flats all day long. These charts usually lack some context. But I think it tells a good story of how Shane Steichen wanted to attack Jesse Minter's quarters centric defense in 2025. pic.twitter.com/FMTPd7rAs3 — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 7, 2026 As you can see there wasn’t a ton of air yards on a lot of these throws, but that’s sort of the safe nature of attacking quarters. Daniel Jones was very efficient finding completions underneath and outside the hashes. But it wasn’t just about attacking the structure of the defense Minter wanted to play. That’s only half the story. Even when they didn't play quarters Steichen found ways to get the ball to the perimeter off of run actions. He had them in a blender. It was the best coached game in Steichen's tenure by far, but also that we've seen from a Colts coach in quite some time. https://t.co/KVH2mtNRa0 pic.twitter.com/e82UPJkMsQ — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 1, 2026 Steichen wanted to get the ball on the perimeter as much as he could, thats where the YAC exists. When the Chargers were loading the box on run downs to stop Taylor, who was running the ball well in this game, Steichen used run actions to move the pocket and get players like Tyler Warren the ball in space. He wanted these linebackers running sideline to sideline whenever possible. HOW WILL THINGS CHANGE IN WEEK 1 ? I think Jessie Minter and Ravens DC Anthony Weaver will be much more intentional of stacking the box and dedicated a resources to stopping Jonathan Taylor. Yes, reports coming out of Colts camp are that Daniel Jones has looked great since he’s been cleared from his achilles injury, and that Alec Pierce should be a go for Week 1. But while that’s great for the Colts, it’s an opposing team’s job to make you prove that. I don’t expect many light boxes for the Colts in Week 1, at least until the Colts punish them for it. Additionally, I expect Anthony Weaver to have a lot of tricks up his sleeve. He’s challenged the Colts, both in 2024 and 2025, in blocking up exotic pressures. I don’t expect the Colts to coast offensively. It should be a real battle.

title: Colts seek to start new streak after slaying old one
summary: Opening week in the NFL is special. After a long offseason, the beginning of a new season brings renewed hope and excitement. Although not always the end of the world, one way to dampen that joy is to lose Week One. The Indianapolis Colts put on a master class of that by going winless since […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 7: Tyler Warren #84 of the Indianapolis Colts runs the ball against Tyrel Dodson #25 of the Miami Dolphins during the NFL 2025 game between Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 7, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Opening week in the NFL is special. After a long offseason, the beginning of a new season brings renewed hope and excitement. Although not always the end of the world, one way to dampen that joy is to lose Week One. The Indianapolis Colts put on a master class of that by going winless since 2013. That decade-plus streak was painful, but it was sweet release when they finally ended the futility by beating the Dolphins last year. With one streak over, the Colts are looking to start a new one. The Dolphins were bad last year. No one knew how bad when the Colts beat the absolute brakes off them, but then again, the Colts were world beaters to start the season. They will have to regain that form if they are going to win against the Ravens. There are a few advantages working in the Colts’ favor. Being at home is always a benefit. It hasn’t always translated into wins but a home game to start the season is more palatable than a road contest. The Colts also have decent health. Some players have dings, but they should be close to full go. Daniel Jones is ready and has an offseason under his belt with the team. The Ravens will prove to be a formidable opening opponent. Lamar Jackson is one of the best in the game. His elusiveness will be a challenge for the Colts to contain. Early projections have the Ravens winning 10-11 games with 9 out of 10 fans feeling optimistic about the season. Winning the AFC North is the target which means they don’t plan on faltering against the Colts. The Colts broke their Week One curse. Now is the time to start a new streak. It won’t be easy, but why should it be? If the Colts can win against the Ravens, it would prove to be a fantastic measuring stick. It would be an early feather in their cap. Let a new streak begin!

full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 14: Travis Kelce #87 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs onto the field prior to the NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL regular season begins this week and ends with a “Monday Night Football” matchup between the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos . Before the action starts on Wednesday night, let’s see where the Chiefs stand in the minds of national football writers. Here’s this week’s sampling: NFL.com : 14 A smooth offseason and seemingly successful return to action for Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City in a place of relative stability entering 2026. There is valid concern regarding left tackle Josh Simmons’ status, though, which isn’t great news for those hoping for a safe start to the season for Mahomes. There’s also the new-look secondary, which hasn’t been tested yet, leaving plenty of questions for the Chiefs to answer when they welcome the AFC West rival Broncos to Arrowhead Stadium on Monday night. — Nick Shook ESPN : 13 Entering this season, Kelce has 13,002 receiving yards. All he needs is 45 yards to surpass Jason Witten for the second most by a tight end in NFL history. Fans can expect Kelce to reach this next accomplishment in the Chiefs’ season opener against the Broncos, a rival he has tormented throughout his Hall of Fame-worthy career. Mahomes, who is expected to be ready for Week 1 after knee surgery, has always made Kelce his go-to pass catcher on third down. It’s possible Kelce passes Witten on a third down before the “Monday Night Football” halftime show. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 14 Last ranking: 18 First game: vs. Broncos, Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET Mock’s projected win total: 9.6 Our last power rankings assumed Patrick Mahomes would probably miss the start of the season. Astoundingly, even though he suffered an ACL tear in mid-December, it looks like he will be the Chiefs’ starting quarterback out of the gate. There is still plenty that ailed the Chiefs a year ago (and could again this year), but it’d be wise not to bet against Mahomes. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 13 When it’s time to call the plays, will they truly commit to the run? — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 12 Don’t go sleeping on the Chiefs. As long as Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid are together, they will be in the playoff mix and more. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 12 Patrick Mahomes is likely going to start in Week 1 coming off an ACL surgery, but it will be a bit of an unusual Week 1 for him. Mahomes and the rest of the Chiefs’ starters usually log some time in the preseason. Mahomes didn’t play at all this preseason as the Chiefs played it safe with him. However, in 2020, when there were no preseason games due to the pandemic, Mahomes had 11 touchdowns and no interceptions in his first four games. We’ll see if he looks rusty early this season. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 13 While focus is justifiably trained on the Super Bowl MVP backfield of QB Patrick Mahomes and RB Kenneth Walker III, plenty should be devoted to a revamped defense − the secondary especially − that was quietly one of the league’s stingiest in K.C.’s lost 2025 campaign. — Nate Davis FOX Sports : 15 Patrick Mahomes may be on track to start the season opener, but will he be the same old superstar? The Chiefs have the chance to rise or fall quickly in these rankings based on the early answer to that. — Ralph Vacchiano

Kickoff is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. The game will be broadcast nationally on ABC and ESPN. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Kansas […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Chris Jones #95 of the Kansas City Chiefs rushes the passer during an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images To cap off Week 1 of the NFL season, on Monday evening, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the Denver Broncos for a “Monday Night Football” bout at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:15 p.m. The game will be broadcast nationally on ABC and ESPN . According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Kansas City begins the week as a 2.5-point favorite. The last time these two franchises faced off was Christmas Day at Arrowhead; Denver closed as a 13.5-point favorite against the Chiefs without quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City covered, but the Broncos pulled away from a tie game in the fourth quarter to win 20-13 . Of course, Denver’s victory sealed the clean sweep of the Chiefs in 2025: in Week 11, the Chiefs were four-point favorites on the road against the Broncos, but lost 22-19 . In the 2026 preseason, the Chiefs were defeated by the Los Angeles Rams and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before tying with the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos beat the Atlanta Falcons and Minnesota Vikings , but lost to the Green Bay Packers .

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . Arrowhead through the years: Chiefs begin new season with games numbered at historic venue | KCTV 5 With a 2031 kickoff date for Chiefs games in Kansas, a finite number of games — somewhere just north of 40, depending on the Chiefs’ participation in international games and the playoffs — remain to be played at historic Arrowhead Stadium. Before the Chiefs kick off another season of play at Arrowhead on Monday, Sept. 14, under the primetime lights against the Denver Broncos, here’s a look back at how we arrived here before the final half-decade of football at the iconic venue. 8 things I think I know about the Kansas City Chiefs ahead of the 2026 NFL season opener against the Denver Broncos | A to Z Sports Steve Spagnuolo’s defense will look sharper than it typically does in Week 1 Typically, when you have a lot of changes and new personnel on any side of the ball, it takes time for those pieces to mesh and gel into a cohesive unit. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense has traditionally taken time to get into the swing of football once the season starts. However, this season things looked and felt a little different during the preseason. The Chiefs did not have their full complement of players due to injury. However, the players who were there and starting for Kansas City felt up to the task, especially late in the preseason. That starting unit was locked down and playing against units that were mostly a mishmash of starters and second-stringers. One bold prediction for every NFL team: Vikings are NFC North champion; Drake Maye wins MVP | The Athletic Kansas City Chiefs: Xavier Worthy will post his first 1,000-yard season Chiefs third-year receiver Xavier Worthy didn’t get much training-camp hype because he had to sit out most drills while protecting a shoulder injury. It’s too bad. He was the Chiefs’ practice MVP over summer drills and is in line for an expanded role after the team purposely limited his route tree last season as he played through a torn labrum. Worthy is still only 23 and should be a full go in Week 1. I think he easily clears his career high of 638 yards from his rookie season — and even gets to 1,000 while flashing higher upside. — Jesse Newell Patrick Mahomes offers support to Chiefs analyst after tragedy | Awful Announcing Tucker Franklin is a beloved host, producer, and all-around personality on KC Sports Network (KCSN) in Kansas City. He was reminded just how beloved he is when tragedy struck last week. Doug Franklin, Tucker’s father, unexpectedly passed away on Aug. 31. Franklin shared the news on X (formerly Twitter), and the sports media community, both locally and nationally, rallied around him to the tune of 595 replies. And while Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is preparing to face the Denver Broncos in Week 1 after making a miraculous recovery from a torn ACL, he also had Franklin on his mind. Forget the stars. These 4 Chiefs players could quietly decide games in 2026 | The Kansas City Star WR Xavier Worthy Worthy was “never 100 %,” he said during training camp in St. Joseph. The consequences of that included, he said, not being able to “run a lot of the things that I would normally run … in the way that I would want to.” So doubt him if you must. And yes, it’s hard not to attach an asterisk here because of reasonable questions about his health and durability. Most of all, though, consider this: In the last game he was fully healthy, Worthy had eight catches for 157 yards and two touchdowns in the otherwise wretched 40-22 Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles. That night, he looked a whole lot like the future for the Chiefs. He still can be. – Vahe Gregorian Around the NFL Sources: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots reach 4-year, $135M deal | ESPN The New England Patriots and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez have agreed to terms on a four-year, $135 million extension, sources told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler late Monday night. The deal includes $102 million guaranteed, sources said. Giants release WR Darius Slayton, team’s longest-tenured player | ESPN The Giants signed Slayton to a three-year, $36 million deal before last season. He was due $13 million this season. The move creates just over $3 million in cap space for this year. “Grateful for my time in NY. 7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next,” he posted to X on Monday. Falcons name Tua Tagovailoa starting QB for Week 1 vs. Steelers; Michael Penix Jr. to be inactive | NFL.com Stefanski told reporters on Monday that Penix, who has been working his way back from last year’s season-ending knee injury, will be inactive against Pittsburgh on Sept. 13. Cooper Rush will serve as Tagovailoa’s backup. “Mike is getting better and better and better, and I’m very proud of him for how far he’s come,” Stefanski said, “but this will continue to be something that we work (on) together with Mike. We’re all on the same page, which is great between myself, Mike, medical, you name it. Everybody feels good about where Mike is heading, and he’ll continue just to work like crazy. That’s his focus, and I think he’s told you guys that. He’s gonna focus on trying to get better every single day.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Will Chiefs’ offense or defense rank higher in 2026? It’s a tough question. Last season, the Chiefs’ defense finished sixth in points allowed and 10th in total yards allowed; the offense finished 21st and 20th in the same categories, respectively. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s unit has outranked the offense in both for three consecutive seasons. In 2022, the last season before offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy initially left the staff, the offense ranked first in points and yards while the defense ranked 16th and 11th. That was the last time the Chiefs’ offense clearly drove the team’s success. title: Monday Musings: Will Chiefs’ offense or defense rank higher in 2026?
summary: With a week to go until the Kansas City Chiefs kick off the 2026 regular season against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football,” it’s time to think about the year as a whole and how it could play out. I joined Jay Binkley of 96.5 The Fan for a Chiefs discussion on the Kansas […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy of the Kansas City Chiefs watches during pregame warm-ups prior to the preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images With a week to go until the Kansas City Chiefs kick off the 2026 regular season against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football,” it’s time to think about the year as a whole and how it could play out. I joined Jay Binkley of 96.5 The Fan for a Chiefs discussion on the Kansas City airwaves on Monday morning and enjoyed thinking through the last question Jay asked: By the end of the season, which unit will be better? Offense or Defense? It’s a tough question. Last season, the Chiefs’ defense finished sixth in points allowed and 10th in total yards allowed; the offense finished 21st and 20th in the same categories, respectively. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s unit has outranked the offense in both for three consecutive seasons. In 2022, the last season before offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy initially left the staff, the offense ranked first in points and yards while the defense ranked 16th and 11th. That was the last time the Chiefs’ offense clearly drove the team’s success. Still, I see the Chiefs’ defense outranking the offense this season. The rookies will come on as the season progresses under Spags, especially pass rusher R Mason Thomas and cornerback Mansoor Delane, and could be a top-10 or top-8 unit by season’s end. The offense may not be putting up the gaudy statistics that quarterback Patrick Mahomes has before, but a strong run game should give the offense a higher floor than the last few seasons.

title: Another game-by-game prediction for the Chiefs’ 2026 season
summary: The NFL regular season is back! After months of waiting, football returns to our televisions Wednesday evening. Before the games kick off, I wanted to predict the record and what level of team we have in the Kansas City Chiefs this season. We’re following the optimistic perspective from Rocky Magana’s 12-5 prediction last week. Let’s […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs watches second quarter game action during an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL regular season is back! After months of waiting, football returns to our televisions Wednesday evening. Before the games kick off, I wanted to predict the record and what level of team we have in the Kansas City Chiefs this season. We’re following the optimistic perspective from Rocky Magana’s 12-5 prediction last week . Let’s get started with Week 1 against the Denver Broncos . Week 1: vs. Broncos I’m starting the season with a loss. I don’t love the Chiefs-Broncos matchup. The Broncos have a secondary that can blanket Kansas City’s pass catchers, and one of the most ferocious pass rushes in the NFL. On top of this, left tackle Josh Simmons might not play. Without Simmons, I don’t think the Chiefs will be able to pass protect long enough for receivers to get open. I expect the defense to keep the score close, but don’t trust the offense. Verdict: Loss Week 2: vs. Indianapolis Colts The good news for the Chiefs is if Simmons misses some time, the next three opponents don’t have fierce pass rushes. The Chiefs offense should look much better in this game. The Colts offense isn’t as strong this year without Michael Pittman and Braden Smith. With Daniel Jones off an injury as well, the Chiefs bounce back. Verdict: Win Week 3: at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins are going to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. This should be an easy win for the Chiefs. Verdict: Win Week 4: at Las Vegas Raiders Maxx Crosby could give us some problems, but it appears Kirk Cousins will be starting for the Raiders in this game. I expect the Chiefs pass rush to dominate against a shaky offensive line and an old, immobile quarterback. We go into the bye 3-1. Verdict: Win Week 5: Bye Week 3-1 Record! Week 6: vs. Los Angeles Chargers At this point, the hope is Simmons will be back. I expect the Chiefs to split their series with the Chargers this year. I think the Chargers will start the season stronger as they have a new offensive scheme with Mike McDaniel that won’t have much tape on them yet. I do think they will slow down as time goes on, but this is still early enough in the season for them to give us problems. Verdict: Loss Week 7: at Seattle Seahawks The Chiefs defense will keep this game close, but I don’t trust our offense against Mike McDonald. Seattle is best at defending the middle of the field and limiting the open windows the Chiefs want to attack. They will make the Chiefs throw outside the numbers against our receivers, and I don’t trust the Chiefs to hit enough throws to move the ball. This is a tough matchup for this roster. Verdict: Loss Week 8: at Broncos As I mentioned, I just think Denver is a bad matchup for us. For two years, the Broncos secondary has smothered the Chiefs. Even with Simmons back, their pass rush and blitzing can still get home. The Broncos offense should be better with Jaylen Waddle at wide receiver. The Chiefs need to make upgrades to their roster to match up with Denver better. Verdict: Loss Week 9: vs New York Jets The previous three games are a brutal way to come out of the bye, but fortunately, the next three should be wins. The Jets are also one of the worst teams in the NFL, and I expect the Chiefs to play desperate in this spot. I would predict a Chiefs blowout in this game. Verdict: Win Week 10: at Atlanta Falcons I expect the Chiefs to keep that positive momentum into Atlanta. The Falcons quarterback situation is pretty dire, and their pass rush is one of the worst in the NFL. These games should give the Chiefs a chance to catch an offensive rhythm. Verdict: Win Week 11: vs. Arizona Cardinals The Cardinals’ skill-position talent is exciting, and they have a young defense. Of these three easier games, I think this one will be the most competitive. But the Chiefs still have much more talent than the Cardinals. The Chiefs’ defense chokes out whoever plays quarterback for the Cardinals in this game. Verdict: Win Week 12: at Buffalo Bill s After three easier games, the schedule gets tough again with Buffalo on a short week. Joe Brady is a different coach, but the Bills have consistently beaten the Chiefs in the regular season. I expect the Chiefs’ defense to play well this year, but I think the Bills run the ball well in this game, and I think the Chiefs lose a close game late. Verdict: Loss Week 13: at Los Angeles Rams The Rams have one of the most loaded rosters in recent NFL years. They have a chance to have top-3 units on both sides of the ball. I could see the Chiefs keeping it close with their game plan, but the Rams’ defense, with Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, closes it out. Verdict: Loss Week 14: vs. Cincinnati Bengals After two tough losses, I think the Chiefs bounce back in a shootout in Cincinnati. The Chiefs’ run game takes off here for the rest of the year. The Bengals also score points, but Kansas City’s young defenders make big plays late to close out the win. Verdict: Win Week 15: vs. New England Patriots This was a tough one for me to pick, but I ended up having this as a loss. The Patriots secondary is very good in man coverage and could stifle our passing game. Drake Maye is really good and can make aggressive throws to beat our defense. This is a close game that goes down to the wire that New England pulls out. Verdict: Loss Week 16: vs. San Francisco 49ers San Francisco has so many injured players already, and they’re an old team. I don’t expect them to play well this late into the season. The Chiefs roll in this game. Verdict: Win Week 17: at Chargers By this point, I expect the Chargers to show more cracks, and the Chiefs will be peaking. The Chiefs go into Los Angeles and win by double digits as they dominate the Chargers’ shaky interior offensive line and run the ball well. Verdict: Win Week 18: vs. Raiders Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will probably be playing by then, but with the Chiefs at 10-7 and likely needing this win for their playoff hopes, they come out focused and end the game early. Verdict: Win Bottom Line Overall, I had the Chiefs at 10-7. The light early schedule besides Denver should give them a chance to start 3-1. Their stretch after the bye week and after Arizona is brutal, but Kansas City does have lighter stretches as well. By December, I expect them to be playing their best football as the run game develops and the defense improves over time. Teams that can play man coverage well will be a tough matchup for us, which caps the Chiefs’ record for me, but I think they’ll be in the mix to make the playoffs.

Giants reach 2-year extensions with Jameis Winston, Jon Runyan | ESPN The New York Giants extended backup quarterback Jameis Winston through the 2028 season on a two-year deal worth $13 million, sources told ESPN on Sunday. I don’t even get how that’s possible,” Shanahan said. “So I feel like I’m in the future. And then also when we play on Friday, which I think is a Thursday in the US, we’re such creatures of habit.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs sign international tight end, release 3 from IR On Friday, the Chiefs reached injury settlements with three players who were waived/injured during Sunday’s final roster cuts. Quarterback Chris Oladokun, guard CJ Hanson and running back EJ Smith have all been waived from Kansas City’s Reserve/Injured (IR) list. Players with less than four accrued seasons who are cut while injured revert to a team’s IR if unclaimed on waivers. An injury settlement has the player and team negotiate an estimated recovery timeframe and pay a prorated portion of base salary to cover the expected missed weeks. The covered timeline rarely becomes public. After the settlement expires, Oladokun, Hanson and Smith will be free to join the active roster or practice squad of any of the NFL’s other 31 teams. A return to Kansas City will not be possible for an additional three weeks after that. summary: Myles Garrett has been reportedly nursing a bit of an injury over part of this past offseason, but as far as the Los Angeles Rams are concerned, Garrett should be good to go against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday. L.A. is expected to have it’s key players ready to roll come Game 1. How […]
full_text: Myles Garrett has been reportedly nursing a bit of an injury over part of this past offseason, but as far as the Los Angeles Rams are concerned, Garrett should be good to go against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday. L.A. is expected to have it’s key players ready to roll come Game 1 . How excited must the NFL be to have this first ever NFL game in Australia happening, but they also get to have Garrett and Aaron Donald as major talking points for the event. This game should draw plenty of eyes, and they are should be no shortage of storylines including, how will Garrett look in his first game with the Rams? Football is not only coming. It’s here. Los Angeles Rams Get Encouraging Intel on Myles Garrett (sports.yahoo) “Garrett and the Rams play their regular-season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, and the expectation is that the star EDGE will be close to 100%. “Garrett … had a little bit of inflammation, I would say, in training camp,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on “Good Morning Football” on September 7. “I don’t expect him to be limited at all. Really don’t believe that there’ll be an issue with him. There’s always going to be a little bit of maintenance, but he is a freakazoid athlete.” Davante Adams’ Australia research takes deadly turn before Rams opener (sports.yahoo) “Asked whether he researched the country before the Rams’ historic season opener against the 49ers , Adams bypassed Melbourne’s coffee, architecture and sports culture for its most dangerous residents. “I think probably what’s typical for Americans to know — the spiders and how dangerous the waters are with all of the octopus,” Adams said. “The most venomous octopus in the world is found there. We got great whites on the south. I think it’s the saltwater crocs on the north. Koalas and stuff a little bit more inland.” 327-Pound Former LA Rams ‘Bowling Ball’ Signs With Raiders (heavy.com) ““We have … signed DT Tim Keenan II and TE Patrick Gurd to the practice squad,” the Las Vegas Raiders announced in a post on X on September 7. “In a corresponding move, we have released DT Gary Smith and S Devin Lafayette from the practice squad. Notably, the Rams will face the Raiders in Las Vegas in Week 7 during the 2026 regular season, giving Keenan an opportunity to exact some measure of revenge.” Los Angeles Rams vs. San Francisco 49ers: How to watch, listen to and live stream Week 1 (therams.com) Los Angeles Rams vs. San Francisco 49ers: How to watch, listen to and live stream Week 1 (therams) “The Rams and 49ers last met in Week 10 of the 2025 season, a 42-26 Rams victory in San Francisco. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 280 yards and four touchdowns with wide receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua, and tight ends Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen on the receiving end of those touchdowns. Running back Kyren Williams had 73 rushing yards and two touchdowns and Blake Corum added 56 yards on the ground. Defensively, cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. had an interception and also led the team with two pass breakups. Inside linebacker Nate Landman had two tackles for loss and 11 total tackles, the latter tied for most on the team alongside safety Quentin Lake and inside linebacker Omar Speights.” Rams’ Former 800-Yard WR Back With Commanders Days After Release (sports.yahoo) “A member of the Los Angeles Rams’ Super Bowl LVI championship offense is staying in the NFL after a short stint on the open market. Former Rams wide receiver Van Jefferson is re-signing with the Washington Commanders on their practice squad, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported. The move comes eight days after Washington released Jefferson during its final roster reduction.“ Do you expect Rams to dominate out of the gate or will it be a work in progress? | ‘GMFB’ (nfl.com) “GMFB” debate if the Los Angeles Rams to dominate out of the gate or will it be a work in progress.“ NFL betting storylines: Rams’ dominance, a healthy midfield and long-shot liabilities (espn.com) “After being one of the top teams in the 2025 regular season and falling just short of the NFL’s championship game, the Los Angeles Rams opened as one of the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI. After a frenetic offseason that saw them bolster an already elite roster, the Rams’ odds to win the big game have been pushed “over the top,” according to bookmakers. At +500, Los Angeles is the favorite to win the title for the 2026 season, with the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens the next closest teams at a distant 10-1, per DraftKings odds. Since 1995, that’s the sixth-largest gap between the favorite and second favorite, according to data from SportsOddsHistory found by ESPN Research. “This is about as short as a favorite tends to get in the NFL before the season starts,” BetMGM trading manager Christian Cipollini told ESPN. “It tends to happen more in different sports, but football is more of a level playing field.” 49ers vs. Rams preview | Week 1 (nfl.com) “Here’s everything you need to know when the San Francisco 49ers play the Los Angeles Rams Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.” The Rams Play In Australia In Two Days And They Haven’t Left Yet (defector) “Before the NFL season kicks off this weekend, it will kick off Wednesday night with a primetime game between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks. And then on Thursday night it will kick off again, with a game between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams, except that game will actually be happening on Friday morning, on account of it being played in Melbourne, Australia. Probably nobody should ask the Rams what day it is when they arrive for the game, because they won’t have much time to get acclimated. They aren’t leaving Los Angeles until tonight. “ Rams’ 2026 Offseason: Win Now, Draft Later (athlonsports) “Not every move was about winning now. Drafting Ty Simpson at No. 13 overall is a bet on the future, the highest pick Snead and head coach Sean McVay have spent on a quarterback, even with Stafford’s own timeline still alive. Critics wanted the pick used elsewhere, given Stafford was coming off an MVP season.“ Comment of the Day: “I would expect any decent coach to try to exploit the weakness of the opposing team’s defense and avoid their strengths. For Rams’ opponents this year, that means trying to take advantage of our linebackers. Short crossing routes across the middle, quarterback scrambles, screen passes, etc. would all be at the top of my list if I was a defensive coordinator going up against the Rams this year.” -Ghost_80 Feedpost of the Day:

title: What will the NFL standings look like in 2026?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are heavily favored to win the Super Bowl in February and came out nicely in these NFL standings predictions for the 2026 season. However, that’s not all when looking ahead to the season, which starts with a Seahawks-Patriots title rematch on Wednesday. Plenty of other surprises are in store in these […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - DECEMBER 18: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams scores a touchdown during overtime against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on December 18, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are heavily favored to win the Super Bowl in February and came out nicely in these NFL standings predictions for the 2026 season. However, that’s not all when looking ahead to the season, which starts with a Seahawks-Patriots title rematch on Wednesday. Plenty of other surprises are in store in these projections, including where the Cowboys and Bengals finish after defensive overalls, who the actual worst team in the NFL is and potential upheaval in the NFC North. It’s time to dive into some NFL regular season standings predictions to see what the Rams will be up against. Turf Show Ramily, I’d also love to see any predictions you have — or to tell me how full of it I am — in the comments. Let’s do this! AFC East Bills (12-5) Patriots (11-6) Dolphins (4-13) Jets (4-13) The Bills whiffed on their last best chance to make a Super Bowl run in 2025, with the Chiefs and Ravens missing the playoffs. Not much should change in Buffalo, even with a new coach in the fold. Josh Allen is still incredible and should compete for MVP honors. He’s the glue keeping that team together. Overall, the Bills are a well-rounded team that will be good enough to lose to KC for the umpteenth time. New England, coming off an AFC title, is a good team that benefited from a painfully easy schedule and a lucky string of playoff opponents to get to the Super Bowl. The Patriots will be a major player in the conference again. A.J. Brown will be a downgrade in the offense after letting Stefon Diggs walk, though. He wasn’t great towards the end of his time in Philly. Guess we’ll see what chemistry he really has with Drake Maye. The Dolphins and Jets are lumped into one since they’ll both be awful. I anticipate the Jets will actually be the worst team in the division, with Miami coming out just ahead. Congrats? Now, the Dolphins have the worst roster, while New York has the worst coaching staff, and that will make the difference. Aaron Glenn is a terrible head coach and might be the first coach fired when his team’s season inevitably goes south. Either way, both directionless franchises are trapped in a top-heavy division. Not ideal. AFC North Ravens (12-5) Bengals (10-7) Steelers (8-9) Browns (4-13) The Ravens had a lot of bad luck in 2025, yet things should be better under new coach Jesse Minter. Lamar Jackson is one of the league’s best quarterbacks and will return to his MVP ways under the new leadership. Baltimore has a painfully easy start to the year, which could help boost their chances at the AFC’s top seed later in the season. The Bengals have the most experienced coach in the division, something not brag-worthy in the slightest, but could help them in the long run. Much of Cincy’s success will hinge on two things: Joe Burrow ’s health and the defense. An average defense will get them back to the playoffs. Let their powerful offense do the rest. Pittsburgh should’ve pulled the trigger on a full rebuild the second Mike Tomlin stepped down. The Steelers are too old and don’t resemble a playoff team. Though, with all their big names, this team would’ve kicked ass five years ago. Mike McCarthy was such an uninspired hire for them. They had a chance to hop on the trend of young offensive minds and instead chose a dinosaur. McCarthy is a good coach, just not what the Steelers needed. Also, Aaron Rodgers and McCarthy didn’t work towards the end of their time in Green Bay, so no one should expect the sequel to go any differently. Even without Myles Garrett , the Browns should be set on defense. They have to be good since their quarterback situation is so putrid. No matter who starts under center won’t matter. This is a poverty franchise whose owners made a stupid call in naming Deshaun Watson the starter. Oh, you thought the coaching staff made that call? Man, it must be nice to be that naive. AFC South Texans (11-6) Jaguars (10-7) Colts (7-10) Titans (5-12) Houston might have a problem at the quarterback spot if CJ Stroud continues his decline. However, that defense will keep them in every game this season. Everyone wants to give the Rams and Seahawks the nod for the best defense, but the Texans are most deserving of that title. Their red-hot finish last season after a sluggish start will carry over as they reclaim the NFC South. Jacksonville should again be a playoff fixture under second-year coach Liam Coen. Trevor Lawrence hasn’t been anything special in the NFL despite flashes, yet he came into his own under Coen throughout the second half of the season. This guy Trevor Lawrence is pretty good at football. RT to #ProBowlVote ! #NYJvsJAX on CBS pic.twitter.com/0aRrNO8Ase — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) December 14, 2025 His progression will be something to monitor as the Jaguars look to make a deep playoff run. The Colts are all aboard the hot mess express. Indianapolis will do enough to remain in the playoff hunt until the final month of the season. I’m not expecting Daniel Jones to build on what he began there, so expect the Colts to be in the QB market again next offseason. Don’t be surprised if Tennessee fields a top 10 defense this season. Robert Saleh is an excellent defensive-minded coach, which the Titans will need since Cam Ward apparently can’t hit the broad side of a barn. Saleh will need the best coaching job of his career if his new team hopes to go anywhere, or else it’ll be his Jets tenure all over again. AFC West Broncos (12-5) Chiefs (10-7) Chargers (10-7) Raiders (6-11) The Broncos surprised many people last year en route to earning the AFC’s top seed. Denver won’t have that luxury in 2026, yet they have a top five roster in the sport. Bo Nix will certainly enjoy throwing to new target Jaylen Waddle, and Sean Payton handing off playcalling duties might be the jumpstart the offense needed. The defense will also be chasing an NFL single-season sack record after finishing with 68 last season. They’ll remain the class of a weak conference, even if their win total dips slightly. With Patrick Mahomes back, the Chiefs should return to playoff contention after an off year. Kansas City lost many pieces via trade and free agency, including a couple to the Rams in Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . Even though they’re not a player in the Super Bowl picture, count out Mahomes and Andy Reid at your own risk. The Chargers are a middling AFC team that’s only relevant because they play in a weak conference. Los Angeles has been outclassed in back-to-back playoff appearances under Jim Harbaugh , and not much should change this season. They’ll be good enough to make the playoffs, but nothing more, which is the story of their team under Harbaugh. Las Vegas should be much improved after moving on quickly from the disastrous Pete Carroll era, even if that’s not well reflected in the win column. First-year coach Klint Kubiak has several young playmakers to work with, like Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. The Raiders will be a handful for opposing defenses. People will look back & wonder how he slipped to late-RD2. — David J.
