title: Why Brock Purdy is a unique challenge to Rams’ new defense
summary: The Los Angeles Rams hope that Week 1 brings a coming out party for Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and their new-look defense. One man stands in the way. Brock Purdy is the last quarterback you want to face if planning to fill up the box score with sacks. Purdy—while still trying to prove he belongs […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 20: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before the preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams hope that Week 1 brings a coming out party for Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and their new-look defense. One man stands in the way. Brock Purdy is the last quarterback you want to face if planning to fill up the box score with sacks. Purdy—while still trying to prove he belongs in the NFL’s elite—is a unique challenge for defenses. He holds the ball longer than most and somehow is still rarely sacked. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), out of all quarterbacks that meet the 2025 20% dropback threshold, Purdy boasted the lowest pressure-to-sack ratio at just 9.0%. Purdy, Bo Nix, and Caleb Williams were the only signal callers in the single digits. The NFL average is in the high teens. QB at fault sack leaders: 23 – Geno Smith 21 – Josh Allen 21 – Cam Ward 17 – Aaron Rodgers 17 – Dak Prescott 17 – Justin Herbert 15 – Baker Mayfield 15 – Jaxson Dart 14 – Sam Darnold 14 – Dillon Gabriel pic.twitter.com/NpeHWQ5ZnS — Steven Patton (@PattonAnalytics) January 6, 2026 More impressive is the fact that Purdy also had the fourth-longest time to throw at 3.23 seconds. Williams was a tick longer at 3.24 seconds. This is the modern prototype—extend to help receivers and avoid negative plays. So if you think that Garrett and Donald are going to feast against a lesser talented 49ers offensive line, you may want to reconsider. And, strangely, the Rams do not know Purdy well. He’s played just three games against the Rams: one in 2023 and two in 2024. Mac Jones started both games against LA last season. It’s rare to have such a lack of familiarity for an entrenched starter within the division. But Purdy isn’t exactly superman. There are ways the Rams can get the better of him. It will simply take more than a strong pass rush to get the job done, and this is where LA has historically come up short against the 49ers. Where Rams can find an advantage How often NFL QBs turned the ball over in 2025 pic.twitter.com/efy8fLj6oB — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 4, 2026 Don’t expect to see much of a deep passing game from Purdy and San Francisco. Purdy was the sixth-least aggressive signal caller in terms of attempts aimed more than 20 yards down the field last season, comprising 9.9% of his passes. He completed just 18 of 34 passes for 514 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions. Purdy’s turnover-worthy play rate of 17.6% on deep balls was the second-worst behind only Tua Tagovailoa. The 49ers will probably limit how often they ask Purdy to push the ball downfield—especially against an aggressive pass rush. LA can turn the table by building a lead early and forcing San Francisco’s hand. Win on first and second down to put him behind the chains on third and long. They cannot allow Purdy to protect a lead. If and when Purdy does throw downfield, the secondary must capitalize on opportunities for takeaways. The ideal scenario is that the Rams are able to paint Purdy into a corner and ask him to win the game with his arm. Kyle Shanahan will have a smart script. LA must get him out of it. The Rams’ defense is built for a different type of quarterback than Brock Purdy. It will be a unique challenge for LA’s new-look unit. Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and Trent McDuffie can get the job done. It just may look different in the season opener than it does against others over the rest of the year.
author: JB Scott

title: Puka Nacua, A.J. Jackson expected to play against 49ers
summary: A suspension could come later but as it stands, the Los Angeles Rams are expected to have both Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackon for Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, despite any off-field issues the two players have had this past offseason. Adam Schefter believes Nacua could avoid a suspension entirely. It’s big news […]
full_text: A suspension could come later but as it stands, the Los Angeles Rams are expected to have both Puka Nacua and Alaric Jackon for Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, despite any off-field issues the two players have had this past offseason. Adam Schefter believes Nacua could avoid a suspension entirely. . @AdamSchefter on a potential Puka Nacua suspension: "I think there's a real possibility that Puka Nacua doesn't face any discipline this season.. He's gonna be out there against the San Francisco 49ers.” ( @PatMcAfeeShow ) pic.twitter.com/xh1BYpiYXv — SleeperNFL (@SleeperNFL) September 7, 2026 It’s big news for the Rams who will need all the help they can get against a generally tough 49ers team. Nacua and Jackson should help the Rams chances, and hopefully for the Rams they’ll be around for most if not all the 2026 season. Keep an eye on which other players end up suiting up such as Aaron Donald and George Kittle. Thursday’s game should be star-filled either way, but fans will have to wait to see if all the expected players can suit up or not. Rams expect Puka Nacua, Alaric Jackson to play vs. 49ers (espn) “The Los Angeles Rams do not expect wide receiver Puka Nacua and left tackle Alaric Jackson to be suspended for Thursday’s season opener against the San Francisco 49ers despite ongoing legal situations, head coach Sean McVay said Sunday. “Yeah, absolutely,” McVay said when asked if he expected the pair to be able to face the Niners in Australia. “That’s what I’ve heard. I haven’t heard anything different.” On Aug. 30, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported neither player would be placed on the commissioner exempt list that day, but both cases remained under the NFL’s review.“ Inside the Rams’ Unique Plan to Make a 15,000-Mile Trip to Australia Feel As Normal As Possible (si.com) “You plan to bring the house,” Burger said in the lead-up to their Week 1 contest at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. “You’re bringing everything. From the usual backup stuff we bring—helmets, pads, cleats—to different level spikes, to different types of jackets and cold-weather gear. We bring everything we have.” While nonstop flights from both Los Angeles and San Francisco across the Pacific Ocean to Melbourne take roughly 16 hours, the two teams are taking two vastly different approaches to the trip. The 49ers departed for Australia last Wednesday, Sept. 2, giving themselves more than a week to acclimate to the 14-hour time difference. The Rams, meanwhile, remain in Inglewood. They’ll arrive in Melbourne the day before the game and leave immediately afterward.“ Rams players will have ‘full lay-out’ beds on flight to Australia (ramswire0 ““I look at it as Friday evening,” McVay said, comparing it to the schedule of a traditional Sunday game. “It’s Tuesday night for you guys, but it would be the equivalent of Friday evening. Sleep through the night and then we’ll get there and we have kind of a rhythm.” Players shouldn’t have too much trouble sleeping through the night on the plane because they’ll each have their own lay-flat bed.“ Rams coach Sean McVay sees late travel to Australia for opener as best course of action (nfl.com) “McVay said the plan was influenced in part by how the Rams approached their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last October, when they arrived on Saturday morning for a Sunday afternoon start. They rolled to a comfortable 35-7 win at Wembley Stadium. However, they had already spent a week on the east coast after playing at the Baltimore Ravens, reducing both the flight’s length and impact of adjusting to a new time zone. This time, the Rams will be spending approximately 15 hours in the air, albeit with lie-flat seats available to all players and coaches. “I feel like we’re just keeping it as normal as we possibly can,” quarterback Matthew Stafford said. “Sunday (is) like a Wednesday for us in our world. Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, hop on the plane and go. We obviously have experience with doing it (in a) different direction, all that kind of stuff, I understand last year in London, but it felt like it worked out for us.” LA Rams’ Former Super Bowl Starter Rejoins Broncos After Surprise Release (heavy.com) “The Broncos signed Rapp on Aug. 20 , adding an experienced option to a safety room headlined by Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga. At the time, Denver noted that Rapp had made 72 career starts with 12 interceptions, 31 passes defensed and 488 tackles. Six days later, however, Denver released Rapp in a pair of corresponding roster moves. The quick exit initially appeared surprising, but Broncos head coach Sean Payton subsequently explained that Rapp needed time away for a personal matter. Payton also left the door wide open for his return. “He needs a little time at home,” Payton said, adding there was a “better than good chance” Rapp would eventually be back with Denver, according to The Denver Gazette .“ Monday Morning Rambling: Why 2026 Is the Rams’ Last Best Chance With Matthew Stafford (ramswire) “As the Rams head into the 2026 season, there’s no doubt they are managing high expectations. After falling in the NFC Championship last season, the Rams made it a point to do what they can to give quarterback Matthew Stafford the pieces he needed to win another Super Bowl . Sam Darnold threw for 346 yards against the Rams’ secondary, so they went out and traded for Trent McDuffie. The Rams had a good pass rush, but lacked a proven closer, so they went out and landed Myles Garrett in a trade. It’s the first time in NFL history that the reigning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year are on the same roster. That doesn’t even mention that Aaron Donald came out of retirement after being away for two years. Yes, the same Aaron Donald who was a three-time Defensive Player of the Year and the best defensive player of his generation. “ 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Does Not Mince Words About Rams’ Aaron Donald (sports.yahoo) “Shanahan cited the joy of Donald’s retirement in 2024, noting the “opposite” for the DT’s return. “[I] remember when he retired, I didn’t see the alerts and stuff, but I heard people yelling down the hallway cheering. I was like, ‘What the hell’s going on?’ And then, I got it on my phone, and it was probably the most we’ve celebrated in the offseason ever. And then it was the exact opposite this year,” Shanahan said. “I wasn’t crushed on the Sunday that he decided because I decided a month ago it was happening. So I prepared for that the right way, and it is what it is. He’s a hell of a player, and we’ll have our work cut out for him.” Rams leaning into villain role ahead of 2026 season: ‘These other teams probably hate us’ (nfl.com) “The Dodgers’ Los Angeles gridiron counterparts are leaning into the same role entering the 2026 NFL season. “You know all these other teams probably hate us,” Rams safety Quentin Lake said, via the Los Angeles Times . “They think we’re like the new Dodgers or something like that.” There’s good reason for others to dislike the Rams in 2026. They feature the reigning NFL MVP in quarterback Matthew Stafford , completed a blockbuster trade for Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett , and topped their sundae by welcoming back All-Pro defensive tackle Aaron Donald from retirement. It’s not quite a Dream Team, but it’s certainly a squad that loaded up on talent like the Dodgers, and one that is focused solely on the ultimate prize: a Lombardi Trophy. With a clear intent to target football’s mountaintop, anything less will be considered a failure.“ Falcons name Tua Tagovailoa starting QB for Week 1 vs. Steelers; Michael Penix Jr. to be inactive “Stefanski told reporters on Monday that Penix, who has been working his way back from last year’s season-ending knee injury , will be inactive against Pittsburgh. Cooper Rush will serve as Tagovailoa’s backup. “Mike is getting better and better and better, and I’m very proud of him for how far he’s come,” Stefanski said, “but this will continue to be something that we…

title: The Rams can help close Kyle Shanahan’s window
summary: Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan were hired as head coaches in the same year for the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. McVay boasts a Super Bowl win while Shanahan has finished on the cusp twice. Shanahan is not running out of time with the 49ers. He’d be one of the most sought […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers' head coach Kyle Shanahan speaks to the media at AAMI Park in Melbourne on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / -- IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE -- | AFP via Getty Images Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan were hired as head coaches in the same year for the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. McVay boasts a Super Bowl win while Shanahan has finished on the cusp twice. Shanahan is not running out of time with the 49ers. He’d be one of the most sought after candidates on the open market if he separated from the team. However, the sand is dwindling for this version of the 49ers. Thursday night’s game between these two teams is not a must-win for either NFC West foe. Shanahan must win over the next four months or his window in San Francisco could be shut so tight it may not be worth trying to re-open. The 49ers’ offense is Shanahan’s hallmark. Year 10 brings a quarterback that is still young surrounded by a lot of pieces that no longer are. Trent Williams is soon to be 38—around the same age as Matthew Stafford at a much more physically demanding position. Kyle Juszczyk is 35. Mike Evans is 33. George Kittle is 32 and is coming off another serious injury. Christian McCaffrey is 30 but is much older in running back years. Ricky Pearsall has been swallowed whole by the injury bug. The problem isn’t so much that the 49ers are old—that isn’t necessarily true. They are simply old in all the wrong places. San Francisco has tried to turnover its defense and raise the next generation of stars. It simply hasn’t worked. I wrote last season that the 49ers’ draft class was off to a poor start to their careers . That is still true after the calendar has turned. Mykel Williams will start the season on the PUP list and miss at least the first four games. There is talk about San Francisco’s best rookie piece from a year ago, Alfred Collins, no longer being a scheme fit for Raheem Morris’ defense. Brock Purdy helped a roster littered with talent reach new heights. He brought more to the table than Jimmy Garoppolo ever did. But now that the 49ers are paying Purdy top dollar, can he elevate a middling roster to competitive in the same way he made a great roster even more formidable? Purdy may never be a superstar quarterback. We know a sizeable portion of his production should be credited to Shanahan. There are serious questions about the signal caller’s game. Can he find a deep ball and reduce turnovers under pressure? The state of the 49ers feels very fragile. Shanahan has years left on his contract and teams would probably trade at least a first round pick in order to bring him on board. But his runway in San Francisco seems to be coming to an end, barring a surprise turnaround. If the Rams take care of business on Thursday night, they can keep Shanahan and the 49ers on their downward trajectory.

title: Raiders News: ESPN gives Las Vegas slim playoff odds in Klint Kubiak’s 1st season
summary: In the span of about two months during the offseason, new Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak went from winning the Super Bowl to making the first pick of the NFL Draft. In other words, Kubiak went from being a part of the best team in the NFL to taking over the worst team […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders walks on the field during warmups before a preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the span of about two months during the offseason, new Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak went from winning the Super Bowl to making the first pick of the NFL Draft. In other words, Kubiak went from being a part of the best team in the NFL to taking over the worst team in the league. The Raiders are also entering year one of a rebuild after reconstructing the roster during the spring. As a result, not much is expected of the former Seattle Seahawks offensive coordinator during his first season as the head man in Las Vegas. A good example of that comes from a recent season preview and predictions column from ESPN , where the Silver and Black were given just a five percent chance to make the playoffs. The article also gives Kubiak’s crew a 1.3 percent chance to win the competitive AFC West, a projected 5.7 wins with a “best-case scenario” of an 8-9 record and matching last year’s 3-14 mark as the worst case. That begs the question: With such low expectations heading into the campaign, how do the Raiders measure success in 2026? “[Fernando] Mendoza shows the signs of a franchise quarterback,” ESPN’s Ryan McFadden said in response to the question above. “The Raiders are a young team that requires patience, so it’s not worth placing postseason expectations on them. But whenever Las Vegas decides to start Mendoza, it will be important for him to show flashes that he can guide this offense for the foreseeable future. Given the team’s recent history at quarterback, having stability at the position is essential for turning the organization around. Building on McFadden’s take, the youth movement in Las Vegas likely won’t yield immediate results in terms of the win/loss column. Instead, the organization’s biggest priority should be developing the young roster so that the team can grow together and become a legitimate and consistent contender in 2027 and beyond. Obviously, Mendoza is the biggest factor in that. But that could mean taking some bumps and bruises during the upcoming season, which starts on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. In Other Raiders’ Links: More practice squad moves: The Raiders announced that they added defensive/nose tackle Tim Keenan III and tight end/fullback Patrick Gurd to the practice squad , releasing defensive/nose tackle Gary Smith III and safety Devin Lafayette in corresponding moves. Raiders land edge rusher in early mock draft: “The Las Vegas Raiders were this close to trading Maxx Crosby this offseason. With or without Crosby next year, the lineup could still use another pass-rush threat to improve the entire defensive front. Texas’ Colin Simmons is super-productive and difficult to handle working off the edge,” via Bleacher Report’s Scouting Department . title: Raiders Week 1: The must-account-for Dolphins in the home opener
summary: It might’ve just been me, but it sure felt like it took a while for us to get into Week 1 mode, but alas, here we are and the Las Vegas Raiders are set to embark on the regular season with Klint Kubiak as their head coach. The Silver & Black kick off its 2026 […]
full_text: Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane (28) runs with the football as Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Decamerion Richardson (25) and Raiders cornerback Darnay Holmes (30) defend in the second half at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 17, 2024, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (David Santiago/Miami Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) | Getty Images It might’ve just been me, but it sure felt like it took a while for us to get into Week 1 mode, but alas, here we are and the Las Vegas Raiders are set to embark on the regular season with Klint Kubiak as their head coach. The Silver & Black kick off its 2026 campaign by hosting the Miami Dolphins inside Allegiant Stadium this Sunday afternoon. And the battle between the AFC West and AFC East squads features a clash between two rookie head coaches — Kubiak and Jeff Hafley — in charge of rebuilding squads. Much like the Raiders did two offseason ago with cleaning house and hiring John Spytek in January of 2025 and two days later inking one-and-done head coach Pete Carroll (which ushered the Kubiak era the following offseason), the Dolphins pressure washed its front office and coaching staff with the additions of GM Jon-Eric Sullivan and Hafley (a pair of Green Bay Packers with the former serving as vice president of player personnel and the latter as defensive coordinator). But as the case was in Las Vegas, Miami’s roster cupboard is far from barren. The team has intriguing elite talent — even after the Dolphins did the customary roster purge that often accompanies a new primary personnel man and head coach. And Kubiak and Co. must account for them as running back De’Von Achane has the explosiveness, speed, and versatility to make even the best NFL defenses look foolish while linebacker Jordyn Brooks is a smart and hard-hitting linebacker that can ruin an NFL offense’s best laid plans. De'Von Achane is setting a goal for himself of leading the league in rushing this season 👀 (via @nflnetwork ) pic.twitter.com/N4s1MCBixC — NFL (@NFL) August 2, 2026 Achane Attack The 24-year-old running back produced a career-best 1,350 yards on 238 carries last season for Miami. Standing 5-foot-9 and 195 pounds, the third-round pick (84th overall) from the 2023 NFL Draft exceeded expectations coming out of Texas A&M. Adding four more end zone trips as a receiver, that 12-touchdown performance in 2025 set as new career-high mark. He’s every bit as fast as the 4.32-second 40-yard dash time he clocked a the NFL Combine and the eight rushing touchdowns he had this past season tied the same number he had as a rookie in 2023. By The Numbers De’Von Achane, Running Back, 4th Year 2025: 16 games (all starts), 238 carries, 1,350 yards, 8 touchdowns; 85 targets, 67 receptions, 488 yards, 4 touchdowns Career: 44 games (36 starts), 544 carries, 3,057 yards, 22 touchdowns; 209 targets, 172 receptions, 1,277 yards, 13 touchdowns The matchup between Achane and the Raiders’ defense puts the unsettled interior run defense under the microscope and spotlight in Week 1. Late-camp addition Folorunso Fatukasi (6-foot-4, 318 pounds, 31 years old) impressed Las Vegas to make the 53-man roster and his fellow defensive tackles — Thomas Booker IV, Adam Butler, Jonah Laulu, Tonka Hemingway, and JJ Pegues — will have their hands full (depending on how his active gameday). That group up front must control the line of scrimmage along with the A and B gaps to allow linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker to make plays alongside Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye on the edges. Achane is the type to truly test the Raiders defense as one mistake, one missed assignment can result in the tailback finding the end zone either from the interior or perimeter. And we’ll get to see if Crosby and Paye — players who can rack up tackles for loss defending the run — can get the job done. Defenders charged with covering Achane out of the backfield as a receiver presents equal headaches and if he gets going, it can limit the Raiders defense from pass rush opportunities against Miami quarterback Malik Willis, who has the athleticism to scramble and run around, himself. The Week 1 matchup entails seeing Leonard’s full gamut defense as opposed to the vanilla play calls he ran during preseason. And that should be intriguing to see how it’ll play out. No. 67 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @MiamiDolphins LB Jordyn Brooks! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/s7Bk6NXWWz — NFL (@NFL) July 14, 2026 By The Brooks The success of Kubiak’s offense is often predicated on the run and what a great test for the Raiders by battling against Brooks. The centerpiece of Hafley’s defense, the 28-year-old Texas Tech product packs a mean wallop in his 6-foot and 240-pound frame. With solid size, speed (4.54-second 40-yard dash time in the 2020 NFL Combine), and exceptional football intelligence, Brooks is the epitome of a sideline-to-sideline linebacker that can blow up stretch or outside zones before the blocking develops. He’s also a downhill punisher who can eradicate gap and power runs, too, which earned him first-team NFL All Pro honors in 2025. By The Numbers Jordyn Brooks, Linebacker, 7th Year 2025: 17 games (all starts), 183 total tackles (99 solo), 13 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 3 pass deflections, 1 forced fumble, 1 fumble recovery Career: 97 games (89 starts), 839 total tackles (494 solo), 47 tackles for loss, 13 sacks, 1 interception, 25 pass deflections, 3 forced fumbles, 6 fumble recoveries Kubiak did well to bring in a fullback to provide the hardnosed lead blocker for his running backs — be it Ashton Jeanty or scintillating rookie Mike Washington Jr. — and the eventual meeting between Connor Heyward and Brooks will be one to watch. Brooks ability to diagnose run plays quickly alongside his size and speed allows the linebacker to truly blow up downhill blocking schemes. Brooks has the instincts and movement skills to be a nuisance in the middle of the field as a cover man — although this is the weakest aspect of his game as Pro Football Reference charted him with allowing 66 receptions on 86 targets (76.7 completion percentage allowed) for 665 yards and three touchdowns last season . With Kubiak’s penchant to run multiple tight end sets, testing Brooks’ coverage chop opens with both Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer and running backs coming out of the backfield is a must-do.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: What does Darrell Luter Jr. bring to Las Vegas Raiders’ roster?
summary: Even after the Las Vegas Raiders filled out their initial 53-man roster at the end of training camp, John Spytek and Klint Kubiak weren’t done making one last tweak. The Raiders picked up cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. from the San Francisco 49ers off the waiver wire, who drew the most interest on the wire with […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Darrell Luter Jr. #28 of the San Francisco 49ers gets set during the third quarter of a preseason NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Even after the Las Vegas Raiders filled out their initial 53-man roster at the end of training camp, John Spytek and Klint Kubiak weren’t done making one last tweak. The Raiders picked up cornerback Darrell Luter Jr. from the San Francisco 49ers off the waiver wire , who drew the most interest on the wire with four other teams putting a claim in on him, according to ESPN’s Field Yates . Luter is expected to serve as a backup corner and special teamer on the Raiders’ roster. He was a key specialist in San Francisco, recording over 500 career snaps on special teams over the last three years by contributing to every unit except for the field goal/PAT kicking team, according to Pro Football Focus . Last season, the 2023 fifth-round pick recorded six total tackles and earned a 68.9 special teams grade. Defensively, the four-year pro doesn’t have much regular-season experience with 342 career snaps, 275 of them and all three of his career starts coming last season. He was targeted 18 times in 2025 and yielded 12 catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns with one PBU, per PFF . However, Luter drew interest with a strong performance in the preseason this summer, allowing just two catches for 18 yards and no touchdowns (one PBU) on seven targets, per PFF . With that in mind, let’s dive into the last three games and see what the veteran corner can bring to Las Vegas’ defense. Every target against Darrell Luter Jr. this preseason #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/KlhufHDPHC — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 I’ll dive deeper into a few of the reps, but above is a look at every time Luter was targeted during the 2026 preseason. If you’re keeping score at home, there are eight plays up there. The discrepency in the targets appears to be that PFF has the linebacker drawing the target on Fernando Mendoza’s interception above. The biggest area of improvement that stands out is his change of direction, as he often has a hitch in his transitions and struggles to drive on routes. However, the Southern Alabama product has decent ball skills and can be effective in press coverage, which lines up with Lance Zierlein of NFL.com’s scouting report when Luter was a draft prospect. “Long-limbed (32 3/8-inch arms) press-cover cornerback with the ball skills and physicality to challenge receivers outside the numbers,” Zierlein wrote. “Luter can be a little leggy in his transitions and burst to the football, but his length helps make up for that and creates pass breakups. Louisiana-Monroe attacked him with back-shoulder throws all game, which is something to keep an eye on in the pros. He’s going to be more effective in press-and-shadow coverage than he is playing Cover 3 or off-man. His ball production dipped in 2022, but his length and playing style fit the NFL game.” For the record, the former Jaguar had four interceptions and 10 passes defended in 2021 before racking up one pick and seven PDs in 2022. This rep is a good high-level view of Darrell Luter's skill set Hitch on the transition prevents him from being able to drive on the route and make a play as the ball arrives, but he has enough speed to recover and still break up the pass after the WR bobbles it #Raiders pic.twitter.com/GF2EXHvCi4 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 This rep provides a 1,000-foot view of Luter’s strengths and weaknesses. He’s playing off-coverage and is isolated against the single receiver in the three-by-one formation. The wideout runs an out route, and the corner does a good job of staying on top of it. Then, the latter has a hitch when trying to drive on the route, which prevents him from being in position to make a play on the ball as it arrives. However, he does have enough speed to get back in the picture after the receiver bobbles the catch, allowing Luter to play the wideout’s hands and prevent the completion. So, the change-of-direction skills are subpar to give his man an opportunity to make the catch. But Luter’s straight-line speed and long arms allow him to take advantage of a mistake and end up winning the rep. For those curious, he ran a 4.46-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine three years ago. Darrell Luter is at his best in press coverage Good job getting hands on the WR in the 5-yard window and squeezing him to the sideline against the go route #Raiders pic.twitter.com/RSAPv6fY0a — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 As Zierlein noted, Luter is at his best in press coverage, and this is a good example of what he can do when he gets his hands on receivers. Luter starts the play as if he’s in soft-shoe coverage (press without a jam) but times up his jam/punch to make contact about four yards into the five-yard window. That’s a good change-up because it can catch wide receivers off-guard, where they’re thinking that they won’t have to deal with any physicality since there was no jam at the line of scrimmage. Additionally, that disrupts the timing of the route, and the corner does a good job of squeezing the wideout toward the sideline to give the quarterback less room to complete the pass to the go route. From there, Luter is in-phase throughout the route, staying in the receiver’s hip pocket. So, he can turn his head to locate the ball in the air and make a play on it instead of nearly overrunning the under throw. But, at the end of the day, Luter has tight coverage and does his job by breaking up the pass. Just with his backside instead of his hands! Darrell Luter with a great play against new teammate Malik Benson His 32⅜-inch arms show up to get the PBU against the back-shoulder throw from Mendoza #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/AFZfJBL1ue — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 You might remember watching this rep during the preseason, as Luter makes a nice play against his new teammates Malik Benson and Fernando Mendoza. This rep is pretty similar to the last one, only he stays in soft-shoe coverage against the go/fade route this time. Also, he does a better job of turning his head to find the ball in the air to be in perfect position to defend against the back-shoulder throw. Those long arms come in handy at the catch point, as he’s able to come up with a PBU to finish the rep and put the Raiders in a third-and-long situation. Nice read by Darrell Luter to sniff out the screen, crash downhill and make the open-field tackle #Raiders pic.twitter.com/tmPgPRRLg3 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 The fourth-year pro is also a pretty good tackler, which is another area where his long arms come into play, and the clip above is a great example. It looks like the 49ers are running Cover 3 with pattern matching principles since both corners have their eyes on the wide receivers they’re lined up across from, while the underneath defenders fall into their zones post-snap. Meanwhile, the Raiders have a good play design where the receiver lined up across from Luter runs a crossing route to get the corner out of position to defend the screen. However, Luter recognizes the play design and crashes downhill. He does benefit from left tackle Kolton Miller eyeing the linebackers and being late to see the corner outside. But Luter’s speed and long arms allow him to take advantage by using a good angle and laying out to trip up Michael Mayer for a one-yard gain. That’s a heads-up play, in addition to the speed and tackling skills. Nice run support from Darrell Luter to trigger downhill and clean this up for a 1-yard gain #Raiders pic.twitter.com/pqWIQbf8dW — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 3, 2026 We’ll wrap up here with a nice play in run support, which is a big part of Luter’s game. For example, he posted an 82.0 PFF run defense grade during the regular…

summary: The Raiders weekly series will recap the biggest stories from the week. Additionally, we will focus on what happens outside the lines leading up to Sunday. Meanwhile, Week 0 is upon us. What is Week 0? It is the week separating the preseason from the regular season. Kirk Cousins is QB1 Las Vegas Raiders head […]
full_text: The Raiders weekly series will recap the biggest stories from the week. Additionally, we will focus on what happens outside the lines leading up to Sunday. Meanwhile, Week 0 is upon us. What is Week 0? It is the week separating the preseason from the regular season. Kirk Cousins is QB1 Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak named Cousins the Week 1 starter against the Miami Dolphins. Cousins has demonstrated the most amount of NFL polish despite a strong push from number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. He has been the more consistent quarterback over the summer and has not committed any turnovers. Raiders get $75m for stadium upgrades One of the things missing from Allegiant Stadium that was beloved in the Oakland Alameda Coliseum was the catwalk from the Coliseum BART station. The catwalk served a great many purposes in both accessibility, live music and the unlicensed marketplace. Las Vegas Stadium Authority Approves Up To $75 Million For Allegiant Stadium Renovation – Pollstar News What this upgrade will do is essentially bridge a better pedestrian connection to the Las Vegas Strip. Provide a better access point for ride sharing services and an exterior venue. Raiders tryout 16 players If you aren’t trying to compete every day, you aren’t trying to get better. The Raiders had 16 players in for a tryout on Thursday; not resting on his laurels, general manager John Spytek made one of the biggest low-risk and high reward moves of the season. He also countered placing Keyron Crawford on the injured reserve list by getting some more help on the edge. Ronnie Bell, Azeez Ojulari and former first-round pick Evan Neal were signed to the practice squad. The corresponding cuts were Albert Okwuegbunam Jr, Jahfari Harvey and Kamar Missouri. Neal, a former national champion at the University of Alabama and the 2022 number seven overall draft pick. Has the size to play tackle but the lateral quickness of a guard at the NFL level. However, Raiders offensive line coach Rick Dennison could be just the coach he needs to fix his mistakes and help him realize his full potential. Ojulari was teammates with Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean at the University of Georgia. Ojulari was a 2021 second-round pick who also found himself starting his career with the New York Giants’ sunken ship. Reuniting with his teammates should be a welcome change of scenery and bring more elite athleticism to a defense that needs it. Bell is a receiver who couldn’t quite catch on with the San Francisco 49ers and New Orleans Saints outside of special teams and a preseason role.

summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to improve at the offensive line position. It was abysmal last season, and the hope is that the new coaching staff can maximize the group’s talent. Offensive line coach Rick Dennsion is already making an imprint. During preseason, the execution was precise and looked completely different than it did […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 10: Owner and managing general partner Mark Davis of the Las Vegas Raiders talks to Richie Incognito #64 before a game against the Chicago Bears at Allegiant Stadium on October 10, 2021 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are looking to improve at the offensive line position. It was abysmal last season, and the hope is that the new coaching staff can maximize the group’s talent. Offensive line coach Rick Dennsion is already making an imprint. During preseason, the execution was precise and looked completely different than it did the year before. Cousins was under pressure one snap, and Mike Washington Jr. averaged 7.3 yards per carry. It caught the eye of former Raider Richie Incognito. Incognito was with the Raiders in 2019 before injuries ended his career. During an interview with Raider Nation Radio, he gave his thoughts on Dennsion and the new outlook for the line. “These guys work hard and their frustration last year was they are putting in all this time, they’re not getting the results on the field, but they really felt like they weren’t getting coached up in the meeting rooms, so there was a lot of frustration.” “I think that frustration is completely gone with a guy like Rick Dennison. He is highly detailed. He’s all about fundamentals. He’s going to get these guys all on the same page and you could see it in the preseason. You could see the double teams happening, the bodies hitting the floor. The backs hitting the holes, so it’s an exciting time.” Hopefully all of this hits the field next Sunday against the Miami Dolphins. It will be the first test for the new offensive line to make its mark on the season. What do you hope, want to, or expect to see from this team in year one of yet another […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Miles Battle #35 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates a fumble recovery against the Atlanta Falcons during the second half at Hard Rock Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. What do you hope, want to, or expect to see from this team in year one of yet another rebuild? Below are some of your thoughts and answers- Urthling expects to see the usual growing pains of a rebuild, but also hopes to see growth from the team as the season progresses. What questions do you have or do you want answered by the 2026-2027 version of your Miami Dolphins? Is Bobby Slowik ‘the guy’ for our OC position? Is he the Bobby Slowik who developed CJ Stroud into Rookie of the Year… or is he the bum who got fired the next season? What did he learn about run-game design from Mike McDaniel? What do you hope, want to or expect to see from this team in year one of yet another rebuild? I hope to see: Disciplined, team-first play. Physicality, grit and competitiveness. Incremental improvement and player development throughout the season. The gelling of this team’s ‘identity’, hopefully taking on a mindset similar to their head coach. What do I expect to see: Lots of mistakes from the young roster. Inconsistency as the rookies ‘figure it out’… high highs and low lows. Constant churning of the bottom 5 roster spots and the practice squad. Jeff Hafley proves he belongs as an NFL coach, despite a bumpy ride. What’s the dead cap hit for next season? We already know this season is the 7th circle of financial hell. WoodStrock1 seems concerned that decent overall play from Willis could prevent the team from drafting a possible future great quarterback. Is good, but not great play from Malik Willis going to prevent them from drafting a potentially franchise changing QB in next years draft, assuming they are in a position to do so? The Earl asked possibly the most important question of this coming season. Is Malik Willis the answer? Yarganaught has some solid/great questions for this upcoming season. Will this team step up for an unproven coach… will they improve each week? Will there be a weak link position/group (e.g. Secondary)? USMCFinPhreak is another who knows that the top question this coming season is if Willis is finally the answer at starting QB or not. What questions do you have or do you want answered by the 2026-2027 version of your Miami Dolphins? At what point in the season will it be decided whether Willis is or is not the QB of the future. Are they willing to roll the dice with Willis long enough to gain a few wins and possibly lose a top 3 draft pick? What do you hope, want to or expect to see from this team in year one of yet another rebuild? I hope to see Willis succeed and become our franchise quarterback, and negate my 2nd question above. I want to see a competitive, disciplined, focused, and spirited team, regardless of the game’s outcome. I expect to see the entire team make strides to improve every week. Phoenix6 is concerned with the defense finally playing tough-nosed football. What questions do you have or do you want answered by the 2026-2027 version of your Miami Dolphins? Is the defense going to play with hard tackling or are they going to continue to play flag football? What do you hope, want to or expect to see from this team in year one of yet another rebuild? Cohesiveness, discipline, to overcome. Dolphster hopes to see the team put on the field this season as a unit that will be the foundation for the team’s future. What I hope to see is a core group of young players step up and become a foundation to begin building a championship team around in the next few years. RobNJ65 just wants to see this new regime follow what works, not panic, and not try to buy our way into winning. Will this new regime stick to the game plan and not drive us back into salary cap hell?? cyberflea just wants to know when the Phins are going to win the big one. When are the Dolphins going to win the Super Bowl and will it be in my lifetime?????? Can you answer that one?????? 🤪🤓🤪🤓🤪 That’s our selection of questions that some of you want answered this coming season. title: Patrick Paul, Aaron Brewer bullish on Kadyn Proctor’s Dolphins debut
summary: The Miami Dolphins will be playing football on Sunday in Las Vegas against the Raiders. Not preseason football, not exhibition football, but real-life, regular season NFL football. As such, their starting left guard — rookie Kadyn Proctor — will be making his National Football League debut. When the Dolphins traded out of selecting safety Caleb […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins guard Kadyn Proctor (74) warms up during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins will be playing football on Sunday in Las Vegas against the Raiders. Not preseason football, not exhibition football, but real-life, regular season NFL football. As such, their starting left guard — rookie Kadyn Proctor — will be making his National Football League debut. When the Dolphins traded out of selecting safety Caleb Downs and bypassed adding EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft to instead select Proctor out of Alabama, the internet exploded with consternation over the selection. But, Miami’s new general manager, Jon-Eric Sullivan, targeted the big lineman for a reason — he wants Miami to be tougher and more physical at the point of attack on offense, and not just reliant on smoke and mirrors like past regimes succeeded with. He also wanted his big investment — quarterback Malik Willis — to be protected at all costs. Throughout the summer, many Dolphins fans continued to bemoan the Proctor selection — but those in the buildings in Miami Gardens are instead singing his praises. Dolphins veteran center Aaron Brewer met with the South Florida media following Monday’s practice and was asked about Proctor’s potential and what makes the young player special. “ His size. His speed. That’s an athletic big dude ,” said Brewer. Miami’s third-year left tackle, Patrick Paul, also had good things to say about Miami’s starting left guard. “ He’s been ready. He’s ready. He’s a different kind of rookie, ” spoke Paul of Proctor. The words have been spoken. Now it’s time for Proctor to quiet the lips of his doubters with action. He’ll get that opportunity on Sunday when the Dolphins take on the Raiders in the late afternoon window of the inaugural NFL Sunday of the 2026 season.

title: Dolphins announce 2026 captains
summary: The Miami Dolphins on Monday announced their 2026 captains, naming two defensive players and four offensive players as team leaders. Head coach Jeff Hafley had indicated last week that the captains would be named via a team vote, telling reporters, “I think it’s important for everybody who is involved to have a vote in that, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) smiles as he speaks to the media during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins on Monday announced their 2026 captains, naming two defensive players and four offensive players as team leaders. Head coach Jeff Hafley had indicated last week that the captains would be named via a team vote, telling reporters, “I think it’s important for everybody who is involved to have a vote in that, certainly starting with the players. I think it’s important that they have a vote in who they believe the captains should be, and I’m excited to see that…But we’ll vote on it and take a look. I think there’s a couple candidates that really deserve it, so I’m excited to see who our players think they are.” He then added on Thursday, “The vote has been taken. I don’t have an ideal number. I’ll look at the votes and if they’re spread out and kind of even, we’ll go there. Some years I’ve had to do this there’s been three, some years there’s been six. It’s just, where’s your team at, who are your leaders, who do the guys on the team think the captain should be, how many votes did each guy get, and you make your judgment. But we have not tallied them up yet. We just voted in the meetings right now. So I will announce that on – I talk to you guys Monday, so you’ll know on Monday. The players will know Monday too. So that’s not going to be something that gets out.” Dolphins 2026 Captains Now that it is Monday, the results are out. Miami’s 2026 captains are: Running back De’Von Achane Center Aaron Brewer Linebacker Jordyn Brooks Left tackle Patrick Paul Defensive tackle Zach Sieler Quarterback Malik Willis Young leaders stepping up Just as the Dolphins are looking to reset the franchise, trusting younger players to develop and perform this season, the captains feature several younger players stepping into leadership roles for the first time. Achane, Willis, and Paul were named captains for the first time. Willis, in his first year as a starting quarterback, joined the Dolphins this year and has immediately assumed a leadership role. Achane and Paul are only 24 years old as they become captains for the first time. Willis is 27. The Dolphins coaching staff and front office named Achane, Brewer, and Brooks the building blocks of the team as they took over and started a rebuild of the franchise. All three were signed to contract extensions this summer and they now add leadership roles for the players as well. Brewer and Brooks are both 28 years old. Brewer and Paul are the anchors on the offensive line. Brewer was a Second-Team All-Pro selection last season and is looking to continue to build, aiming to be First-Team this year . Paul, entering his third year, has established himself as a strong left tackle and has been taking on more leadership responsibilities this offseason and during training camp. Sieler is the longest-tenured player on Miami’s roster, having joined the team as a waiver claim from the Baltimore Ravens during the 2019 season. He has been selected as a captain the past two seasons and continues that leadership role this year. He is 31 years old.

For the Miami Dolphins, Week 1 kicks off on Sunday afternoon when they visit the Las Vegas Raiders. The season is almost here, but are the Dolphins ready for the 18-week, 17-game grind? According to fans, several major concerns loom as the season approaches. In our recent SB Nation Reacts survey, we asked which position group concerns fans most for the Dolphins after last week’s roster cuts. The defensive secondary, which includes cornerbacks and safeties, dominated the poll with 60 percent of the vote. Offensive line, a constant area of concern for Miami, ranked second, though it was a distant runner-up with just 15 percent of responses. Edge, wide receiver, and special teams rounded out the vote with 13-, 8-, and 5-percent of the vote, respectively. We also recently asked which second-year player you think will make take the biggest jump forward this season, and again, the results were overwhelming. After a rookie season where he struggled at left guard, Jonah Savaiinaea has moved to right guard this year and the fans think he will blossom there. With 65 percent of the vote, Savaiinaea is clearly the player the Dolphins’ fans think will take the biggest jump. Safety Dante Trader, Jr., was second in the poll, receiving 15 percent of the vote, followed by defensive tackles Kenneth Grant at nine percent and Zeek Biggers at seven percent. Running back Ollie Gordon II rounds out the survey with four percent of the vote. The Dolphins will need a lot to go right this year, with several second-year players making a leap forward and position groups like the secondary proving themselves, if they are going to have success in 2026. Miami remains +75,000 to win the Super Bowl , according to the FanDuel Sportsbook oddmakers, the second longest odds in the league. Can the Dolphins shock the world? Do you agree with the poll results? Let us know in the comments.

title: The Miami Dolphins are not tanking!
summary: Tanking.  It’s a term thrown around by sports fans whenever their favorite team is expecting to be… less than good.  According to Wikipedia, “tanking in sports refers to the practice of intentionally fielding non-competitive teams to take advantage of league rules that benefit losing teams.”  There have been a few teams across the sports world […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley gestures as he speaks to the media during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tanking. It’s a term thrown around by sports fans whenever their favorite team is expecting to be… less than good. According to Wikipedia, “ tanking in sports refers to the practice of intentionally fielding non-competitive teams to take advantage of league rules that benefit losing teams .” There have been a few teams across the sports world accused of tanking in the past few years, including our very own Miami Dolphins. In 2019, the Dolphins were accused of tanking for a certain Alabama quarterback prospect that almost everyone wanted. Yes folks, Tua Tagovailoa was the apple of the eye for most fans. I recall seeing tweets whining, crying, and lamenting the signing of Ryan Fitzpatrick as he would be JUST good enough to prevent the Dolphins from losing enough to draft their beloved Tua. Maybe that was the case then, but I’m here to tell you that the 2026 Miami Dolphins are absolutely, positively, without-a-doubt, 100% NOT TANKING! I have several good reasons that you should listen to that will show you exactly why they are not tanking. Now… I’m not saying this team will be GOOD. I do in fact believe this team will not have a good record when the season is over. But they are not intentionally losing games for some benefit. Let’s look at the reasons why they are not losing on purpose and I guarantee you that by the time you finish reading this article, you’ll see things my way. Or you should. REASON 1: HOW TO TANK The most basic premise to begin a tank is to offload talent that will prevent you from losing. Generally, that means getting rid of good players by trading them for draft picks or cutting them outright. If the 2026 Dolphins were tanking, they would have offloaded a bunch of talent, right? Let’s look at who they moved on from this season. First and foremost is Tyreek Hill. I’m putting him first because he was the most talented player on the Dolphins roster from the last decade, maybe two, that was cut this offseason. Hill also missed most of the 2025 season with a devastating leg injury and still has not signed with anyone. It is very possible that he never plays again. The next player is the aforementioned Tagovailoa. As much as we all wanted to #BlameTannehill, no player that I can recall has been as divisive as Tua. If I wanted to create a post that gets tons of clicks and comments, I’d simply write something about Tua. Fans would come out the woodworks to offer their two cents. Regardless of your opinion of him, there is one thing I would say that EVERYONE would agree on: Tua was not taking the 2026 Dolphins to the Super Bowl. Heck… we’re not even sure he’ll start in Atlanta. Who else? Chubb? Fitzpatrick? Waddle? Chubb is a good edge rusher that was overpaid as an elite one. Fitzpatrick is an older player at a lower value position. Jaylen Waddle is the ONLY player the Dolphins moved on from this offseason that would have made a significant impact on the game. Fans were divided on him as well, with some thinking he was good enough to be a #1 WR and others thinking he was overpaid. But everyone must look at the trade haul for Waddle and compare it to what Philly got for AJ Brown. Jon-Eric Sullivan traded Waddle and pick 111 for picks 30, 94, and 130. Brown is an older player, but far more established and decorated than Waddle. Philly got a 2027 5th rounder and a 2028 first rounder. That’s a win for the Dolphins, especially when the 94th pick was used on a wide receiver. Regardless of what you think about these players, we can all agree that keeping them wouldn’t make the team competitive in 2026. Better maybe, but not competitive in the way we want them to be. And finding replacements was never going to be easy. They could have added some better pieces in free agency if they had had the cap space. But they were not going to add players that would put them over the top. Miami has won free agency before to no avail… remember ? Franchise altering players rarely hit free agency. All the personnel shuffling maybe alters win projections by a few games. But that leads to reason 2. REASON 2: TALENT RETENTION AND ACQUISITION If a team wants to tank, then they not only have to dump talent, but they cannot retain or replace it. Key word: RETAIN. At least not adequately. If you haven’t by now, you need to go subscribe to my Substack page Aqua And Orange Review . Yes, I’m calling BOTH games! In a recent article, I compared the talent of the 2019 Dolphins – the one accused of tanking – and the current roster. I’ll let you read it (click the link) for yourself, but the 2026 Dolphins are doing a horrible job of talent management if they are trying to lose. The 2019 Dolphins dumped players and replaced them with nothing. The best player from previous rosters that they kept was DeVante Parker. The 2026 Dolphins extended Achane, Brooks, and Brewer instead of shipping them off for picks. Achane would have gotten the biggest haul of the group in a trade, but he’s also the youngest. But, but, but… he won’t be good when the Dolphins are ready to compete. You sure about that? Clearly the people in charge don’t feel that way. Brooks and Brewer are older vets that would have gotten something in a trade, but the Dolphins kept them anyway. That would be a self-defeating move if they wanted to lose on purpose. Achane, Brooks, Brewer, and their free agent quarterback will help them win games. REASON 3: QUARTERBACK Football is a fascinating sport. It’s a chess match between 11 offensive players and 11 defensive players that require all 11 of either side to be on the same page. Yet despite being possibly the most team-oriented sport, no position influences the overall outcome in any sport than the quarterback. If a football team is trying to lose or put themselves in a position to be bad enough to lose, then the easiest way to have a bad quarterback. The 2019 Dolphins traded for Josh Rosen and signed Ryan Fitzpatrick. Rosen was a flop from day one and Fitz was a bridge quarterback at best. The 2026 Dolphins didn’t have much cap room to spend, but they went out and spent what they could to sign Malik Willis to be the franchise quarterback. Well… that’s the hope. He gets the first shot at it. Maybe he succeeds and maybe he doesn’t. But a GM doesn’t sign a player like that if the goal is to lose. If Willis plays the way we all hope he plays, the Dolphins will not be the worst team in the league and they will win more games than most expect. They certainly wouldn’t give him the contract they did if the goal was to be bad. REASON 4: YOUNG MEANS INEXPERIENCED, NOT NECESSARILY BAD The 2026 Dolphins made 13 draft selections in the 2026 draft. They had all their draft capital up front. The 2019 Dolphins had only 6 picks but acquired several picks for the 2020 draft and beyond. That’s a major difference. If the goal was to lose for a better draft pick, then it would be preferable to have as many draft picks as possible AFTER THE FACT. Particularly first round picks just in case they win enough to be outside the range for 1st overall. Instead, the Dolphins used all their draft capital in 2026 to fill a variety of positions. It’s not just the rookies either. Since the team didn’t have the cap space to get veterans to fill spots, they will be heavily reliant on rookies and second year players. They have 8 current starters that are rookies or second year players. That number could jump to 11 once Chris Bell, Trey Moore, and Kenneth Grant are back in the mix. That’s half of the starting lineup. Of course, this means a learning curve and mistakes along the way. It will be rough starting out. But the goal will be to see…

title: Dolphins rookie Michael Taaffe shares important message
summary: Miami Dolphins rookie safety Michael Taaffe met with the media at the end of last week, giving reporters a chance to ask him some questions as he prepares for his first NFL regular-season game when the Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1. Taaffe was happy to share his thoughts on the youngest […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDNES, FL - JUNE 09: Miami Dolphins safety Michael Taaffe (31) runs drills during the Miami Dolphins OTA on Tuesday, June 9, 2026 at Baptist Health Training Complexr in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins rookie safety Michael Taaffe met with the media at the end of last week, giving reporters a chance to ask him some questions as he prepares for his first NFL regular-season game when the Dolphins face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1. Taaffe was happy to share his thoughts on the youngest roster in the NFL having a chance to grow together as the Dolphins rebuild their roster and how his game fits into the physical mentality the coaching staff is instilling in the team. It was his closing comment, however, that may have been the most powerful statement. And no matter what you’re going through, you’re loved and people care for you so hang in there. “Last thing I want to say, I think everybody knows it’s Suicide Prevention Month, so just a call to action to everybody out there: you are enough, you are loved and no matter what you’re going through, just know that there’s a rainbow on the other side, there’s life on the other side. And no matter what you’re going through, you’re loved and people care for you so hang in there. I know it’s tough in this life and Satan tries to grab us at the wrong times but just know that you are loved and nothing that you’re going through, other people aren’t going through. So stay strong and you are enough.” If you or someone you know is in crisis, within the United States please dial 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. For Veterans, you can get assistance with specific support for what you are going through by pressing 1 after calling the 988 hotline. The call is free, confidential, and is available in English and Spanish. You can also text HOME to 741741 to reach the hotline via text messages. Taaffe’s message in bringing awareness to Suicide Prevention Month is an important one. This week includes September 8 (9/8) which has been designated as a day of action to bring awareness to the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. September 10 is World Suicide Prevention Day. As for the football aspects of Taaffe’s media availability, he said of the rookies and younger players serving in big roles with the team and building together, he explained, “Oh, it’s been great. I mean, we have to shout out the veterans. The veterans have done such a good job of welcoming us, humbling us at times too, but also welcoming us to what it looks like in the NFL, to what it looks like in the league and how to go about business the right way. So definitely shout out to all the veterans. But at the end of the day, these rookies, they’ve become my best friends the last couple months. And so it’s been really cool to break bread with them, share sweat on the field and go through some adversity, go through positives. And so it’s really fun to see those guys on the field and the real life bullets. It’s gonna be fun to see how we take this thing the next couple years.” Taaffe, at 6-foot, 190-pounds, is not the most imposing safety on a team that is stressing the need to be physical. How does he overcome his size to embody what the coaching staff wants? “Do my job really, really well,” he replied. “That’s what I always remind myself every single day is if I can do my job really, really well, then all those other things will take care of itself. If you just go run down really, really fast and know what you’re looking at the right time, know where your feet are at the right time, then you’ll be able to play this game forever long you want at a really high level. I think Jessie Bates, I think he’s one of the top dawgs and he’s one of the safeties that I look up to the most and he’s always preached that to me because he’s kind of a little bit similar frame when he came in as a rookie. So I really, really like him.” For the Dolphins, with Week 1 starting and the entire 2026 season looming, the football aspects of Taaffe’s media availability are important and entertaining. But his comments highlighting Suicide Prevention Month transcend everything else. Please reach out if you are struggling.

title: Harrison Smith Returns — And the Cap Gets Complicated
summary: Harrison Smith is back — and Tyler Forness is not doing the fanboy version. On a Labor Day Real Forno Show, Forness and producer Dave Stefano unpack the Hitman’s one-year Vikings return, the cap squeeze it creates, and a CFL-inspired pitch for a real NFL Rivalry Weekend before Week 1 vs. Green Bay. The contract […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on during warmups before the game against the Baltimore Ravens at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harrison Smith is back — and Tyler Forness is not doing the fanboy version. On a Labor Day Real Forno Show , Forness and producer Dave Stefano unpack the Hitman’s one-year Vikings return, the cap squeeze it creates, and a CFL-inspired pitch for a real NFL Rivalry Weekend before Week 1 vs. Green Bay. The contract is the headline. Smith’s deal is structured as roughly $8 million base value with $4 million in per-game roster bonuses and $4 million in playoff incentives that max near $16 million only if Minnesota wins the Super Bowl. Play all 17 and he lands around $12.25 million. Forness supports the player getting paid — “Harrison Smith got his money, and on a human level, good for him” — then flips to the team view. Minnesota had about $8.8 million in cap space before the signing. After bonus, per-game money, and the leftover dead cap from the spring release, operating room looks closer to $2 million. “That’s not enough to operate a season,” Forness said. “You have to have more than that.” The football case is layered. Forness will not pretend Smith is replaceable by a draft pick. “Harrison Smith’s brain cannot be found on the street. It cannot be drafted.” Bringing him back lets Josh Metellus stay in his own role instead of becoming a full Harrison clone. The worry is the other half of the job. Flores’ packaging still needs legs after the snap — the A-gap look that bails to single-high. “If he can’t do that anymore, then you can just absolutely destroy it. Jared Goff, Matthew Stafford, they’ll kill it.” Stefano pushed the conductor argument: “The Vikings are not paying for Smith’s legs, they’re paying for his pre-snap chaos.” Forness’s answer: chaos is worthless if quarterbacks can just throw at the 37-year-old. He also walked the ugly cap chess — Blake Cashman, T.J. Hockenson, Will Fries, Andrew Van Ginkel — where pushing money out only works if you actually want those players long term. They also spent the open on a CFL Labor Day Classic idea: lock one mid-October weekend as Rivalry Weekend, same divisional pairings every year, trophies, merch, promotion that actually sells the fight. “Everything is pro wrestling. It is what you make it.” Then they read fan bold predictions: Kyler Murray leading the team in rushing, Justin Jefferson chasing 2,000 yards and the Triple Crown, Dallas Turner leading the league in strip sacks, Will Reichard drilling 70 in Mexico City, Super Bowl 61 matching the franchise’s 1961 founding year. Key points: Smith return: one year, ~$12.25M if he plays 17, max via Super Bowl incentives Cap: thin operating space after Jefferson, Darrisaw, and Murphy already restructured On-field: brain and communication vs. possible athletic drop Metellus stays Metellus if Smith is the communicator Rivalry Weekend pitch: fixed October week, not Thanksgiving Fan spice: Murray rushing title, Jefferson records, Turner strip sacks Next on the network: Packers preview, Who Will Be King , Two Old Bloggers Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Watch the full Labor Day episode on Vikings 1st & SKOL / Bleav. Forness is not here to tell you the Hitman is automatically a win. He’s here to ask what $12.25 million costs in August flexibility — and whether Week 4 still looks like Week 1. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . What do you think? Is Smith the glue that holds Flores together, or the cap bill that shows up in November?

title: Hitman or Hype? Harrison Smith’s Return Highlights Vikings Roster Overhaul
summary: Harrison Smith is BACK for Year 15, the Vikings roster churned 24 hours after setting the 53, and Aaron Jones vs. Jordan Mason remains unsettled — here’s everything you missed on Two Old Bloggers. The Minnesota Vikings barely let the ink dry on their initial 53-man roster before tearing it apart. Within 24 hours, they […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Harrison Smith #22 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harrison Smith is BACK for Year 15 , the Vikings roster churned 24 hours after setting the 53, and Aaron Jones vs. Jordan Mason remains unsettled — here’s everything you missed on Two Old Bloggers . The Minnesota Vikings barely let the ink dry on their initial 53-man roster before tearing it apart. Within 24 hours, they added offensive linemen Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac, cut Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell (re-signing both to the practice squad), and then delivered the biggest surprise of the weekend: Harrison “Hitman” Smith returning on a one-year deal worth $12.25 million, escalating to $16.25 million with playoff incentives. As Darren Campbell put it: “Bringing back Harrison Smith bolsters that depth.” With Jamal Adams lost for the year, Theo Jackson battling a leg injury, and both Jakobe and Jacob Thomas nicked up, the safety room was paper-thin. Smith, now 37, remains the NFL’s active interceptions leader and is the only player in the secondary besides Josh Metellus who can audible out of coverages late in the play clock. The Vikings also signed 35-year-old edge rusher Kyle Van Noy to the practice squad — a move both hosts endorsed but questioned in its timing. “They got to add a veteran with some track record,” Darren argued, noting that Jadeveon Clowney, Von Miller, and other targets had already signed elsewhere while Minnesota waited. On the running back battle, the unofficial depth chart lists Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason as co-starters, but Darren made the case that Jones will open as 1A: “The receiving abilities and pass blocking — those are two things that Aaron Jones really has Kevin O’Connell and Wes Phillips’ trust.” Mason out-rushed Jones by 210 yards last season but caught just 14 passes. The show also covered J.J. McCarthy’s uncertain future — “his story isn’t written yet,” per Nolan Teasley — the new GM’s refreshingly blunt press conference style, and ESPN’s Top 100 snubbing Andrew Van Ginkel and Brian O’Neill. “If Brian O’Neill was on the Dallas Cowboys, he’d be All-Pro every year,” Darren quipped. Key Points: Harrison Smith returns on a 1-year, $12.25M deal (up to $16.25M with playoffs); Mike Garafolo confirmed he’s playing Week 1 Vikings added OL Trevor Keegan and Nick Samac off waivers; Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell cleared and re-signed to the practice squad Kyle Van Noy signed to the practice squad for edge depth; Flores familiarity a plus, but 2025 PFF grades (63.0 overall, 51.8 pass rush) raise concerns Aaron Jones likely opens as RB1A over Jordan Mason due to superior pass catching and pass blocking; new wide-zone blocking scheme under Keith Carter and Frank Smith J.J. McCarthy could be QB3; his future depends on his development, Kyler Murray’s performance, and trade interest New GM Nolan Teasley is direct and concise — a sharp contrast to Kwesi Adofo-Mensah’s word salad ESPN Top 100 included only Justin Jefferson (10th); Andrew Van Ginkel and Brian O’Neill both snubbed Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Football is back, and the Vikings face the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium to open the season. Two Old Bloggers moves to Saturdays starting next week — so if you want deep-dive Vikings analysis with the numbers, the visuals, and the passion, make sure you’re subscribed. Fan With Us! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and the at the @BleavNetwork . title: 2026 NFL Week 1: Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings
summary: Ladies and gentlemen, we have officially made it to the start of the 2026 NFL season, and it’s going to get off to quite a start for our Minnesota Vikings as they play host to their biggest rivals. The Vikings will welcome the Green Bay Packers to U.S. Bank Stadium to kick off the regular […]
full_text: Ladies and gentlemen, we have officially made it to the start of the 2026 NFL season, and it’s going to get off to quite a start for our Minnesota Vikings as they play host to their biggest rivals. The Vikings will welcome the Green Bay Packers to U.S. Bank Stadium to kick off the regular season, and it will be featured across the country on CBS in the late window on Sunday afternoon. These two teams split their series last season. The Packers thumped the Vikings in Week 12 at Lambeau Field by a score of 23-6 as Micah Parsons single-handedly shredded the Minnesota offensive line, while the Vikings won the regular season finale at U.S. Bank Stadium, 16-3, as the Packers rested a bunch of their players as they had nothing to play for going into the postseason. Green Bay will come into this one without a couple of pretty significant pieces. Parsons, who tore an ACL late last season, is on the Physically Unable to Perform List for the Packers and will miss at least the first four games of this season, while running back Josh Jacobs is on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, fallout from a domestic violence incident from this offseason. The Vikings, once again, have another new face at quarterback to start the season, as Kyler Murray will take over as the starter for Kevin O’Connell’s team. He played just one drive in the preseason, but has apparently gotten very solid reviews in practice this offseason. We’ll see how well that transfers over to the field when things get real. The Vikings’ defense, which finished last season on a serious roll, will look to bring that momentum into this season. If the offense can back them up at a higher level than they did last season, this could be a big year in Minnesota. Kickoff for this one is scheduled for 3:25 PM Central time, with coverage being provided by CBS, which is WCCO-4 in the Twin Cities area. We will have all of our stories for this week’s game in this stream for you to access all in one place, so keep it right here for all of the latest news on this week’s contest. title: Instant grades for Christian Gonzalez contract extension with Patriots
summary: On Labor Day, the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez birthed a contract extension to make him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL. According to reports, the months-long process culminated on Monday in an agreement that will pay the 24-year-old $135 million over four years. We don’t know the full structure of the deal yet, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - DECEMBER 1: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to the game against the New York Giants at Gillette Stadium on December 1, 2025 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Labor Day, the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez birthed a contract extension to make him the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL. According to reports, the months-long process culminated on Monday in an agreement that will pay the 24-year-old $135 million over four years . We don’t know the full structure of the deal yet, but the fact that it got signed in the first place is telling. So, let’s put a grade it. Instant grades: Patriots sign CB Christian Gonzalez to 4-year, $135M extension Bernd Buchmasser: The signs always pointed toward Gonzalez and the Patriots ultimately reaching an agreement, but the timeline and eventual scope of the deal was where the uncertainty lied. It took a while for those questions to get resolved, but doing so before the start of the season is the best-case scenario even though it meant a massive investment on the team’s part. | Grade: A+ Andrew Guindon: This is a regime that’s emphasized retaining and rewarding its top talent, and that’s what the Patriots ultimately did with Gonzalez. Having a true premier shutdown cornerback on your roster, such as Gonzalez is a luxury in the NFL. Those are the types of players you pay while Drake Maye is still under his rookie contract. He showcased how impactful he can be in the biggest moments during last season’s Super Bowl, and now he’s under contract through 2031. | Grade: A+ Pat Lane: I don’t care how long it took, they locked up their CB1 and sent a message that they are going to reward guys for their play and commitment to the team. I don’t love the fact that Robert Kraft spoke about it to the media, because he opened the door on that, but the fact that they signed him, and had it just above Devon Witherspoon is fantastic. | Grade: A+ Matt St. Jean: There were some questions about how Christian Gonzalez might fit with Mike Vrabel’s scheme, but those were erased down to stretch as he embraced physicality and then showcased his premier coverage skills in the Super Bowl. Gonzalez is the kind of player who can take any opposing receiver out of the game and erase any chance for big plays in his area of the field. That’s highly valuable, and worth the price the Patriots paid. | Grade: A+ Dylan Klayman: Gonzalez as a top corner in the league deserved to be paid like it, especially after his standout performance throughout the playoffs. Locking him up before the season starts is huge, so it doesn’t create another distraction, and your CB1 can just go out there and play. Obviously, it would have been nice if there wasn’t a whole story in the media from Kraft about the contract, and Gonzalez’s camp getting mad about it. But at least it is in the rear view mirror now, and you have one of your best players signed for the foreseeable future. | Grade: A+ What do you think about the Gonzalez extension? Do you like it? Do you not? Please participate in our poll and head to the comment section to discuss with the rest of the community.
