title: Where can the Steelers rank top 10 in 2026?
summary: Top 10s have long been the standard of excellence when it comes to rankings, and in the 32-team NFL, it’s a signifier of being in the top third of the league — not unachievable or elite, but above average in a game where even the smallest of margins can make a massive difference. So, with […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Joey Porter Jr. #24 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Top 10s have long been the standard of excellence when it comes to rankings, and in the 32-team NFL, it’s a signifier of being in the top third of the league — not unachievable or elite, but above average in a game where even the smallest of margins can make a massive difference. So, with the Steelers’ regular season debut rapidly approaching this Sunday and predictions season starting to give way to actual football, let’s take a look at where Pittsburgh could rank among NFL teams in the four main yardage metrics: passing, running, pass defense, and run defense. They’re listed below based on how likely they are to land in the top 10 this season, from most to least. Pittsburgh didn’t finish as a top-10 team in any of these metrics in 2025. Could things change under a new coaching staff this year? 1. Run defense 2025 finish: 13th in NFL; 113.1 rushing yards allowed per game Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: This is a deep defensive line that features the ageless Cam Heyward and a bevy of run stuffers including Derrick Harmon, Yahya Black, Sebastian Joseph-Day and even impressive rookie Gabriel Rubio. Pittsburgh’s edge rusher room is better defending the run than many realize as well. The strong front should open things up for an athletic inside linebacker room that could finally live up to its potential in Patrick Graham’s aggressive scheme. And for the most part, the Steelers’ secondary isn’t afraid to tackle, with names such as DeShon Elliott, Jaquan Brisker and Jalen Ramsey all being known for laying out big hits in the box. Why they won’t: The range of the Steelers’ inside linebacker room is not a question, but communication and block-shedding issues have been a common theme of past seasons for Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson. Top backup Cole Holcomb still doesn’t look like the player he was pre-injury, either. The defensive line also isn’t without its question marks. Heyward still looked elite last year but is now firmly in his late 30s. And a lot of the optimism surrounding the group’s depth is banking on some sort of second-year leap from Harmon and Black, which isn’t a guarantee. 2. Pass defense 2025 finish: 29th in NFL. 243.9 passing yards allowed per game . Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Pittsburgh boasts one of the deepest cornerback rooms in the NFL with an excellent projected starting trio in Joey Porter Jr., Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean (Killer J’s, anyone?). Don’t forget Jaquan Brisker, either, a versatile safety who should be a big improvement over the list of veterans the team cycled through last year. Pair that revamped secondary with a modern Patrick Graham scheme and star-studded pass rush, and the Steelers’ passing defense has the pieces to take a big leap from its disappointing 2025. Why they won’t: Porter has barely practiced all summer and has hinted at a contract holdout. Ramsey will turn 32 this season. The starting secondary as a whole hasn’t been the most available this summer and could still be gelling come Week 1. The safety depth chart could once again sink the defense, with a lack of range across the board and DeShon Elliott starting the season on injured reserve. There are a surprising number of factors that could go wrong. 3. Running offense 2025 finish: 26th in NFL; 103.3 rushing yards per game Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle are both 1,000-yard season-capable runners who give the Steelers one of the most underrated one-two punches in the NFL. The Zach Frazier/Mason McCormick duo should also be a powerhouse in the run game, and new head coach Mike McCarthy’s more varied run scheme should give the team a more diverse ground attack that might better cater to some players’ strengths. Keep in mind that tight end Darnell Washington might be the best run blocker at his position in the NFL, as well. Why they won’t: Warren and Dowdle are good but not superstars, and if the offensive line fails to generate enough push up front like what happened in the preseason, the team’s running backs might not be able to create much yardage. Remember that the Steelers often needed to switch to a jumbo package or heavily use Washington last year to successfully run the ball, and the team will likely be using more 11 personnel in 2026. The right side of the Pittsburgh O-line doesn’t have a ton of power, and the group as a whole was built for Arthur Smith’s zone scheme, not a McCarthy system that uses more gap/power concepts. 4. Passing offense 2025: 22nd in NFL; 202.4 passing yards per game Why the Steelers will finish in the top 10: Aaron Rodgers’ arm is still remarkably strong even at age 42, and the Steelers revamped the team’s wide receiver room entering 2026 with the additions of veteran possession receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard. Despite a down 2025, WR1 DK Metcalf is still an explosive player and should see a boost in a modernized passing game under McCarthy. The same could be said of tight end Pat Freiermuth, who has been underused in past seasons but could finally break out under the coach who jumpstarted the careers of Jake Ferguson and Dalton Schultz. Don’t underrate Warren’s ability as a check-down target, either. Why they won’t: Rodgers had a historically fast time to throw last season, which shouldn’t change much in 2026 considering the team is still catering to his preferences, the offensive line remains a work in progress, and Rodgers is still in his 40s and not going to be running around extending plays like he used to. That quick passing game could lead to a strong completion percentage, but it also doesn’t do much to create big plays. And beyond Metcalf, the passing game is severely lacking in more options to gain chunk yardage. Do you think the Steelers will rank in the top 10 in any of the above categories in 2026? What other metrics could Pittsburgh rank especially high or low in? Join the BTSC community and let us know in the comments.

summary: The cornerback market rose again in the early morning hours Tuesday as the New England Patriots and star defensive back Christian Gonzalez agreed to a record-setting four-year, $135 million extension with $102 million guaranteed just ahead of the team’s season opener, insider Jordan Schultz reported. Gonzalez’s $33.75 million yearly average sets the new top mark […]

(Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The cornerback market rose again in the early morning hours Tuesday as the New England Patriots and star defensive back Christian Gonzalez agreed to a record-setting four-year, $135 million extension with $102 million guaranteed just ahead of the team’s season opener, insider Jordan Schultz reported. BREAKING: The #Patriots and All-Pro CB Christian Gonzalez have agreed to a 4-year, $135M extension with $102M guaranteed, per multiple sources. The deal, done by @WinSportsGroup , makes Gonzalez, who earned Pro Bowl honors last season, the NFL’s highest-paid CB in history. pic.twitter.com/gJF9WLNPDD — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 8, 2026 Gonzalez’s $33.75 million yearly average sets the new top mark for cornerbacks, just ahead of the $33 million average-per-year contract fellow 2023 draftee and Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon signed earlier this offseason. Now, only one big-name cornerback contract dispute from the 2023 draft remains: the Steelers and Joey Porter Jr.’s “ impasse .” Pittsburgh remains adamant in its policy of not negotiating with players during the regular season. And Porter hasn’t closed the door on sitting out games if he isn’t extended by Week 1. With the Steelers opening their season on Sunday, Sept. 13, the remaining window for an extension this offseason is rapidly shrinking — and the cornerback market keeps going up. Porter is entering the final year of his rookie contract. While it’s clear Porter wants to be paid like the high-end CB1 he established himself as last season, it remains to be seen if he’s hoping to reset the cornerback market himself or simply land a deal in the upper tier of his position group. It’s worth noting he’s represented by Win Sports Group, the same agency that negotiated the previously record-setting deals for Gonzalez and Witherspoon. As of Gonzalez’s extensions, six cornerbacks are now averaging $30 million or more yearly on their current contracts.

title: Steelers will not have season-long captains under Mike McCarthy
summary: Sunday will mark the official start of a new era of Pittsburgh Steelers football as Mike McCarthy will make his regular season debut as the head coach of the team he grew up rooting for. It will be the first time since 2007 that a new man will be in charge of the Steelers for […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 04: Cameron Heyward #97 and Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrate after defeating the Baltimore Ravens at Acrisure Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday will mark the official start of a new era of Pittsburgh Steelers football as Mike McCarthy will make his regular season debut as the head coach of the team he grew up rooting for. It will be the first time since 2007 that a new man will be in charge of the Steelers for their season opener. With that will come a number of changes to the way the team handles business. One of those things this season will be the way in which the team names captains. When asked about how the team would select captains in Monday’s press conference, McCarthy provided some details into the changes coming to that selection process this fall. “We’ll do the weekly captain format,” McCarthy told the media. “So, without getting ahead of myself here, when we get to that point in that week I’ll get that information to you.” Under former head coach Mike Tomlin, captains were named in the preseason and stayed the same throughout the duration of the season. Now, no single player will have the right to be a captain all season long. This is not an entirely new concept for McCarthy, as he took a similar approach to naming weekly captains during his time as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. Now, he brings a fresh captain-choosing philosophy to his hometown. Last season, Aaron Rodgers, Cam Heyward, and Miles Killebrew were named captains before the start of the season. After Killebrew suffered a season-ending injury, it was linebacker Payton Wilson who took over as the special teams captain. It would not be surprising to see veterans like Rodgers and Heyward earn the weekly captain title several times throughout the season, but now younger players will be incentivized for their efforts by potentially earning the title of weekly captain. summary: When the Pittsburgh Steelers selected Max Iheanachor 21st overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, the immediate question was how soon the young tackle would be thrust into the starting lineup. It seems as though Steelers fans will have to wait for the regular-season debut of their first-round draft pick, as Dylan Cook appears to be […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Dylan Cook #60 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to block TJ Parker #99 of the Buffalo Bills during the first half of a pre-season game at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Pittsburgh Steelers selected Max Iheanachor 21st overall in the 2026 NFL Draft, the immediate question was how soon the young tackle would be thrust into the starting lineup. It seems as though Steelers fans will have to wait for the regular-season debut of their first-round draft pick, as Dylan Cook appears to be slated to start at right tackle when the Steelers take the field against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. During his press conference on Monday, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy would not commit to naming a definitive starter at right tackle, but he offered some insight into what the team is thinking just days before their Week 1 matchup. McCarthy said that Cook has been taking “most of the reps” at right tackle as he has been all summer long. “We feel really good about Dylan,” McCarthy told the media when asked about cohesion among the five starting offensive linemen. Combine what McCarthy said about Cook taking most of the reps and a vote of confidence, and it’s reasonable to assume that it will be No. 60 getting the nod to start in Week 1. Later in his media availability, the Steelers head coach expressed how impressed he has been with Iheanachor when he has been healthy enough to play. “Make no mistake about it, he can play,” McCarthy said. Due to the injury that the rookie tackle suffered in camp, it seems that Iheanchor will have to wait to earn a spot in the starting lineup on Pittsburgh’s offensive line. It would be tough to throw the rookie tackle into the starting lineup right away after playing in just one preseason game, so this seems like the decision we have all been expecting. The Steelers offensive line will have new starters in Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson to begin 2026. After an up-and-down performance in the preseason, McCarthy is putting his faith in the offensive line to come together ahead of their season opener. Let us know what you think in the comments . Running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London are two of the better skill players in the league. Pittsburgh will look to apply pressure to Tua and force him to make difficult decisions against a defense expected to be aggressive under new DC Patrick Graham. full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Seattle Seahawks runs against Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots during the second quarter in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Less than 48 hours away from the start of the 2026 NFL season, the second domino in the cornerback market has fallen. The New England Patriots and All-Pro Christian Gonzalez have agreed to a 4-year, $135 million contract extension with $102 million in guarantees, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz on Monday night. BREAKING: The #Patriots and All-Pro CB Christian Gonzalez have agreed to a 4-year, $135M extension with $102M guaranteed, per multiple sources. The deal, done by @WinSportsGroup , makes Gonzalez, who earned Pro Bowl honors last season, the NFL’s highest-paid CB in history. pic.twitter.com/gJF9WLNPDD — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 8, 2026 After the Seattle Seahawks and Devon Witherspoon agreed to a four-year, $132 million ($101 million guaranteed) extension that made him the highest-paid cornerback in football , it was a matter of time until the Pats and Gonzalez followed suit and topped that figure — and despite some concern that a deal wouldn’t get done before the season opener , they now have come to an agreement. The extension comes over a month after Patriots owner Robert Kraft told media the team had offered Gonzalez a cornerback-record deal. Gonzalez held off on signing that contract offer, with the assumption being he was waiting out Seattle Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who was also in line to sign a mega-deal at the time. Both Witherspoon and Gonzalez have emerged as bona fide stars at the position since they were taken in the 2023 NFL Draft, with Witherspoon selected fifth overall and Gonzalez coming off the board at pick 17. Gonzalez, who missed most of his rookie season through injury, has gone on to be a Pro Bowler and earn a second-team All-Pro nod in 2024. Witherspoon, meanwhile, has been named a Pro Bowler in each of his three seasons and earned second-team All-Pro honors a year ago. Witherspoon’s tenure as the league’s highest-paid cornerback was short-lived, but with the All-Pro cemented in Seattle for the foreseeable future, that reality suits the Seahawks just fine. Any thought of Gonzalez holding out of the Seahawks game can also be put to rest. The two most expensive corners in the NFL will both be on the field come Sept. 9.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks’ first injury report of the season was far from promising , and left many wondering who will suit up at safety in the regular season opener against the New England Patriots on Wednesday. Unfortunately, Monday’s report didn’t do much to ease those concerns. Seahawks September 7 practice report Did not participate: S Ty Okada (hamstring) Limited participant: S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) WR Tory Horton (hamstring) OT Josh Jones (knee) Full participant: TE A.J. Barner (oblique) OG Anthony Bradford (knee) CB Julian Neal (quadricep) RB Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) With Emmanwori’s status against the Patriots up in the air, a second consecutive absence from Ty Okada is alarming to say the least. Alongside Bud Clark, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve just 0ver two weeks ago, Julian Love is now the lone healthy safety on the active roster. Despite the flurry of injuries, Seattle has four safeties on their practice squad (Maxen Hook, AJ Finley, D’Anthony Bell and Rodney Thomas II), should Emmanwori and/or Okada be sidelined in Week 1. The Seahawks are set to release their game designations on Tuesday. On the other side of the ball, Anthony Bradford was the only player whose status improved, going from a limited to full participant. As for second-year wideout Tory Horton, he remained limited while he continues to navigate through a hamstring injury. On August 21, head coach Mike Macdonald indicated Horton would be sidelined for “a period of time,” and although his return to practice bodes well for a quick return, it still doesn’t sound likely he’ll suit up on Wednesday. His offseason has been packed with injuries and as a result, missed parts of Organized Team Activities (OTA), numerous training camp practices, and the entire preseason. As for the Patriots, center Ben Brown (knee) was downgraded to out and running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was once again a non-participant. Although he hasn’t yet been ruled out, Henderson hasn’t practiced since hurting his ankle on August 24 and isn’t expected to play. However, Seattle’s trenches are set for a challenge as star defensive tackle Christian Barmore returned to practice as a full participant after being sidelined on Sunday with a knee injury.

title: Which trends will continue or change for the 49ers in 2026?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing to kick off the NFL season Thursday night in Australia against their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams. The teams split meetings last season, with the 49ers winning in SoFi Stadium and the Rams returning the favor with a convincing win at Levi’s Stadium. While both teams will […]
full_text: The San Francisco 49ers are preparing to kick off the NFL season Thursday night in Australia against their NFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Rams. The teams split meetings last season, with the 49ers winning in SoFi Stadium and the Rams returning the favor with a convincing win at Levi’s Stadium. While both teams will remain familiar, they won’t be the same in 2025, as both Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay will add new wrinkles to their offenses. With that in mind, let’s look at some statistical and personnel trends that should continue to change for the 2026 season. 49ers rushing success rate Christian McCaffrey was incredible in 2025. With a target rate of 23.5%, the running back was targeted more than CeeDee Lamb, Ladd McConkey, and Michael Pittman. So much of McCaffrey’s production comes from Shanahan’s ability to create space for McCaffrey and mismatches in the passing game. However, on the flip side, the 49ers ranked 16th in the NFL with a 42.4% success rate on rushing plays. Middle of the pack has never been where the 49ers offense sits, but there were multiple reasons for the down season on the ground. McCaffrey, in particular, ranked 37th in the NFL in EPA/rush with his 0.97 average yards before contact, coming in at 46th in the league. On outside zone runs, McCaffrey’s yards-before-contact number falls to 0.63. The 49ers finish 8th in the NFL in EPA/play because of the fifth-highest EPA/pass in the league at 0.12. This number has to go up, and if it does, the offense will be burning bright all season. 21 personnel groupings The 49ers, by far, lead the NFL in 21 personnel with a league-high 393 snaps from 21, which is a 36.32% rate. Only the Baltimore Ravens compete with the 49ers, with a 28.77 EPA out of 21 personnel, second to the 49ers’ 29.99 EPA. This trend is sure to continue while fullback Kyle Juszczyk is on the roster. The 49ers use the veteran fullback to identify coverages and to create lanes as a blocker in the running game. However, the 49ers finished tenth with an -0.02 EPA/rush from 21 personnel. The bump is from the 0.18 EPA/pass, and still the 49ers finished with the highest total EPA from 21 personnel. While the NFL is shifting to lighter backfields, the trend of McCaffrey and Juice on the field isn’t going anywhere. Interception rate Look, this may seem like cherry-picking or taking a simple idea and running with it, but 49ers quarterbacks finished 27th with an interception rate of 2.79%. Funny enough, the Seattle Seahawks had a higher interception rate at 3.12%, but when your defense is dominant and can bail you out, the difference is clear. The 49ers defense will improve from last year, simply because it’s almost impossible to be worse in certain metrics, but turning the football and putting pressure on this defense isn’t the optimal approach. We love when Brock Purdy takes calculated risks, but the biggest improvement needed in his game is limiting interceptions and turnovers overall. You don’t want to curb his playmaking, but living to play another down is definitely a place for Purdy to raise his game.

Bosa had the same black sleeve on his right knee that he wore last Wednesday, and he appeared to be adjusting it frequently.” Mike Evans downplays missing time: ‘None of my injuries were significant’ “The training staff, they did a great job working with me. I know I’m an older player. I’ve had probably over a thousand practices, football practices in my life now, so I know what I’m doing out there. They know what they’re doing. They did a good job taking care of me. None of my injuries were significant. If it was a game week, I wouldn’t have missed any time.” The newest 49er had a whirlwind trip to Australia. Now he’ll be needed in the opener (paywall) “As Kareem, 28, explained, his whirlwind journey actually began a few days earlier, on Aug. 31, when he was cut by the New York Giants. Two days later, the Falcons signed him to their practice squad, and one day after that, the 49ers came calling with a big request — drop everything and get to Australia. While the 49ers flew on a jumbo charter flight complete with 84 lie-flat seats, Kareem flew commercially — first to the Bay Area on Thursday morning to get a physical, and then on an 11:20 p.m. flight that night out of San Francisco. Whereas his new teammates had a day to adjust to the 17-hour time difference, Kareem landed Saturday morning and was whisked to his first 49ers practice. He said he felt surprisingly good despite the long flights. Though he didn’t have the extra-long, lie-flat seats that Trent Williams and Osa Odighizuwa enjoyed, the 49ers hooked him up with a lie-flat-ish seat on the United Airlines flight. “It was cool,” he said. “I don’t think I’d ever sat in one of those before. But being my size, it’s still a little too small. My feet were mashed up against the wall. So I was kind of tucked in the fetal position, trying to sleep.” He said the 49ers also gave him a plan for the flight — everything from how much he should drink to when he should sleep to how often he should put on a pair of blue-light glasses. “I had a little flight kit — melatonin and a hydration package just to help me sleep, so that when I got here, I could perform,” he said. “When I got here, it was a pretty smooth transition.” 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan takes comedy show to Australia with hilarious presser “When asked about how his team adjusted to the 15-hour flight and time difference, Shanahan relayed what he heard from some of his players. “Each guy’s different,” he said. “Some guys feel good and feel great, and then you talk to them five hours later, they’re like, ‘Never mind, that left.’ Some guys started off bad and then feel good later.” Shanahan was asked about the seating configuration on the plane that placed quarterback Brock Purdy behind center Jake Brendel. Was that a coincidence or by design? “They were doing snaps for 17 straight hours,” Shanahan deadpanned. “No, that was just luck.” Kawakami: 49ers 2026 season prediction — 12-5 and stronger for surviving all the travel (paywall) “You might’ve heard that the 49ers have big travel on both sides of this schedule, including three road trips in their last four games — at the Chargers on a Thursday night, at the Chiefs, and at Arizona, sandwiched around a home game against the Eagles. I’ll add that the Chargers and Cardinals are two short trips that shouldn’t be too draining, especially after the 49ers get seven Levi’s games and a bye from Week 2 through Week 14. If the 49ers aren’t going through another spate of injury hell, they should go at worst 2-2 in these games — and 3-1 or 4-0 are certainly in play. I think they have built up a decent enough core of young players, especially if this rookie class is as good as it’s looked in the preseason, to run through the tape. And I think Purdy is the kind of quarterback who is built for late runs. So I’ll guess that the 49ers lose to the Chargers but (with some extra rest) beat the Chiefs, Eagles, and Cardinals … and finish 12-5, probably with a good wild-card berth, just like last year. I think they’re better than last year, but the schedule is tougher, and though I shrug my shoulders at some of the complaining about the wear and tear of all this travel, I don’t think it’s nothing. A strong team, though, should hold up just fine through it. I think the 49ers are strong enough to compete with Seattle and the Rams and get into the postseason.”

title: Kyle Shanahan disappointed that NFL took away ‘home game in LA’ for Australia game
summary: When it was announced that the San Francisco 49ers were playing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, one of the biggest detractors was head coach Kyle Shanahan, who expressed his displeasure with the travel and setup. Having landed in Australia and now preparing for the Week 1 game this week, has his mind changed about […]
full_text: Oct 2, 2025; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) rushes for a touchdown San Francisco 49ers during the second half at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When it was announced that the San Francisco 49ers were playing the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, one of the biggest detractors was head coach Kyle Shanahan, who expressed his displeasure with the travel and setup. Having landed in Australia and now preparing for the Week 1 game this week, has his mind changed about the situation? “When I said that, that was nothing against Australia or anything,” Shanahan said on Sunday. “That’s just about competition and how important our 17 games are. It’s cool for us, just we always have an advantage of having one, I see it as one home game a year in L.A. Just the way our fans are and take over that stadium.” The 49ers do generally get that extra home game, forcing the Rams into silent counts at their own home stadium. So, there are certain years where San Francisco could get their nine original home games plus that extra game. This season, San Francisco has eight home games and nine road contests, with the Australia game counting as a road game. So, they won’t have an extra appearance at SoFi Stadium (although they do face the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi in December). But the 49ers fanbase does travel well, so Week 1 could be a similar environment anyway. “It was disappointing to let them off the hook and get them out of that,” Shanahan continued. “But, I have a feeling knowing how our fans roll, I have a feeling they won’t be much different here. I expect to have a good showing. I wouldn’t say it hit me right on the plane, but after being here for a couple of days, this is the right time to be here, it’s the right place to be, and it’s the right team to go against.” If there were a week for an international game, Week 1 is the most ideal, as teams can prepare for it beforehand, whereas they have to adjust on the fly in-season. That’s why the Rams approach is quite unique, as they’re essentially preparing like it’s in-season with their flights. After getting a few days to adjust, Shanahan is happy that the team went with their approach. “Not comparing us to them, but yeah I was glad. I know how I felt the last couple, two days. It’s a little different for a coach, toughing through how you use your mind for three-and-a-half hours, a little bit different than your body. But yeah, I’m glad that we’ve been out here because we feel real good today.” San Francisco and Los Angeles kick off on Friday morning local time, but the game will be aired on Netflix at 5:35 p.m. Pacific time on Thursday evening.

Quarterback Baker Mayfield, tackle Tristan Wirfs, wide receiver Chris Godwin, nose tackle Vita Vea, linebacker Alex Anzalone and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will wear the captain’s “C” this season. Krewe, meet your 2026 captains 👏 pic.twitter.com/1fE6d83JZV — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) September 7, 2026 Mayfield, Wirfs, Vea and Winfield return as captains from the 2025 team. Godwin returns to the role after previously serving as a captain in 2023, while Anzalone joins the leadership group in his first season with Tampa Bay after serving as a captain during each of his five seasons with the Detroit Lions. The changes come after two longtime Buccaneers captains departed during the offseason. Lavonte David retired after 14 seasons with Tampa Bay, while Mike Evans signed with the San Francisco 49ers in free agency. Tampa Bay opens the regular season Sunday on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium for Week 1.

title: Who will lead the Titans in receiving in Week 1?
summary: The Tennessee Titans will make their 2026 NFL season debut by hosting the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium in Week 1 this Sunday. There’s so much to learn about these new-look Titans. Head coach Robert Saleh and the team’s new coordinators Brian Daboll and Gus Bradley will officially make their debuts. The most important […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans will make their 2026 NFL season debut by hosting the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium in Week 1 this Sunday. There’s so much to learn about these new-look Titans. Head coach Robert Saleh and the team’s new coordinators Brian Daboll and Gus Bradley will officially make their debuts. The most important aspect of the Titans’ 2026 campaign is the development of sophomore quarterback Cam Ward. Coach Daboll is being tasked with overseeing his ascension. The Titans’ new-look passing game will finally be unveiled versus the Jets. This is a deep receiving core in Tennessee. Carnell Tate was drafted at fourth overall to grow alongside Ward. Wan’Dale Robinson was signed in free agency for his ability to be a high-volume, reliable weapon. Calvin Ridley is also back, and Elic Ayomanor had an excellent training camp. The Titans are four-deep at receiver. Who do you think will lead the Titans in receiving in Week 1? It’s an interesting question. Fans would love to see Tate explode after he failed to record a single preseason catch. Robinson should be Ward’s most reliable weapon, possibly leading the Titans in targets. Ridley is a big-play threat who once played in Daboll’s offense at Alabama. Running backs and tight ends should also be heavily involved in the Titans’ passing attack. Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, Gunnar Helm, and Daniel Bellinger will play notable roles in Daboll’s offense. Ward will be tasked with spreading the ball around to a plethora of players. The Titans should also establish the run via Pollard and Spears. This Titans-Jets rematch is littered with revenge storylines. From Saleh to John Franklin-Myers, Jacob Martin, Jermaine Johnson, Solomon Thomas, and Tony Adams, Tennessee is loaded with former Jets players. Who leads the Titans’ new-look passing attack in receiving is another question.

summary: The Daily Slop – 8 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 8 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links At long last… Week 1 is upon us 🙌 pic.twitter.com/QZ66mrMfWf — NFL (@NFL) September 7, 2026 Articles Sports Illustrated Albert Breer’s Takeaways: Where Every NFL Team Stands Heading Into the 2026 Season It’s really rare that a veteran coach such as Dan Quinn goes through the sort of on-the-fly wholesale philosophical change that the Commandersdid this offseason, and there’s no question it’s just different with more complex schemes coming in with new coordinators David Blough and Daronte Jones. Now the trick will be fitting some of the old standbys into the new way of doing things, and all eyes are going to be on quarterback Jayden Daniels in that regard . Losing Laremy Tunsil in camp—he won’t be back until at least January, and even that may be a longshot)—is a tough blow, and only underlines how his adjustment to Blough’s scheme has to chart the course back to the playoffs. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN NFL team previews 2026: Predictions, rankings, depth charts Commanders Biggest strength: Jayden Daniels. The third-year QB gives the Commanders a chance in every game and, as one AFC executive said, erases a lot of faults. Daniels has grown as a leader and in his comfort level running a new offense. He also has the strongest receiving corps he has played with in Washington this season. He also should have a stronger defense to help, giving him either more chances or better field position. Daniels just needs a line that can be solid. — John Keim This season is a success if … Daniels stays healthy and the defense produces with its addition of speed and athleticism. If all that happens, the Commanders have a chance for a strong rebound season. — Keim One key fantasy nugget: With a healthy Daniels, wide receiver Terry McLaurin is a solid bounce-back candidate this season. He averaged 11.4 points per game in 2025 but will be the WR1 in a Washington offense featuring more West Coast system routes. — Bowen Bold prediction for 2026: New safety Nick Cross will lead all safeties in tackles. Cross recorded an 89th percentile tackle rate (tackles per play) against the run among safeties last year, and 74th percentile against the pass. — Walder To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated 5 Questions That Will Define Commanders vs. Eagles in Week 1 Which Washington Receiver Becomes Philadelphia’s Third Problem? With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs as players the Eagles will obviously prioritize, that will leave a stack of guys who could get opportunities to step forward. That list includes Antonio Williams, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane, Dyami Brown, and Treylon Burks. Williams’ strong summer likely signals he’ll be someone to watch, although don’t be surprised to see Diggs move around to different spots, including the slot. The most hopeful outcome for Washington: Philadelphia’s secondary depth will be tested as someone outside the top two receivers steps up and makes them regret it. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Hogs Haven Mark Tyler breaks down Commanders defense & why it will be the backbone of the 2026 campaign More than half of the defense has completely turned over. Gone are Von Miller (who was once a great player in this league) and Jacob Martin. They are being replaced by uber-athletic edge rushers in Oweh and Chaisson. Dorance Armstrong, who was a starter last year before being injured, should slot into a rotational role along with rookie Joshua Josephs once he returns from his one-game suspension. The interior has been bolstered by the additions of Tim Settle and Charles Omehihu to go along with Payne and Kinlaw. Both are scheme/technique diverse and can be moved around the front five. Washington’s linebacker corps has been completely revamped. Styles takes over for the aging Bobby Wagner – who was a liability anywhere outside the A and B gaps and in coverage. He offers the ability to impact all three levels of this defense and will share green dot responsibilities with veteran Frankie Luvu. Speaking of Luvu, he came into camp in the best shape of his career and is looking to regain his 2024 form after being played out of position for the majority of 2025. Leo Chenal is the new free-agent addition, and his versatility and toughness against the run and as a situational pass rusher as a walked-up SAM will be a welcome addition to this defense. The Commanders defensive backs have taken on a completely new identity. Safety Nick Cross will be the leader of the secondary. His presence on the defense will force offensive coordinators to monitor his alignment on every play. Jeremy Reaves and Quan Martin (who had a very good training camp), will both see time in Jones’ three-safety looks and Tyler Owens seems to have carved out a role as a “position-less player” who can be deployed at all three levels. Sainristil and Robertson can move between the inside and outside with Douglas and Moreau adding the veteran presences until Trey Amos returns. At kickoff on Sunday afternoon in Philly, there could be up to eight new starters on this 2026 defense. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable Three offensive players I’m watching closely in Week 1 against the Eagles TE Chig Okonkwo The former Maryland product is known for creating yards after the catch and has an explosive athletic profile. Built like a wide receiver at 6’3″ and 238 pounds, Okonkwo may not have the precise route-running savvy of Ertz, but he should inject a different kind of vertical stress into the offense. In D.C., he will be playing with the best quarterback of his career. In Tennessee, his ceiling was capped by a revolving door of shaky quarterback play, and now he has a signal-caller with pinpoint accuracy who can lead him up the field. Okonkwo signed a three-year, $30M deal this offseason to bring some serious youth and explosiveness to our tight end room. The Commanders desperately lacked a true seam-buster last year, especially as Ertz battled injuries down the stretch. Enter Okonkwo, who is coming off career highs with 56 receptions for 560 yards. More importantly, the man is an absolute YAC monster: last season, he ranked 7th among all NFL tight ends in Yards After Catch per reception at 6.2 yards, according to Next Gen Stats. We haven’t seen Okonkwo much this offseason due to the team managing his health, but all signs point to a breakout season for the former Titan. Will this come to fruition, or did we all fall for Ashburn Syndrome? I want to see some heavy targets dialed up for Chig right out of the gate in Week 1. In Tennessee, he thrived on manufactured touches—designed bubble screens, motion out of the backfield, and flexing into the slot to isolate linebackers. If the Eagles try to pin their ears back and play aggressive coverage to slow down Terry McLaurin, Okonkwo should find plenty of green grass over the middle for quick, explosive catch-and-run opportunities. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Wire A strong reason for optimism in 2026 The Commanders’ ranking in passing yards last season has more to do with the injuries to Jayden Daniels and less to do with anything else, but having Diggs as a weapon along with Terry McLaurin, that makes this offense much more difficult to defend. Throw in rookie Antonio Williams and tight end Chig Okonkwo, and you’ve got yourself a pretty dynamic unit. If you’ve been paying attention, there are actually several reasons to be…

title: Washington Commanders at the Eagles in Week 1 – Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer, Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles safety Brandon Johnson (49) breaks up pass intended for Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks (13) at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer, Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: Things have changed a lot since June, when Bill-in-Bangkok wrote his preview of this week’s season opener against the defending NFC East champs in Philly. The loss of Laremy Tunsil turned up the heat on the Commanders’ 2026 season before it even started, while the absence of Nick Allegretti for most of training camp put the spotlight on Adam Peters’ decision, back in February, to move on from center Tyler Biadasz. A move to injured reserve with a designation to return for Trey Amos has shaken confidence in a secondary that struggled last season, but the addition of Stefon Diggs has been huge for the outlook of the Commanders’ offense. Sports writers have soured on the Commanders early, even as the coaches and players have reaffirmed their confidence in one another. Frascella’s 2026 NFC East Preseason Predictions: 4. Washington Commanders: 5-12 3. New York Giants: 6-11 2. Philadelphia Eagles: 10-7 1. Dallas Cowboys: 12-5 … what are your predictions? https://t.co/Lcn4kqZChe pic.twitter.com/svDyH7OniR — John Frascella (Football) (@NFLFrascella) September 4, 2026 The Washington Commanders have two new coordinators in David Blough and Daronte Jones. Blough hasn’t unveiled his new offense, but we know to expect the quarterback under center more, plenty of motion, and play-action. Penalties have been a concern discussed by head coach Dan Quinn throughout training camp. Daronte Jones has kept his defense under wraps, but occasional glimpses — like a six-man blitz versus Detroit — show a blitz-heavy scheme with disguised pressures and coverages. New Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is also installing an under center, motion-heavy offense, with a core philosophy of providing clarity for Jalen Hurts before the snap. That offense should be timing- and rhythm-based. The unique alignments and route concepts littered within this Sean Mannion offense is fun to study even this early on. He’s got RBs flexed out, WRs at the wing behind an OT, pony personnel (two RBs), on top of the pre-snap motion (orbit/return) that’s ingrained in his scheme… — Ryan Fowler (@_RyanFowler_) August 13, 2026 Eagles defensive coordinator, Vic Fangio, returns to run his two-high safety system designed to disguise coverages pre-snap behind disciplined front seven execution. There seems to be some thought among Eagles fans that, as a rookie defensive coordinator, Daronte Jones is a nice slow pitch start for Mannion, but Jones already appears to be one of the more competent coaches on Dan Quinn’s staff. The new offensive schemes in Philly and Washington represent significant shifts for the quarterbacks of both teams. Simply huddling the offense on a regular basis will be new for Jayden Daniels. Last season, the average NFL offense huddled about 82 percent of the time. With Daniels on the field, the Commanders huddled just about 32 percent of the time. So far, Jayden Daniels has looked sharp during training camp and practice with the word “surgical” being used a lot, but after taking an ugly three offensive snaps in the 2nd preseason game, Dan Quinn shut Jayden and the rest of the 1st-team offense down for the rest of that game and the final one in Baltimore. There is a lot to project, but with new offensive weapons, Daniels should be effective if the line can give him time to work. Jalen Hurts, on the other hand, has reportedly had a rocky transition so far, throwing numerous interceptions in training camp. Mannion’s offense tasks him with throwing in rhythm as a wide receiver comes out of his breaks, which does not appear to be a completely natural fit for Hurts. Mannion is expected to want to work the middle of the field where Jalen has little experience. If the Commanders can disrupt the timing of the Eagles’ passing attack, there should be an opportunity for the secondary to corral some interceptions. Quarterbacks Throwing Over the Middle since 2023 From the Stats & Scheme newsletter pic.twitter.com/KtTFwaEDag — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) September 4, 2026 Eagles Training Camp Day 16 Takeaways: Jalen Hurts has 13 interceptions in 16 practices this year Hurts had 15 interceptions the last four training camps combined Hurts and offense are turning it over way too much — and if it keeps up in the regular season they both will and… pic.twitter.com/DxqviQ5i5V — Eliot Shorr-Parks (@EliotShorrParks) August 26, 2026 The Commanders have invested heavily in edge talent, adding both Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson in the offseason. If both are healthy, they will lead the pass rushing attack for the Washington. Jones will be counting on the two edges to speed up Hurts’ clock and protect Washington’s secondary. The Eagles return Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis; the pair working against new Commanders starting center Nick Allegretti will be a matchup to watch. Not listed in Hog Haven’s summer preview, which was published in June (and which you can read below), is Philly’s trade acquisition of Dontayvion Wicks. First-round selection Makai Lemon suffered a hamstring injury during OTAs and experienced some setbacks, so it should be Wicks and Smith to start following the trade of A.J. Brown. Washington also added wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who will look to breakout in Washington’s remade offense versus Eagles free agent addition Riq Woolen. Both offensive coordinators prioritize three-down ability in their running backs, so we should see plenty of Saquon Barkley and Commanders’ free agent addition Rachaad White in the receiving game. This is a tough matchup for the Commanders to start their season, with the difficulty level ratcheted up on the road. The team’s best hope is the Eagles’ offense takes longer to gel than Washington’s defense. If the defense can contain the game early and allow Jayden Daniels time to settle in, he could provide enough game-changing plays to give his team the chance to walk away with an upset win in a divisional season opener on the road. title: Dan Quinn: Full participation in practice today; trending in right direction for Week 1
summary: Dan Quinn is back for his weekly “Tell the Truth Mondays” as the team begins their official Week 1 preparations. The season opener is in Philadelphia this year, and they’re visiting last season’s NFC East Champion Eagles, where the Commanders are big underdogs. That game will be followed up with another road division game against […]
full_text: Dan Quinn is back for his weekly “Tell the Truth Mondays” as the team begins their official Week 1 preparations. The season opener is in Philadelphia this year, and they’re visiting last season’s NFC East Champion Eagles, where the Commanders are big underdogs. That game will be followed up with another road division game against the Cowboys. In his press conference, Quinn said everyone participated in practice today, including OLB Odafe Oweh, who has been dealing with a calf injury. DQ stressed that today was only a walkthrough, but added that everyone is trending towards being available for Week 1. Quinn likes the energy he’s seen from the team so far, and also the leadership. He named five season-long captains, a change from the weekly captains he’s done the previous years. He will still name one additional captain weekly, but Jayden Daniels, Terry McLaurin, Frankie Luvu, Jeremy Reaves, and Tress Way are clear leaders in the locker room. Daniels only played one series in the preseason again, but Quinn insisted that he has gotten more reps in training camp and during joint practices that prepared him for his third season in the NFL. Training camp has been more intense than Quinn’s first two in Washington, another part of the plan to not have a repeat of last year’s disappointing 5-12 record. Roster Moves: We have made the following roster moves: – Signed WR Van Jefferson to the practice squad – Released TE Joshua Simon from the practice squad — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 7, 2026 Team Captains: This year: five season long captains + one weekly captain 🫡 pic.twitter.com/StBAxuKZ73 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 7, 2026 Leading the charge this season @NWFCU | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/WUxkoAL1kq — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 7, 2026 The #Commanders will have season long captains. Offense: Jayden Daniels & Terry McLaurin Defense: Frankie Luvu & Jeremy Reaves ST: Tress Way One game captain will be named on Friday's each week. — CWallSports (@cwallse) September 7, 2026 Just got done here with the team and it doesn’t get old, the starting the season vibes, the energy that comes with that and this group was certainly outstanding. I think it’s the leaders that make up the group which prompted me to do something that I haven’t done in a long time. Usually, we do Fridays and captains of the week and so this year prompted us as a team to vote for some season-long captains and then we’ll add one game captain on Friday. So, we announced that to the team today as well and so on offense it’ll be Jayden and Terry, on defense it’s Luvu and Reaves, and on special teams it’s Tress Way and man I’d follow these five guys anywhere. I thought what a great representation of the captains who we are and where we are. Just has a great vibe to it and excited to get rolling with 2026 with them and also get rolling with you guys so let’s get started and we can begin. Decision to have year-long captains: I think it was probably the team, there’s a lot of leaders here and that was probably the thing that prompted us to say, ‘Hey, this is probably the right time to add some guys to it and really be an extension, for the team’ And like, man, these are five really heavy hitters and leaders here. And it was nice to see some others. There are a lot of guys that got votes on this year’s team, and I think it kind of speaks to the trust that their teammates have in these five and the work that they’ve put in. So, for a guy like Jeremy just, he has been an absolute legitimate leader for a while. And so, to see that paid forward, I wasn’t surprised one bit. Same thing for Jayden to see all the stuff he went through and put the work in to know that, like, man, people see that. And all the work that he’s put in there, so all the joy Terry’s bringing. I could probably go on and on. But I think it was the group that, you know, said this is the right time to do this. Odafe Oweh at practice today: Dan Quinn said everybody, including Odafe Oweh, participated in practice today. Quinn added that everyone is trending in the right direction to be ready for Week 1 — Zach Selby (@ZachSelbyWC) September 7, 2026 Two first-time coordinators: I think there’s advantages for sure. As the season begins, there’s not a tendency, there’s not a ‘This is what he does on second down or third down, this is the scheme you know from years past. ’So those are the advantages. The disadvantages. Obviously, just going through some of the experiences, as you know, just from like training camp and going through games to try to simulate as much as you can for play callers. But there’s no getting around that. They’ve prepared, they’ve put the work in, and so, they’re ready to get rolling. But you’re right on the point that’s the challenge of it all. And so, we’re ready to get rolling. Team energy: Dan Quinn: "I like the energy of our team" — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) September 7, 2026 Jayden Daniels’ preparation for the season: Dan Quinn on Jayden Daniels' preparation: He took more reps than he ever has. I thought that was most important to get those hours in the bank with the new offense — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) September 7, 2026 He’s always somebody that’s been fit, but I would say, he took more reps than he ever has. I thought that was probably the most important part just to get those banked hours of the system. And you can do that at quarterback; it’s not at every play where you’re running down the field or going. That was by design, but I thought David was really on it in pushing him into that space. There were some practices he might’ve got twice as many as some others just for the reps, the communication, the calls. So, I thought that was really valuable. The conditioning part for him, there were some days where if you’re outside the pocket, you’re remaining a passer or other days where he can use his legs to run. The most taxing part, you didn’t want to overthrow. He’s a guy that throws a lot anyway, so some of those were runs and procedures to get through it. He’s banked a lot of hours in this system, so I thought, this is a guy that maxed out the offseason, the training camp to really get himself ready. His work ethic’s been something I’ve always admired, but to see it maybe just tic up again in term s of the readiness, to demonstrate that to his teammates, that’s a big deal. Team readiness: Yeah. What I try to do in training camp, I got some KPIs that I’m looking for in practice, you know, where are we on penalties? Where are we at on the speeds? Where are we on the execution or mental errors? So, I stay with that program through the camp, and then you wanna see, obviously, the numbers continuing to go up as the reps are going up. Can they stay in that same focus? Can they stay in that same spot? That demonstrates it some for me. And then coming back after the break, we put in four days of good practice prior to it. So, after you reduce down to the roster, add guys back. I wanted to see who was ready to really lock in on the details of it all. That’s what I was looking for. And then the first day of it today was kind of the same for me. I’m looking for absolute lock in the details of it and eliminating the mistakes. And when you do that, the practices are pretty sharp. They go quickly. So, it’s off to a good start today. full_text: The Commanders announced their team captains on Monday afternoon, but in a way that Dan Quinn hasn’t normally done. During his first two seasons at the helm, Quinn had announced captains each week, but, for 2026, he instead named captains for the season that were voted on by the players. DQ said he will still name one additionsl weekly captain for each game, but here are the guys who will lead the crew for the full season: Leading the charge this season @NWFCU | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/WUxkoAL1kq — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 7, 2026 The #Commanders will have season long captains. Offense: Jayden Daniels & Terry McLaurin Defense: Frankie Luvu & Jeremy Reaves ST: Tress Way One game captain will be named on Friday's each week. — CWallSports (@cwallse) September 7, 2026 Offense QB Jayden Daniels This one is obvious. Daniels has taken a step up in terms of leadership, with his knowledge of the offense reigning supreme. He has been instrumental in learning David Blough’s system and then teaching it to everyone else. Daniels isn’t getting the honor just because he’s the QB. He earned the gig. WR Terry McLaurin Anyone who has ever listened to Scary Terry speak will be aware that the dude knows his stuff. He’ll lead an improved group of skill players that includes Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo, Antonio Williams and more who should be much better than in years past. Defense LB Frankie Luvu I think, post-draft, we all expected Sonny Styles to run the show and for Leo Chenal to be the other strong voice in the linebacker room. Turns out it’s Luvu, a wild animal in his younger days who can still play like a feral dog. Luvu is smart and decisive and will make opponents hurt. Quinn made the smart call here. S Jeremy Reaves Jeremy Reaves was always a special teams player but has emerged as a defensive stalwart. Let him cook. That’ll let Quan Martin play more in the slot. Also, Reaves doesn’t tolerate bullshit. He tells it like it is. Special Teams P Tress Way One of the best punters in the game. Full Stop.

With an offseason at full health, Diggs is ready to hit the ground running as a key weapon for Jayden Daniels in Year 3. The QB-friendly WR should help. pic.twitter.com/FBrZnbsPxC — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 5, 2026 Everyone, from the multitude of content creators on social media to Major Tuddy, was overcome with jubilation. Even FOX Sports’ Skip Bayless was kind enough to chime in: The Washington Commanders now have the best WR corps in league. 😤 #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/UHkMJZpOTE — Chris Bryant (@HogfarmerChris) August 5, 2026 Must admit, Stefon Diggs is a smart signing for the Commanders. He will help Jayden Daniels just the way he benefited Drake Maye last season. Nice fit opposite Scary Terry. Not saying they're CeeDee and Pick, but who is? — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) August 5, 2026 Now that we can all sleep easy heading into the season knowing Terry McLaurin has his first real running mate since being drafted by Washington in the third round of the 2019 NFL Draft, the focus will shift to how David Blough will incorporate all of his new offensive toys on Sept. 13 versus the Eagles. Stefon Diggs compliments Terry McLaurin's skillset and is gonna make life a lot easier for Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/8ywXXStBi4 — Nick Penticoff (@NickPenticoff) August 5, 2026 With this new-found jubilation over the offensive weapons Daniels now has at his disposal and the hole that remains at center and to a lesser degree, left guard, all the focus seems to be on the offensive side of the ball. It’s easy to forget about the biggest area of improvement needed for this football team. DEFENSE! The stats below from the 2025 season are courtesy of Commanders Wire, written by my friend Ivan Lambert: Revealing some brutal statistics from Commanders’ 2025 defense “They were 32nd in most every statistic that matters, or at least bottom five in every defensive statistic that matters. Yards per play, yards per pass, EPA (Explosive Plays Allowed), etc.” “Dead last in yards per drive allowed, dead last in 3 & outs forced, 31st in turnovers per drive forced” “When teams reached the Red Zone, the Commanders defense allowed a touchdown 68 percent of those drives, which was second worst.” “They were the only defense in the NFL to allow over 35 percent of drives to reach the red zone and over 67 percent of those to score touchdowns. They were the only defense in the last five years to allow that combination.” “The defense allowed 101 points scored in the first quarter last year, which was the fifth most in the NFL.” “Therefore, they trailed by a combined 64 points after the first quarter last season, which was second worst in the NFL.” “The defense allowed opponents’ opening drives of games to average 49 yards, worst in the NFL last year. Even more, it was the worst of any Washington defense this century (26 seasons). It was the 13th worst of any defense this century.” “Of the 17 opening drives last season, the Commanders defense forced only three punts. It was the worst of any Washington defense this century, and the worst of any NFL defense this century.” These really are some BRUTAL stats to read! 2026 Defense Adam Peters and Dan Quinn were adamant about turning this defense around. When free agency opened, Peters aggressively attacked the defensive side of the ball signing the following players: Odafe Oweh (EDGE) K’Lavon Chaisson (EDGE) Leo Chenal (linebacker) Nick Cross (safety) Amik Robertson (corner) Tim Settle (DT) Charles Omenihu (DT/DE) All seven of these new additions made the 53-man roster and are expected to be starters or contribute heavily to the rotation. Peters would double-down in the 2026 NFL Draft where he used two of the team’s first three picks on defense: Sonny Styles (Round 1, pick 7) Joshua Josephs (Round 5, pick 147) Styles and Josephs are on the 53-man roster and both are expected to be significant contributors in 2026, with Styles as a starting inside linebacker and Josephs part of the two-deep at EDGE. After the draft, Adam signed veteran Rasul Douglas to add depth to the cornerback room. The 31-year-old corner started 13 games for the Dolphins in 2025, posting 13 passes defended and two interceptions. During training camp, when Trey Amos suffered an ankle sprain shortly after returning to action, Peters signed veteran Fabian Moreau for depth. Both Moreau and Douglas are in the 53-man roster and are expected to be contributors this season. A complete defensive turnover Washington’s 2025 roster after Thanksgiving EDGE: Von Miller DT: Daron Payne DT: Javon Kinlaw EDGE: Jacob Martin LB: Bobby Wagner LB: Frankie Luvu CB: Mike Sainristil CB: Jonathan Jones Slot CB: Noah Igbinoghene S : Will Harris/Jeremy Reaves S: Quan Martin Not only was this group old, but they were also slow and not at all in sync with one another, especially on the back end. The Commanders’ defensive line struggled to get off blocks and generate pressure. The linebackers were incapable of getting to outside runs and were a major liability in the passing game. The defensive backs were the worst statistical group in the league against the pass, and the number of missed tackles in run support was mind-blowing. To put it mildly, and backed up by Ivan’s stats above, this defense was a complete embarrassment. Fast Forward to Sept. 2026 More than half of the defense has completely turned over. Gone are Von Miller (who was once a great player in this league) and Jacob Martin. They are being replaced by uber-athletic edge rushers in Oweh and Chaisson. Dorance Armstrong, who was a starter last year before being injured, should slot into a rotational role along with rookie Joshua Josephs once he returns from his one-game suspension. The interior has been bolstered by the additions of Tim Settle and Charles Omehihu to go along with Payne and Kinlaw. Both are scheme/technique diverse and can be moved around the front five. Washington’s linebacker corps has been completely revamped. Styles takes over for the aging Bobby Wagner – who was a liability anywhere outside the A and B gaps and in coverage. He offers the ability to impact all three levels of this defense and will share green dot responsibilities with veteran Frankie Luvu. Speaking of Luvu, he came into camp in the best shape of his career and is looking to regain his 2024 form after being played out of position for the majority of 2025. Leo Chenal is the new free-agent addition, and his versatility and toughness against the run and as a situational pass rusher as a walked-up SAM will be a welcome addition to this defense. The Commanders defensive backs have taken on a completely new identity. Safety Nick Cross will be the leader of the secondary. His presence on the defense will force offensive coordinators to monitor his alignment on every play. Jeremy Reaves and Quan Martin (who had a very good training camp), will both see time in Jones’ three-safety looks and Tyler Owens seems to have carved out a role as a “position-less player” who can be deployed at all three levels. Sainristil and Robertson can move between the inside and outside with Douglas and Moreau adding the veteran presences until Trey Amos returns. At kickoff on Sunday afternoon in Philly, there could be up to eight new starters on this 2026 defense. That is what we call addition by subtraction! Scheme is king I have talked a lot about the players on this defense, but the biggest key to success this season may be the new scheme implemented by new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones. For those who aren’t familiar with Jones’ background,…

full_text: The Daily Slop – 7 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links this time next week you will be watching Commanders football 🙂‍↕️ pic.twitter.com/xlJNPvalLq — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 6, 2026 See you in 1 Sunday. pic.twitter.com/wh1XQQN5ay — Scott Hanson (@ScottHanson) September 6, 2026 Articles The Athletic (paywall) WTF is the Athletic talking about??? One question for each NFL team Washington Commanders: Who will make up the foundation in the next team build? The Commanders missed their opportunity to build a contender during Jayden Daniels’ rookie contract window. Daniels will be eligible for an extension next season and will likely reset the market. If he’s healthy, he can elevate this team as he did in his rookie season, but let’s be real, this isn’t a Super Bowl-worthy roster. [T]he Commanders should be identifying who they want to keep as building blocks for their next team build-out, and they will have to be more economical. To read more of this stupid article, CLICK HERE COMMANDERS COLLAPSE TALK GOES TOO FAR: National Panic Is Overblown Last Man Standig (paywall) Let’s talk about what’s right with the Commanders Daniels looked sharp. Get past the initial two camp practices when, per usual, the defense was a step ahead of the offense, and he cooked. Daniels’ accuracy was among the most consistent positives throughout camp, all while appearing increasingly comfortable within first-time coordinator David Blough’s offense. Daniels looked spry all summer, and there was nary a conversation over the offseason about lingering problems. We should also note his resilient, Gumby-like body when it comes to absorbing blows. Whatever else you think about the Commanders, their ceiling looks considerably different with No. 5 available. For more from Ben Standig, click here Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) How David Blough can help the Commanders run game In this post, we’re going to look at how Blough can help make things easier for the offensive line in the run game through various schematic tweaks. Running the ball effectively is one of the best ways to help mask any offensive line issues you may have, because it’s much easier for those lineman to work forward on run blocks than sit back and pass protect. But running the ball effectively isn’t always easy. The Commanders face some good interior defensive lineman early in the season and just calling a bunch of run plays on their own won’t work. Blough will have to have more up his sleeve. One of the first weapons he has in his arsenal is motion. Under Kliff Kingsbury, the Commanders opted against using much motion in order to get lined up quickly and be able to go up-tempo. But Blough is planning to slow things down a lot more, which opens up the ability to use more motion. Just using motion for the sake of using it adds nothing to an offense, but used correctly, it can really help out the offensive line. The Commanders are expected to transition to more of a zone-based run scheme this year under David Blough. @nick_akridge and I breaking down some film from the Commanders preseason game vs Miami to show some of the nuances of zone running pic.twitter.com/m2T5bmYigv — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 18, 2026 There's some questions surrounding the Commanders OL ahead of the new season, particularly at LG and C. So what can new OC David Blough do to help mask any OL issues in the run game? I took a closer look: https://t.co/JJ9DIjoBpy pic.twitter.com/J6cqoMsmio — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) September 7, 2026 Commanders Wire Commanders WR has one word to describe offense vs. Eagles in Week 1 When Abraham asked, “What is this offense going to be like?” Lane quickly responded, “Yeah, it’s going to be explosive! We got a lot of explosive guys on the field. And Blough and the rest of the offensive side, they’ve been putting us in great positions to use our explosiveness. So, expect an explosive offense. I’m excited.” I caught up with Commanders second year WR Jaylin Lane after today's practice. About the David Blough offense that will be unleashed against the Eagles, Jaylin told me, "it's going to be explosive…I'm excited." pic.twitter.com/L7s9Ax5ZBk — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) September 1, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Final commanders rookie power rankings: Who rose most before Week 1? 3. EDGE Joshua Josephs — Previous: No. 2 Joshua Josephs has been the most consistent rookie riser on the roster since the pads came out. While he did technically “fall” on this list, it shouldn’t be viewed negatively; Styles merely passed him. Josephs was able to capitalize on injuries to players above him on the depth chart . The extra field time he saw in camp, joint practice sessions, and the preseason led to what defensive coordinator Daronte Jones loves to see out of his guys: disruption. What’s wild about Josephs’ rise over the course of camp is the fact that Washington specifically targeted, and spent a good portion of cap space on that exact position room. After the draft, many wondered if he’d even make the team with Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson added to the mix and Dorance Armstrong returning from injury . That led to the August question: could Josephs force his way onto the team? Which, of course, after his play on the field, turned into: how many regular-season snaps will the team give him now? To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable How Washington’s rookies fared this offseason & preseason Matt Gulbin is the one who may have been most discussed among the Commanders’ fanbase where the rookie arrived as a center, though drew reps at guard before Quinn moved him back exclusively to center over the final week of training camp. The sixth round pick proved to be one of two offensive line rookies on the 53-man roster alongside Tanoa Togiai, yet Gulbin allowed just two hurries through the first two games to clearly outplay Julian Good-Jones to earn the backup center job. “I think over the course of the summer and over the course of training camp, we saw development in Matt,” Newmark said. “We saw growth in Matt and really excited with where he’s at currently and what we project him to develop into.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Bold NFL 2026 season predictions Washington Commanders: A rookie will star, but not the one most expect First-round linebacker Sonny Styles has given little reason to think he won’t have a solid rookie year with the Commanders. But third-round receiver Antonio Williams, an unheralded selection at No. 71, will be the team’s young breakout star of 2026. Williams, a 5-foot-11, 195-pound receiver out of Clemson, boasted a quiet confidence and a skill set that will make him a go-to target for Jayden Daniels and a key piece of the team’s future. Williams has the versatility to play inside and out, despite playing primarily in the slot in college. He also has the route-running polish of a veteran and a knack for making contested over-the-shoulder catches appear easy. Washington already has a third-round receiving gem in Terry McLaurin. Williams may be next. — Nicki Jhabvala To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Texas Longhorns WR Ryan Wingo should be on Commanders’ draft radar after dazzling Week 1 display Wingo finished with seven catches from eight targets for 121 receiving yards and one touchdown. While the standard he was facing wouldn’t exactly be classed as stellar, it was also a sign that the desired improvements have been made this offseason to become more influential. Simply put, this is a prospect the Commanders should be watching extremely closely from here on. Washington’s wide receiver room looks strong heading into the season.…
